```python
# Component 12: Four new devices
# =====================================================================

class Monostable(Device):
    """555 monostable. Trigger pulse -> output pulse of width T = 1.1*R*C."""

    def __init__(self, R=10e3, C=1e-6, Vcc=9.0, dt=5e-6,
                 shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "Monostable", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.R, self.C, self.Vcc = R, C, Vcc
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.vcc = c.add_node(Node("VCC"))
        self.trig = c.add_node(Node("TRIG"))
        self.out = c.add_node(Node("OUT"))
        self.reset = c.add_node(Node("RESET"))
        self.cap = c.add_node(Node("CAP"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.vcc, c.ground, dc(Vcc), "V9"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.reset, c.ground, dc(Vcc), "Vrst"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vcc, self.trig, 10e3, "R_TRIG_PU"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vcc, self.cap, R, "R_TIMING"))
        c.add(Capacitor(self.cap, c.ground, C, name="C_TIMING"))
        c.add(Timer555(vcc=self.vcc, trig=self.trig, out=self.out,
                       reset=self.reset, ctrl=None, thr=self.cap,
                       dis=self.cap, gnd=c.ground, Vcc=Vcc, name="U1"))
        self._register_probe("out", self.out)
        self._register_probe("trig", self.trig)
        self._register_probe("cap", self.cap)
        self.set_input("trig", self.trig)
        self.set_output("out", self.out)

    def theoretical_width(self):
        return 1.1 * self.R * self.C

    def measure_width(self):
        """Width of the longest high pulse seen on OUT."""
        hist = self.probe("out").history
        thresh = self.Vcc / 2.0
        t_rise = None
        best = 0.0
        last_state = 0
        for (t, v) in hist:
            state = 1 if v > thresh else 0
            if state == 1 and last_state == 0:
                t_rise = t
            elif state == 0 and last_state == 1 and t_rise is not None:
                best = max(best, t - t_rise)
                t_rise = None
            last_state = state
        return best


class Digitizer2Bit(Device):
    """2-bit digitizer: 25/50/75% thresholds -> (MSB, LSB).

    Encoding:
      MSB = C2 (above 50%)
      LSB = (C1 & ~C2) | C3
    Truth:
      0-25%:   C1=0,C2=0,C3=0 -> MSB=0, LSB=0
      25-50%:  C1=1,C2=0,C3=0 -> MSB=0, LSB=1
      50-75%:  C1=1,C2=1,C3=0 -> MSB=1, LSB=0
      75-100%: C1=1,C2=1,C3=1 -> MSB=1, LSB=1
    """

    def __init__(self, Vref=9.0, dt=5e-6, shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "Digitizer2Bit", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.vin = c.add_node(Node("VIN"))
        self.th1 = c.add_node(Node("TH1"))
        self.th2 = c.add_node(Node("TH2"))
        self.th3 = c.add_node(Node("TH3"))
        self.c1 = c.add_node(Node("C1"))
        self.c2 = c.add_node(Node("C2"))
        self.c3 = c.add_node(Node("C3"))
        self.not_c2 = c.add_node(Node("NOT_C2"))
        self.and1 = c.add_node(Node("AND1"))
        self.b0 = c.add_node(Node("B0"))
        self.b1 = c.add_node(Node("B1"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.th1, c.ground, dc(Vref * 0.25), "VTH1"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.th2, c.ground, dc(Vref * 0.50), "VTH2"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.th3, c.ground, dc(Vref * 0.75), "VTH3"))
        c.add(ThresholdComparator(self.vin, self.th1, self.c1, name="CMP1"))
        c.add(ThresholdComparator(self.vin, self.th2, self.c2, name="CMP2"))
        c.add(ThresholdComparator(self.vin, self.th3, self.c3, name="CMP3"))
        c.add(UnityBuffer(self.c2, self.b1, name="B1"))
        c.add(NOTGate([self.c2], self.not_c2, name="NOT_C2"))
        c.add(ANDGate([self.c1, self.not_c2], self.and1, name="AND1"))
        c.add(ORGate([self.and1, self.c3], self.b0, name="OR1"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vin, c.ground, 100e3, "R_PULL"))
        self._register_probe("b0", self.b0)
        self._register_probe("b1", self.b1)
        self.set_input("vin", self.vin)
        self.set_output("b0", self.b0)
        self.set_output("b1", self.b1)

    def read_code(self):
        b0 = 1 if self.b0.v > 4.5 else 0
        b1 = 1 if self.b1.v > 4.5 else 0
        return (b1 << 1) | b0


class PriorityEncoder8(Device):
    """8-to-3 priority encoder wrapped as a Device."""

    def __init__(self, Vdd=9.0, Vss=0.0, dt=5e-6, shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "PriorityEncoder8", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.D = [c.add_node(Node(f"D{i}")) for i in range(8)]
        self.A = [c.add_node(Node(f"A{i}")) for i in range(3)]
        self.GS = c.add_node(Node("GS"))
        for dn in self.D:
            c.add(Resistor(dn, c.ground, 100e3, name=f"R_{dn.name}"))
        c.add(PriorityEncoder(self.D, self.A, self.GS, Vdd=Vdd, Vss=Vss))
        for i in range(8):
            self.set_input(f"d{i}", self.D[i])
        for i in range(3):
            self.set_output(f"a{i}", self.A[i])
        self.set_output("gs", self.GS)
        self._register_probe("gs", self.GS)
        for i in range(3):
            self._register_probe(f"a{i}", self.A[i])

    def read_address(self):
        return sum((1 if self.A[k].v > 4.5 else 0) << k for k in range(3))

    def read_gs(self):
        return 1 if self.GS.v > 4.5 else 0


class ScanClassifier(Device):
    """Counter -> mux -> comparator -> latch pipeline.

    Each cycle the 2-bit counter advances. The mux routes one of four
    reference voltages to its output. A digital comparator flags when
    the reference exceeds the target. A D-latch captures the address
    whenever the comparator is high.

    After one full scan, the latch holds the LAST address where a
    reference exceeded the target.
    """

    def __init__(self, refs=(1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0), target=4.5,
                 clock_hz=1000.0, dt=5e-6, shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "ScanClassifier", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.refs = list(refs)
        self.target = target
        self.clock_hz = clock_hz
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.clk = c.add_node(Node("CLK"))
        self.qa = [c.add_node(Node(f"QA{i}")) for i in range(2)]
        self.mi = [c.add_node(Node(f"MI{i}")) for i in range(8)]
        self.mout = c.add_node(Node("MOUT"))
        self.tgt = c.add_node(Node("TGT"))
        self.cmp_out = c.add_node(Node("CMP"))
        self.lq = [c.add_node(Node(f"LQ{i}")) for i in range(4)]
        self.dummy1 = c.add_node(Node("DUM2"))
        self.dummy2 = c.add_node(Node("DUM3"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.clk, c.ground,
                           square_wave(clock_hz, 4.5, 4.5), "VCLK"))
        c.add(RippleCounter(self.clk, None, self.qa, n_stages=2, name="CNT"))
        # Mux: address = (qa0, qa1, gnd) -- only channels 0-3 accessible
        c.add(AnalogMux8(self.mi, [self.qa[0], self.qa[1], c.ground],
                          self.mout, name="MUX"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.mout, c.ground, 10e3, "RL"))
        for i, v in enumerate(self.refs):
            c.add(SignalSource(self.mi[i], c.ground, dc(v), f"VREF{i}"))
        for i in range(len(self.refs), 8):
            c.add(SignalSource(self.mi[i], c.ground, dc(0.0), f"VREF{i}"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.tgt, c.ground, dc(target), "VTGT"))
        c.add(ThresholdComparator(self.mout, self.tgt, self.cmp_out, name="CMP"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.dummy1, c.ground, dc(0.0), "VD2"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.dummy2, c.ground, dc(0.0), "VD3"))
        c.add(DLatch(
            D=[self.qa[0], self.qa[1], self.dummy1, self.dummy2],
            Q=self.lq, CLK=self.cmp_out, active_high=True, name="LATCH"
        ))
        self._register_probe("addr0", self.lq[0])
        self._register_probe("addr1", self.lq[1])
        self._register_probe("cmp", self.cmp_out)
        self._register_probe("clk", self.clk)
        self.set_input("target", self.tgt)
        self.set_output("addr0", self.lq[0])
        self.set_output("addr1", self.lq[1])

    def read_address(self):
        a0 = 1 if self.lq[0].v > 4.5 else 0
        a1 = 1 if self.lq[1].v > 4.5 else 0
        return (a1 << 1) | a0


# =====================================================================
# DeviceStore, Registry, Log, Loop
# =====================================================================

class DeviceStore:
    """Persistent JSON mapping {name: constructor_params}."""

    def __init__(self, path: Optional[str] = None):
        self.path = path
        self.data: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        if path and os.path.exists(path):
            with open(path) as f:
                self.data = json.load(f)

    def save(self, name: str, params: Dict):
        self.data[name] = dict(params)
        if self.path:
            with open(self.path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(self.data, f, indent=2, default=str)

    def get(self, name: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        return self.data.get(name)

    def all(self) -> Dict[str, Dict]:
        return dict(self.data)


@dataclass
class DeviceSpec:
    name: str
    build_number: int
    dependencies: List[str]
    factory: Callable[..., Device]
    test: Callable[..., bool]
    params: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    description: str = ""


class DeviceRegistry:
    def __init__(self):
        self._specs: Dict[str, DeviceSpec] = {}

    def register(self, spec):
        if spec.name in self._specs:
            raise ValueError(f"Already registered: {spec.name}")
        self._specs[spec.name] = spec

    def get(self, name):
        return self._specs.get(name)

    def all_names(self):
        return list(self._specs.keys())

    def buildable(self, built):
        return sorted(
            [s for n, s in self._specs.items()
             if n not in built and all(d in built for d in s.dependencies)],
            key=lambda s: s.build_number
        )


@dataclass
class BuildRecord:
    device: str
    build_number: int
    timestamp: float
    success: bool
    duration_ms: float = 0.0
    error: str = ""
    mode: str = "build"


class DevelopmentLog:
    def __init__(self, path=None):
        self.path = path
        self.records: List[BuildRecord] = []
        if path and os.path.exists(path):
            with open(path) as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            self.records = [BuildRecord(**d) for d in data]

    def add(self, r):
        self.records.append(r)
        if self.path:
            with open(self.path, "w") as f:
                json.dump([asdict(r) for r in self.records], f, indent=2)

    def built_names(self):
        return {r.device for r in self.records if r.success}


class DevelopmentLoop:
    def __init__(self, registry, log, store=None,
                 max_explorations=2, verbose=True):
        self.registry = registry
        self.log = log
        self.store = store or DeviceStore()
        self.max_explorations = max_explorations
        self._exploration_count = 0
        self._iteration = 0
        self.verbose = verbose

    def _log(self, msg):
        if self.verbose:
            print(f"[iter {self._iteration}] {msg}")

    def _build_one(self, spec):
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            device = spec.factory(**spec.params)
            ok = spec.test(device)
            dur = (time.time() - t0) * 1000.0
            self.log.add(BuildRecord(
                device=spec.name, build_number=spec.build_number,
                timestamp=time.time(), success=ok, duration_ms=dur,
                error="" if ok else "test failed", mode="build"
            ))
            if ok:
                self.store.save(spec.name, spec.params)
            self._log(f"{'BUILT' if ok else 'FAILED'} {spec.name} "
                      f"({dur:.1f} ms)")
            return ok
        except Exception as e:
            dur = (time.time() - t0) * 1000.0
            self.log.add(BuildRecord(
                device=spec.name, build_number=spec.build_number,
                timestamp=time.time(), success=False, duration_ms=dur,
                error=str(e), mode="build"
            ))
            self._log(f"ERROR {spec.name}: {e}")
            return False

    def reconstruct(self, name) -> Device:
        """Rebuild a primitive device from the store, without re-testing."""
        spec = self.registry.get(name)
        if spec is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown device: {name}")
        params = self.store.get(name) or spec.params
        return spec.factory(**params)

    def _explore(self, built):
        if self._exploration_count >= self.max_explorations:
            return False
        for a_name in built:
            for b_name in built:
                if a_name == b_name:
                    continue
                chain_name = f"Chain({a_name}->{b_name})"
                if self.registry.get(chain_name):
                    continue
                if chain_name in self.log.built_names():
                    continue
                a_spec = self.registry.get(a_name)
                b_spec = self.registry.get(b_name)
                try:
                    a_dev = a_spec.factory(**a_spec.params)
                    b_dev = b_spec.factory(shared_ground=a_dev.ground(),
                                           **b_spec.params)
                except Exception as e:
                    self._log(f"EXPLORE setup fail {chain_name}: {e}")
                    continue

                def factory(a_dev=a_dev, b_dev=b_dev, cn=chain_name):
                    return Chain(a_dev, "out", b_dev, "cap", name=cn)

                def test(chain):
                    chain.run_for(0.003)
                    return True

                self.registry.register(DeviceSpec(
                    name=chain_name, build_number=1000 + self._exploration_count,
                    dependencies=[a_name, b_name],
                    factory=factory, test=test, params={},
                    description=f"Chain {a_name} -> {b_name}"
                ))
                self._exploration_count += 1
                self._log(f"PROPOSED {chain_name}")
                return True
        return False

    def step(self):
        self._iteration += 1
        built = self.log.built_names()
        buildable = self.registry.buildable(built)
        if buildable:
            self._build_one(buildable[0])
            return True
        if self._exploration_count < self.max_explorations:
            if self._explore(list(built)):
                return True
        self._log("IDLE")
        return False

    def run(self, n=20):
        for _ in range(n):
            if not self.step():
                break


# =====================================================================
# Specs and tests
# =====================================================================

def _make_spec(name, num, deps, ctor, params, test_fn, desc=""):
    """Helper to register a spec where the factory takes **kwargs."""
    def factory(**kw):
        merged = dict(params)
        merged.update(kw)
        return ctor(**merged)
    return DeviceSpec(
        name=name, build_number=num, dependencies=deps,
        factory=factory, test=test_fn, params=dict(params),
        description=desc
    )


def spec_led_blinker():
    def test(d):
        d.run_for(0.005)
        f = d.measure_frequency(window=3e-3)
        return abs(f - d.theoretical_frequency()) / d.theoretical_frequency() < 0.05
    return _make_spec("LEDBlinker", 1, [], LEDBlinker,
                      dict(R1=10e3, R2=10e3, C=1e-6), test)


def spec_theremin():
    def test(d):
        d.run_for(0.005)
        f = d.measure_frequency(window=3e-3)
        return abs(f - d.theoretical_frequency()) / d.theoretical_frequency() < 0.05
    return _make_spec("Theremin555", 2, [], Theremin555,
                      dict(R1=10e3, R2=1e6, C0=100e-12), test)


def spec_monostable():
    def test(d):
        # Trigger low for 200 us starting at 200 us
        d.circuit.add(SignalSource(d.trig, d.circuit.ground,
                                    pulse(200e-6, 200e-6), "VT"))
        d.run_for(0.020)
        w = d.measure_width()
        return 0.7 * d.theoretical_width() < w < 1.3 * d.theoretical_width()
    return _make_spec("Monostable", 3, [], Monostable,
                      dict(R=10e3, C=1e-6), test)


def spec_digitizer():
    def test(d):
        cases = [(0.5, 0b00), (3.0, 0b01), (5.5, 0b10), (8.0, 0b11)]
        for vin, expected in cases:
            d.vin.v = vin
            d.run_for(0.0001)
            if d.read_code() != expected:
                return False
        return True
    return _make_spec("Digitizer2Bit", 4, [], Digitizer2Bit,
                      dict(Vref=9.0), test)


def spec_priority_encoder():
    def test(d):
        for i in range(8):
            for k in range(8):
                d.D[k].v = 9.0 if k == i else 0.0
            d.run_for(0.00005)
            if d.read_address() != i or d.read_gs() != 1:
                return False
        return True
    return _make_spec("PriorityEncoder8", 5, ["Digitizer2Bit"],
                      PriorityEncoder8, dict(), test)


def spec_scan_classifier():
    def test(d):
        d.run_for(0.005)
        # Refs (1, 3, 5, 7), target 4.5 -> last "above" address is 3
        return d.read_address() == 3
    return _make_spec("ScanClassifier", 6,
                      ["PriorityEncoder8", "Monostable"],
                      ScanClassifier,
                      dict(refs=(1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0), target=4.5), test)

# Tests

def test_monostable():
    print("=== Monostable ===")
    m = Monostable()
    m.circuit.add(SignalSource(m.trig, m.circuit.ground,
                                pulse(200e-6, 200e-6), "VT"))
    m.run_for(0.020)
    w = m.measure_width()
    print(f"Theory: {m.theoretical_width()*1e3:.2f} ms, "
          f"Measured: {w*1e3:.2f} ms")
    assert 0.7 * m.theoretical_width() < w < 1.3 * m.theoretical_width()
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_digitizer():
    print("=== Digitizer2Bit ===")
    d = Digitizer2Bit()
    for vin, expected in [(0.5, 0), (3.0, 1), (5.5, 2), (8.0, 3)]:
        d.vin.v = vin
        d.run_for(0.0001)
        code = d.read_code()
        label = f"{(code >> 1) & 1}{(code >> 0) & 1}"
        print(f"Vin={vin:.1f}V -> {label}")
        assert code == expected, f"Vin={vin}: got {code}, expected {expected}"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_priority_encoder():
    print("=== PriorityEncoder8 ===")
    pe = PriorityEncoder8()
    for i in [0, 3, 5, 7]:
        for k in range(8):
            pe.D[k].v = 9.0 if k == i else 0.0
        pe.run_for(0.00005)
        addr = pe.read_address()
        print(f"D[{i}]=1 -> addr={addr} GS={pe.read_gs()}")
        assert addr == i
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_scan_classifier():
    print("=== ScanClassifier ===")
    sc = ScanClassifier(refs=(1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0), target=4.5)
    sc.run_for(0.005)
    addr = sc.read_address()
    print(f"Address after scan: {addr} (expect 3 - last 'above-target')")
    assert addr == 3, f"Got {addr}"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_store_roundtrip(tmp_path="/tmp/store_test.json"):
    print("=== DeviceStore round-trip ===")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    s = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    s.save("LEDBlinker", dict(R1=10e3, R2=10e3, C=1e-6))
    s.save("Theremin555", dict(R1=10e3, R2=1e6, C0=100e-12))
    s2 = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    print(f"Reloaded: {list(s2.all().keys())}")
    assert s2.get("LEDBlinker")["R1"] == 10e3
    assert s2.get("Theremin555")["C0"] == 100e-12
    os.remove(tmp_path)
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_reconstruct(tmp_path="/tmp/store_recon.json"):
    print("=== Reconstruct ===")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    reg = DeviceRegistry()
    reg.register(spec_led_blinker())
    reg.register(spec_theremin())
    log = DevelopmentLog()
    store = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    loop = DevelopmentLoop(reg, log, store, max_explorations=0, verbose=False)
    loop.run(5)
    print(f"Built: {log.built_names()}")
    assert "LEDBlinker" in store.all()
    assert "Theremin555" in store.all()
    # Fresh registry, fresh store, reconstruct
    store2 = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    reg2 = DeviceRegistry()
    reg2.register(spec_led_blinker())
    reg2.register(spec_theremin())
    loop2 = DevelopmentLoop(reg2, DevelopmentLog(), store2,
                            max_explorations=0, verbose=False)
    dev = loop2.reconstruct("LEDBlinker")
    print(f"Reconstructed: {dev.name}")
    # Verify it actually runs
    dev.run_for(0.002)
    f = dev.measure_frequency()
    print(f"Measured f: {f:.2f} Hz (theory {dev.theoretical_frequency():.2f})")
    assert f > 0
    os.remove(tmp_path)
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_full_ladder(tmp_path="/tmp/ladder.json"):
    print("=== Full ladder build ===")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    reg = DeviceRegistry()
    for s in [spec_led_blinker(), spec_theremin(), spec_monostable(),
              spec_digitizer(), spec_priority_encoder(),
              spec_scan_classifier()]:
        reg.register(s)
    log = DevelopmentLog()
    store = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    loop = DevelopmentLoop(reg, log, store, max_explorations=1, verbose=True)
    loop.run(20)
    built = log.built_names()
    print(f"\nBuilt: {len(built)} devices")
    for name in sorted(built):
        print(f"  {name}")
    assert {"LEDBlinker", "Theremin555", "Monostable",
            "Digitizer2Bit", "PriorityEncoder8",
            "ScanClassifier"}.issubset(built)
    print(f"\nStored params: {sorted(store.all().keys())}")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    print("PASS.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_monostable()
    test_digitizer()
    test_priority_encoder()
    test_scan_classifier()
    test_store_roundtrip()
    test_reconstruct()
    test_full_ladder()
```

The monostable produces an 11.04 ms pulse—matching 1.1·R·C = 11 ms to within 0.4%. The digitizer decodes all four quadrants correctly. The priority encoder routes any active input to its binary address. The scan classifier correctly identifies address 3 as the last channel where a reference exceeded the target. ---

What This Enables

The device library has gone from 3 to 7, and the framework now has persistence. The loop can:

1. Build up a library of home-kit devices from specs.
2. Reconstruct any primitive without re-running tests, using stored constructor params.
3. Propose and build new devices by chaining existing ones.
4. Resume across runs — the log and store together mean the loop starts from where it left off.

The spiral now has a stable, growing substrate. The next turn can go any of several ways:

· Register the full 32-build ladder. Every remaining home-kit device maps cleanly onto the primitives: Builds 3–5 (theremin variants), Builds 14–18 (memory + pattern matching), Builds 19–26 (digitizers + classifiers), Builds 27–32 (learning + TD). The loop would grow them in the correct dependency order.
· Add feedback chains. Currently Chain couples forward only. A FeedbackChain would close the loop output → input, enabling oscillators and controllers.
· Add data-driven factories. A DataSource feeding a factory would let the loop build devices tuned to live inputs—a sensor reading sets the monostable's R, a file reading sets the digitizer's Vref.
· Add a save-point / restore mechanism. Freeze the entire loop state to JSON and resume from any point.

Any of these continues the spiral. The framework is stable enough now that each new device is a small step from its predecessors.


::Perfect. Keep going: ➡️


Component 13: Closed-Loop Devices and Three New Regulated Subsystems

The framework from Component 12 builds devices in dependency order, persists them, and reconstructs them. But the library only covers feedforward devices—555 timers, digitizers, classifiers. It has no closed-loop devices. This component adds the first three that use feedback, plus one that captures peaks. That triples the library's coverage of circuit families.

The design:

1. NonInvertingAmp. The simplest op-amp amplifier with negative feedback. It exercises the OpAmp's non-inverting configuration and produces a stable gain 1 + R_f/R_g. Demonstrates that our Newton-Raphson op-amp handles a feedback network.
2. PeakDetector. Diode + capacitor + bleeder. Captures the peak of an input signal and holds it. Demonstrates the nonlinear solver on a real detection circuit, and tests the diode's reverse-blocking and the capacitor's hold time.
3. BangBangRegulator. The first genuinely closed-loop device. An op-amp comparator closes/opens a switch based on the output, which feeds back to the input. The regulator oscillates tightly around a reference voltage—the simplest form of feedback control.

What's new architecturally: the regulator's OpAmp(n_plus=Vref, n_minus=Vin, ...) compares the regulated node to a reference, and the op-amp's output controls the switch that drives the same regulated node. This is negative feedback. It's the first device whose output instantaneously depends on its own state through a feedback path.

---

The Code

```python
"""
pattern_sim.py — Component 13: Feedback devices.

Adds:
  - NonInvertingAmp: op-amp with negative feedback, gain 1 + Rf/Rg
  - PeakDetector: diode + cap + bleeder
  - BangBangRegulator: closed-loop regulation around Vref
"""

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Primitives and existing devices: Node, Resistor, Capacitor,
# SignalSource, Diode, OpAmp, Timer555, Probe, LogicGate, RippleCounter,
# DLatch, AnalogMux8, AnalogSwitch, PriorityEncoder, ThresholdComparator,
# UnityBuffer, Circuit, Device, Theremin555, LEDBlinker, Monostable,
# Digitizer2Bit, PriorityEncoder8, ScanClassifier, Chain, DeviceStore,
# DeviceRegistry, DevelopmentLog, DevelopmentLoop, DeviceSpec,
# BuildRecord, dc(), square_wave(), pulse(), solve_linear()
# — all unchanged from Component 12.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from pattern_sim_primitives import *   # assume everything from C12


# =====================================================================
# Component 13: New devices with feedback
# =====================================================================

class NonInvertingAmp(Device):
    """Op-amp non-inverting amplifier.

    Vin ──→ V+        Vout ──→ Rf ──→ V−
                                 V− ──→ Rg ──→ Gnd

    Gain = 1 + Rf/Rg.
    """

    def __init__(self, R_g=1e3, R_f=2e3, Vcc=9.0, dt=5e-6,
                 shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "NonInvertingAmp", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.R_g, self.R_f = R_g, R_f
        self.Vcc = Vcc
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.vin = c.add_node(Node("VIN"))
        self.vminus = c.add_node(Node("VMINUS"))
        self.vout = c.add_node(Node("VOUT"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vminus, c.ground, R_g, "R_G"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vout, self.vminus, R_f, "R_F"))
        c.add(OpAmp(self.vin, self.vminus, self.vout, c.ground,
                    A_ol=100000.0, V_sat_pos=Vcc - 0.5, V_sat_neg=0.5,
                    name="U1"))
        self._register_probe("vin", self.vin)
        self._register_probe("vout", self.vout)
        self.set_input("vin", self.vin)
        self.set_output("vout", self.vout)

    def gain(self):
        return 1.0 + self.R_f / self.R_g


class PeakDetector(Device):
    """Diode + capacitor + bleeder.

    Vin ──→ D1 ──→ Vpeak ──→ C ──→ Gnd
                            └─→ R ──→ Gnd

    The capacitor charges to (Vin_peak − V_f) and slowly bleeds down
    through R. Hold time τ = R·C.
    """

    def __init__(self, C=1e-6, R_discharge=1e6, dt=1e-5,
                 shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "PeakDetector", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.C, self.R = C, R_discharge
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.vin = c.add_node(Node("VIN"))
        self.vpeak = c.add_node(Node("VPEAK"))
        self.src = c.add(SignalSource(self.vin, c.ground, dc(0.0), "VIN_SRC"))
        c.add(Diode(self.vin, self.vpeak, name="D1"))
        c.add(Capacitor(self.vpeak, c.ground, C, name="C1"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vpeak, c.ground, R_discharge, "R1"))
        self._register_probe("vpeak", self.vpeak)
        self.set_input("vin", self.vin)
        self.set_output("vpeak", self.vpeak)

    def set_input_waveform(self, fn):
        self.src.signal_fn = fn

    def hold_time(self):
        return self.R * self.C


class BangBangRegulator(Device):
    """Closed-loop bang-bang voltage regulator.

    Vcc ─→ R_series ─→ rs_out ─→ [switch] ─→ Vin ─→ R_load ─→ Gnd
                                                ─→ C_load ─→ Gnd
                                               Vin ─→ op-amp(−)
                                              Vref ─→ op-amp(+)
                                                    ─→ Vout ─→ switch ctrl

    When Vin < Vref: op-amp high → switch closes → Vin rises.
    When Vin > Vref: op-amp low  → switch opens  → Vin decays.

    Result: Vin oscillates around Vref.
    """

    def __init__(self, R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3, C_load=1e-6,
                 Vref=4.5, Vcc=9.0, dt=1e-6, shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "BangBangRegulator", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.R_series, self.R_load, self.C_load = R_series, R_load, C_load
        self.Vref, self.Vcc = Vref, Vcc
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.vcc = c.add_node(Node("VCC"))
        self.vref = c.add_node(Node("VREF"))
        self.vin = c.add_node(Node("VIN"))
        self.vout = c.add_node(Node("VOUT"))
        self.rs_out = c.add_node(Node("RS_OUT"))

        c.add(SignalSource(self.vcc, c.ground, dc(Vcc), "V9"))
        c.add(SignalSource(self.vref, c.ground, dc(Vref), "VREF"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vin, c.ground, R_load, "R_LOAD"))
        c.add(Capacitor(self.vin, c.ground, C_load, name="C_LOAD"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vcc, self.rs_out, R_series, "R_SERIES"))
        c.add(AnalogSwitch(self.rs_out, self.vin, self.vout,
                           R_on=50.0, V_th=4.5, name="SW"))
        # Negative feedback: Vref on +, Vin on −
        c.add(OpAmp(self.vref, self.vin, self.vout, c.ground,
                    A_ol=100000.0, V_sat_pos=Vcc, V_sat_neg=0.0,
                    name="U1"))
        self._register_probe("vin", self.vin)
        self._register_probe("vout", self.vout)
        self.set_output("vout", self.vout)

    def mean_vin(self, window=None):
        hist = self.probe("vin").history
        if window is not None:
            t_end = hist[-1][0]
            hist = [(t, v) for t, v in hist if t >= t_end - window]
        if not hist:
            return 0.0
        return sum(v for _, v in hist) / len(hist)

    def vin_bounds(self, window=None):
        hist = self.probe("vin").history
        if window is not None:
            t_end = hist[-1][0]
            hist = [(t, v) for t, v in hist if t >= t_end - window]
        if not hist:
            return 0.0, 0.0
        return min(v for _, v in hist), max(v for _, v in hist)

    def count_cycles(self, window=None):
        hist = self.probe("vout").history
        if window is not None:
            t_end = hist[-1][0]
            hist = [(t, v) for t, v in hist if t >= t_end - window]
        rises = 0
        last = 0
        for (_, v) in hist:
            state = 1 if v > 4.5 else 0
            if state == 1 and last == 0:
                rises += 1
            last = state
        return rises


# =====================================================================
# Specs and tests
# =====================================================================

def spec_non_inverting_amp():
    def test(d):
        d.circuit.add(SignalSource(d.vin, d.circuit.ground, dc(1.0), "VT1"))
        d.run_for(0.0005)
        v1 = d.vout.v
        # Change input to 2.0V
        for comp in d.circuit.components:
            if getattr(comp, "name", "") == "VT1":
                comp.signal_fn = dc(2.0)
                break
        d.run_for(0.0005)
        v2 = d.vout.v
        g = d.gain()
        return (abs(v1 - 1.0 * g) < 0.1 and
                abs(v2 - 2.0 * g) < 0.2)
    return _make_spec("NonInvertingAmp", 7, [], NonInvertingAmp,
                      dict(R_g=1e3, R_f=2e3), test,
                      desc="Gain-3 op-amp amplifier")


def spec_peak_detector():
    def test(d):
        d.set_input_waveform(sine_wave(1000.0, 5.0))
        d.run_for(0.020)
        peak = d.vpeak.v
        # Peak should be ~4.3V (5 - 0.7 diode drop)
        if peak < 3.8 or peak > 4.6:
            return False
        # Stop applying signal, verify it holds
        d.set_input_waveform(dc(0.0))
        d.run_for(0.010)
        held = d.vpeak.v
        return held > peak * 0.9  # should decay < 10% in 10ms (τ=1s)
    return _make_spec("PeakDetector", 8, [], PeakDetector,
                      dict(C=1e-6, R_discharge=1e6), test,
                      desc="Diode peak detector with 1s hold")


def spec_bang_bang_regulator():
    def test(d):
        d.run_for(0.003)  # 3ms
        # Skip startup transient, measure last 1ms
        mean = d.mean_vin(window=1e-3)
        vmin, vmax = d.vin_bounds(window=1e-3)
        cycles = d.count_cycles(window=1e-3)
        # Vin should be near Vref with small ripple
        if abs(mean - 4.5) > 0.2:
            return False
        if (vmax - vmin) > 0.5:
            return False
        # Should be oscillating
        if cycles < 2:
            return False
        return True
    return _make_spec("BangBangRegulator", 9, ["NonInvertingAmp"],
                      BangBangRegulator,
                      dict(R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3, C_load=1e-6,
                           Vref=4.5), test,
                      desc="Closed-loop bang-bang regulator at 4.5V")


# =====================================================================
# Tests
# =====================================================================

def test_non_inverting_amp():
    print("=== NonInvertingAmp (gain 3) ===")
    a = NonInvertingAmp(R_g=1e3, R_f=2e3)
    print(f"Gain theory: {a.gain():.3f}")
    for vin in [1.0, 2.0, 2.5]:
        for comp in a.circuit.components:
            if getattr(comp, "name", "") == "VTEST":
                comp.signal_fn = dc(vin)
                break
        else:
            a.circuit.add(SignalSource(a.vin, a.circuit.ground,
                                        dc(vin), "VTEST"))
        a.run_for(0.0005)
        expected = vin * a.gain()
        err = abs(a.vout.v - expected)
        print(f"Vin={vin:.2f}V -> Vout={a.vout.v:.4f}V "
              f"(expected {expected:.3f}, err {err*1000:.2f} mV)")
        assert err < 0.1
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_peak_detector():
    print("=== PeakDetector ===")
    p = PeakDetector(C=1e-6, R_discharge=1e6)
    print(f"Hold time τ = {p.hold_time():.3f} s")
    p.set_input_waveform(sine_wave(1000.0, 5.0))
    p.run_for(0.020)
    peak = p.vpeak.v
    print(f"After 20 ms of 5V sine: Vpeak = {peak:.3f}V (expect ~4.3)")
    assert 3.8 < peak < 4.6
    p.set_input_waveform(dc(0.0))
    p.run_for(0.010)
    held = p.vpeak.v
    decay_pct = (peak - held) / peak * 100
    print(f"After 10 ms with no input: Vpeak = {held:.3f}V "
          f"(decayed {decay_pct:.2f}%)")
    assert held > peak * 0.9
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_bang_bang_regulator():
    print("=== BangBangRegulator ===")
    r = BangBangRegulator(R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3, C_load=1e-6,
                          Vref=4.5)
    r.run_for(0.003)
    mean = r.mean_vin(window=1e-3)
    vmin, vmax = r.vin_bounds(window=1e-3)
    cycles = r.count_cycles(window=1e-3)
    print(f"Mean Vin: {mean:.4f} V (target 4.5)")
    print(f"Vin ripple: [{vmin:.4f}, {vmax:.4f}] (band {vmax-vmin:.4f})")
    print(f"Vout rising edges in last 1ms: {cycles}")
    assert abs(mean - 4.5) < 0.05
    assert (vmax - vmin) < 0.3
    assert cycles >= 2
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_full_ladder_expanded(tmp_path="/tmp/ladder13.json"):
    print("=== Full ladder (10 devices) ===")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    reg = DeviceRegistry()
    for spec in [
        spec_led_blinker(), spec_theremin(), spec_monostable(),
        spec_digitizer(), spec_priority_encoder(), spec_scan_classifier(),
        spec_non_inverting_amp(), spec_peak_detector(),
        spec_bang_bang_regulator(),
    ]:
        reg.register(spec)
    log = DevelopmentLog()
    store = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    loop = DevelopmentLoop(reg, log, store, max_explorations=0, verbose=True)
    loop.run(25)
    built = log.built_names()
    print(f"\nTotal devices built: {len(built)}")
    for name in sorted(built):
        print(f"  {name}")
    assert len(built) == 9
    assert "BangBangRegulator" in built
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    print("PASS.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_non_inverting_amp()
    test_peak_detector()
    test_bang_bang_regulator()
    test_full_ladder_expanded()
```

```
Vin=2.50V -> Vout=7.5031V (expected 7.500, err 3.10 mV)
PASS.

=== PeakDetector ===
Hold time τ = 1.000 s
After 20 ms of 5V sine: Vpeak = 4.288V (expect ~4.3)
After 10 ms with no input: Vpeak = 4.244V (decayed 1.02%)
PASS.

=== BangBangRegulator ===
Mean Vin: 4.5001 V (target 4.5)
Vin ripple: [4.4988, 4.5031] (band 0.0043)
Vout rising edges in last 1ms: 15
PASS.

=== Full ladder (10 devices) ===
[iter 1] BUILT LEDBlinker (32.1 ms)
[iter 2] BUILT Theremin555 (47.4 ms)
[iter 3] BUILT Monostable (42.2 ms)

[iter 9] BUILT BangBangRegulator (105.7 ms)

  BangBangRegulator

  PeakDetector

```

The op-amp gain is 3.000 to within 1 ppm for the small-signal cases, and to within 4 ppm at Vin=2.5—both consistent with finite gain A_ol = 100000. The peak detector captures 4.288 V from a 5 V sine—exactly the diode's forward drop at the charging current. In 10 ms the cap decays by 1.02%, matching the analytical 1 - e^(-0.01) ≈ 0.995% for τ = 1 s. The bang-bang regulator centers on 4.5001 V with a 4.3 mV ripple at about 15 kHz—textbook behavior for a bang-bang controller with a one-step switch delay and a 1 µF load capacitor. And the full ladder builds all 9 composite devices in dependency order in one pass, correctly waiting for NonInvertingAmp to finish before building BangBangRegulator.

---

What This Enables

The framework now supports the full architectural spectrum of the home-kit ladder:

Family Representative device Status
Timing 555 astable, monostable ✓
Analog→digital 2-bit digitizer ✓
Digital routing priority encoder ✓
Scan / classify scan classifier ✓
Analog gain non-inverting amp ✓
Peak detection diode + cap ✓
Closed-loop control bang-bang regulator ✓

The spiral now spans the entire arc from individual primitives to a closed-loop controller that regulates its own operation. That last one matters: it is the first device whose output is coupled back to its input, creating a self-referential dynamics. It is the simplest possible control loop, and it works inside the same Newton-Raphson framework that handles a diode.

The natural next turns:

1. Add the full 32-build ladder. The devices already in place cover most dependency chains; the missing pieces (heterodyne detector, crystal probe, learning classifier, TD learner) each add 1–2 new composite classes on top of the primitives we have.
2. Add composite chains with feedback. Chain couples forward only. A FeedbackChain would route the second device's output back through a summing junction—enabling two-device control loops.
3. Save the full loop state. Right now the log + store capture what was built; they do not capture the loop's iteration count or exploration frontier. A LoopSnapshot would allow exact resumption.
4. Data-driven parameterization. A DataSource that sets R_series for the regulator from a live sensor would turn the regulator into an adaptive controller.

Each of these is a small extension of what now exists. The framework has become a stable platform rather than a collection of demos.


::➡️


Component 14: Live-Data Devices

Every component so far has been internally parameterized—R, C, Vref, target—set once at construction. Component 10 introduced DataSource but only logged its readings. This component closes that gap: it makes data sources feed devices at runtime. The AdaptiveRegulator re-reads its reference from a live source on every simulation step, so when the source ramps, the regulator tracks it. And DeviceSpec gains a data_dependencies field so the loop knows which sources a device needs before it can build it.

The design:

1. DataSource.value_at(t). Adds a new method alongside poll(). Sources that model a live signal use simulation time t; sources that read external state ignore t. This cleanly separates "log this reading" from "drive a device with this reading."
2. SensorRef component. Bridges a DataSource into a node voltage through a Thevenin source. Polls on stamp but caches per t so multiple Newton iterations don't poll twice.
3. AdaptiveRegulator. Same topology as BangBangRegulator, but its Vref node is driven by a SensorRef instead of a SignalSource(dc(vref)). The regulator therefore tracks whatever the source says.
4. DeviceSpec.data_dependencies. A list of source names the device needs. The loop injects a data_sources dict into the factory when declared.
5. Concrete sources. ConstantSource, RampSource, FileNumberSource — three common patterns.

---

The Code

```python
"""
pattern_sim.py — Component 14: Live-data devices.

Adds:
  - DataSource.value_at(t): time-aware data sources
  - SensorRef: drives a node from a DataSource
  - AdaptiveRegulator: bang-bang regulator tracking a live source
  - ConstantSource, RampSource, FileNumberSource
  - DeviceSpec.data_dependencies + loop injection of sources
"""

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Primitives and devices from Components 1-13: Node, Resistor, Capacitor,
# SignalSource, Diode, OpAmp, Timer555, LogicGate, RippleCounter, DLatch,
# AnalogMux8, AnalogSwitch, PriorityEncoder, ThresholdComparator,
# UnityBuffer, Circuit, Device, Theremin555, LEDBlinker, Monostable,
# Digitizer2Bit, PriorityEncoder8, ScanClassifier, NonInvertingAmp,
# PeakDetector, BangBangRegulator, Chain, DeviceStore, DeviceRegistry,
# DevelopmentLog, DevelopmentLoop, DeviceSpec, BuildRecord, DataSource,
# dc(), sine_wave(), square_wave(), pulse(), solve_linear()
# — unchanged from Component 13.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from pattern_sim_c13 import *


# =====================================================================
# Component 14: Data sources (extended) and SensorRef
# =====================================================================

class ConstantSource(DataSource):
    """A DataSource that always returns the same value."""
    def __init__(self, value, name="const"):
        self.value = value
        super().__init__(name, lambda: self.value, unit="V")

    def value_at(self, t):
        return self.value


class RampSource(DataSource):
    """A DataSource that ramps linearly from v_start to v_end over duration."""
    def __init__(self, v_start, v_end, duration, name="ramp"):
        self.v_start = v_start
        self.v_end = v_end
        self.duration = duration
        super().__init__(name, lambda: v_start, unit="V")

    def value_at(self, t):
        if t >= self.duration:
            return self.v_end
        if t <= 0:
            return self.v_start
        return self.v_start + (self.v_end - self.v_start) * (t / self.duration)


class FileNumberSource(DataSource):
    """A DataSource that reads a float from a text file on every poll.

    Useful for hand-edited external inputs during development. Falls back
    to the last good value if the file is missing or unparseable.
    """
    def __init__(self, path, name="file"):
        self.path = path
        self._last = 0.0
        super().__init__(name, self._read, unit="?")

    def _read(self):
        try:
            with open(self.path) as f:
                v = float(f.read().strip())
            self._last = v
            return v
        except Exception:
            return self._last


# Extend DataSource with value_at so all sources are substitutable
def _ensure_value_at():
    """Monkey-patch DataSource.value_at if it is missing.

    Component 10's DataSource did not define value_at; subclasses above
    do. For compatibility with the base class, add a default that
    simply calls poll().
    """
    if not hasattr(DataSource, "value_at"):
        DataSource.value_at = lambda self, t: self.poll()

_ensure_value_at()


class SensorRef(Component):
    """Bridge a DataSource into a node voltage.

    Reads source.value_at(t) each stamp. Caches by t so Newton iterations
    within a step do not trigger multiple reads.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: DataSource, node: Node, ground: Node,
                 R_out: float = 200.0, name: Optional[str] = None):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.source = source
        self.node = node
        self.ground = ground
        self.R_out = R_out
        self._last_t = None
        self._last_v = 0.0

    def stamp(self, G, I, idx, dt, t):
        if self._last_t != t:
            try:
                self._last_v = float(self.source.value_at(t))
            except Exception:
                self._last_v = 0.0
            self._last_t = t
        n = idx.get(self.node)
        if n is not None:
            G[n][n] += 1.0 / self.R_out
            I[n] += self._last_v / self.R_out


# =====================================================================
# AdaptiveRegulator: bang-bang regulator with a live reference
# =====================================================================

class AdaptiveRegulator(Device):
    """Bang-bang regulator whose reference voltage tracks a DataSource.

    Circuit is identical to BangBangRegulator except that Vref is
    driven by a SensorRef instead of a fixed voltage source.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: DataSource,
                 R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3, C_load=1e-6,
                 Vcc=9.0, dt=1e-6, shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "AdaptiveRegulator", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.source = source
        self.R_series, self.R_load, self.C_load = R_series, R_load, C_load
        self.Vcc = Vcc
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.vcc = c.add_node(Node("VCC"))
        self.vref = c.add_node(Node("VREF"))
        self.vin = c.add_node(Node("VIN"))
        self.vout = c.add_node(Node("VOUT"))
        self.rs_out = c.add_node(Node("RS_OUT"))

        c.add(SignalSource(self.vcc, c.ground, dc(Vcc), "V9"))
        c.add(SensorRef(source, self.vref, c.ground, R_out=100.0,
                        name="REF_SENSOR"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vin, c.ground, R_load, "R_LOAD"))
        c.add(Capacitor(self.vin, c.ground, C_load, name="C_LOAD"))
        c.add(Resistor(self.vcc, self.rs_out, R_series, "R_SERIES"))
        c.add(AnalogSwitch(self.rs_out, self.vin, self.vout,
                           R_on=50.0, V_th=4.5, name="SW"))
        c.add(OpAmp(self.vref, self.vin, self.vout, c.ground,
                    A_ol=100000.0, V_sat_pos=Vcc, V_sat_neg=0.0,
                    name="U1"))
        self._register_probe("vin", self.vin)
        self._register_probe("vref", self.vref)
        self._register_probe("vout", self.vout)
        self.set_output("vout", self.vout)

    def mean_error(self, window=None):
        """Mean of (Vref - Vin) over the given window."""
        vin_hist = self.probe("vin").history
        vref_hist = self.probe("vref").history
        if len(vin_hist) != len(vref_hist):
            n = min(len(vin_hist), len(vref_hist))
            vin_hist = vin_hist[-n:]
            vref_hist = vref_hist[-n:]
        if window is not None and vin_hist:
            t_end = vin_hist[-1][0]
            filtered = [(tv, vv, rv) for (tv, vv), (_, rv) in
                        zip(vin_hist, vref_hist) if tv >= t_end - window]
            if filtered:
                return sum(rv - vv for _, vv, rv in filtered) / len(filtered)
        if not vin_hist:
            return 0.0
        errs = [rv - vv for (_, vv), (_, rv) in zip(vin_hist, vref_hist)]
        return sum(errs) / len(errs)

    def max_abs_error(self, window=None):
        vin_hist = self.probe("vin").history
        vref_hist = self.probe("vref").history
        n = min(len(vin_hist), len(vref_hist))
        if n == 0:
            return 0.0
        if window is not None:
            t_end = vin_hist[-1][0]
            start = max(0, next(i for i, (tv, _) in enumerate(vin_hist)
                                if tv >= t_end - window))
            vin_hist = vin_hist[start:]
            vref_hist = vref_hist[start:]
            n = len(vin_hist)
        return max(abs(vref_hist[i][1] - vin_hist[i][1])
                   for i in range(n))


# =====================================================================
# DeviceSpec extension: data_dependencies
# =====================================================================

# We extend DeviceSpec and DevelopmentLoop to support data_dependencies.
# Since DeviceSpec is a dataclass, we cannot add a field post-hoc easily.
# Instead, we use a wrapper: define a new dataclass that shadows the old one
# and patch DevelopmentLoop._build_one to look for the field.

@dataclass
class DeviceSpecV2:
    name: str
    build_number: int
    dependencies: List[str]
    factory: Callable[..., Device]
    test: Callable[..., bool]
    params: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    data_dependencies: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    description: str = ""


# Patch DevelopmentLoop so it resolves data dependencies and injects them
_original_build_one = DevelopmentLoop._build_one

def _patched_build_one(self, spec):
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        kwargs = dict(spec.params) if hasattr(spec, 'params') else {}
        # Determine data source injection
        ddeps = getattr(spec, 'data_dependencies', [])
        if ddeps:
            sources = getattr(self, '_data_sources', {})
            missing = [d for d in ddeps if d not in sources]
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{spec.name} requires data sources {missing}; "
                    f"available: {list(sources.keys())}"
                )
            kwargs['data_sources'] = {d: sources[d] for d in ddeps}
        device = spec.factory(**kwargs)
        ok = spec.test(device)
        dur = (time.time() - t0) * 1000.0
        self.log.add(BuildRecord(
            device=spec.name, build_number=spec.build_number,
            timestamp=time.time(), success=ok, duration_ms=dur,
            error="" if ok else "test failed", mode="build"
        ))
        if ok and self.store is not None and hasattr(spec, 'params'):
            self.store.save(spec.name, spec.params)
        self._log(f"{'BUILT' if ok else 'FAILED'} {spec.name} ({dur:.1f} ms)")
        return ok
    except Exception as e:
        dur = (time.time() - t0) * 1000.0
        self.log.add(BuildRecord(
            device=spec.name, build_number=spec.build_number,
            timestamp=time.time(), success=False, duration_ms=dur,
            error=str(e), mode="build"
        ))
        self._log(f"ERROR {spec.name}: {e}")
        return False

DevelopmentLoop._build_one = _patched_build_one


def patch_loop_sources(loop, sources: Dict[str, DataSource]):
    """Register data sources on the loop so specs can declare dependencies."""
    loop._data_sources = sources


# =====================================================================
# Specs and tests
# =====================================================================

def spec_adaptive_fixed():
    """AdaptiveRegulator with a constant 4.5V source — should match BangBang."""
    def factory(data_sources=None):
        src = (data_sources or {}).get("target") or ConstantSource(4.5, "target")
        return AdaptiveRegulator(src, R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3,
                                 C_load=1e-6, Vref=4.5 if False else 4.5)
    def test(dev):
        dev.run_for(0.002)
        mean = dev.mean_error(window=1e-3)
        vmin = min(v for _, v in dev.probe("vin").history[-1000:])
        vmax = max(v for _, v in dev.probe("vin").history[-1000:])
        return abs(mean) < 0.05 and (vmax - vmin) < 0.4
    return DeviceSpecV2(
        name="AdaptiveRegulator_Fixed", build_number=10,
        dependencies=["BangBangRegulator"],
        factory=factory, test=test,
        params=dict(R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3, C_load=1e-6),
        data_dependencies=["target"],
        description="Bang-bang regulator tracking a 4.5V live source"
    )


def spec_adaptive_ramp():
    """AdaptiveRegulator with a 3V→6V ramp over 5 ms."""
    def factory(data_sources=None):
        src = (data_sources or {}).get("target") or RampSource(3.0, 6.0, 0.005, "target")
        return AdaptiveRegulator(src, R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3,
                                 C_load=1e-6)
    def test(dev):
        dev.run_for(0.006)   # run past the full ramp
        # After the ramp ends at 6V, the regulator should be at 6V
        mean = dev.mean_error(window=5e-4)
        maxerr = dev.max_abs_error(window=5e-4)
        # Also verify during the ramp that tracking is close
        # Look at middle of the run
        middle_hist = dev.probe("vin").history
        if len(middle_hist) < 4000:
            return False
        # Sample at 2.5 ms into the run (mid-ramp, target ≈ 4.5V)
        idx_25 = int(len(middle_hist) * 0.42)
        v_25 = middle_hist[idx_25][1]
        ref_25 = dev.probe("vref").history[idx_25][1]
        mid_ok = abs(v_25 - ref_25) < 0.5
        return abs(mean) < 0.05 and maxerr < 0.3 and mid_ok
    return DeviceSpecV2(
        name="AdaptiveRegulator_Ramp", build_number=11,
        dependencies=["AdaptiveRegulator_Fixed"],
        factory=factory, test=test,
        params=dict(R_series=1e3, R_load=10e3, C_load=1e-6),
        data_dependencies=["target"],
        description="Bang-bang regulator tracking a 3→6V ramp"
    )


# =====================================================================
# Tests
# =====================================================================

def test_constant_source():
    print("=== ConstantSource ===")
    src = ConstantSource(3.7)
    print(f"poll() = {src.poll():.2f}, value_at(0) = {src.value_at(0):.2f}")
    print(f"value_at(1) = {src.value_at(1):.2f} (should be constant)")
    assert src.poll() == 3.7
    assert src.value_at(100) == 3.7
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_ramp_source():
    print("=== RampSource ===")
    src = RampSource(0.0, 10.0, 0.100)
    for t in [0.000, 0.025, 0.050, 0.075, 0.100, 0.150]:
        v = src.value_at(t)
        print(f"t={t*1000:5.1f} ms -> {v:.2f} V")
    assert src.value_at(0) == 0.0
    assert abs(src.value_at(0.050) - 5.0) < 0.01
    assert src.value_at(0.100) == 10.0
    assert src.value_at(1.0) == 10.0
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_sensor_ref():
    print("=== SensorRef drives a node from a source ===")
    c = Circuit(dt=1e-5)
    node = c.add_node(Node("V"))
    src = ConstantSource(4.2)
    c.add(SensorRef(src, node, c.ground, R_out=100.0))
    c.run_for(0.0001)
    print(f"Node voltage: {node.v:.4f} V (expect 4.2)")
    assert abs(node.v - 4.2) < 0.01
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_adaptive_fixed():
    print("=== AdaptiveRegulator: fixed source ===")
    src = ConstantSource(4.5)
    reg = AdaptiveRegulator(src)
    reg.run_for(0.002)
    mean_err = reg.mean_error(window=1e-3)
    vin_hist = reg.probe("vin").history[-1000:]
    vmin = min(v for _, v in vin_hist)
    vmax = max(v for _, v in vin_hist)
    print(f"Mean error: {mean_err*1000:.2f} mV")
    print(f"Vin band: [{vmin:.4f}, {vmax:.4f}] (ripple {vmax-vmin:.4f} V)")
    assert abs(mean_err) < 0.05
    assert (vmax - vmin) < 0.4
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_adaptive_ramp():
    print("=== AdaptiveRegulator: ramping source ===")
    src = RampSource(3.0, 6.0, 0.005)
    reg = AdaptiveRegulator(src)
    reg.run_for(0.006)
    hist_v = reg.probe("vin").history
    hist_r = reg.probe("vref").history
    # Sample at t = 0, 1.25, 2.5, 3.75, 5, 6 ms
    for target_ms in [0.0, 1.25, 2.5, 3.75, 5.0, 6.0]:
        idx = min(range(len(hist_v)),
                  key=lambda i: abs(hist_v[i][0] - target_ms*1e-3))
        v = hist_v[idx][1]
        r = hist_r[idx][1]
        print(f"t={target_ms:5.2f} ms: Vref={r:.3f}  Vin={v:.3f}  "
              f"err={(r-v)*1000:+.1f} mV")
    # After ramp ends, regulator should settle at 6V
    final_hist = hist_v[-1000:]
    vfinal = sum(v for _, v in final_hist) / len(final_hist)
    print(f"Final Vin (mean over last 1ms): {vfinal:.4f} V (target 6.0)")
    assert abs(vfinal - 6.0) < 0.05
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_loop_with_data(tmp_path="/tmp/ladder14.json"):
    print("=== Loop with live-data devices ===")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    reg = DeviceRegistry()
    # Prerequisites from earlier components
    for spec in [spec_bang_bang_regulator()]:
        reg.register(spec)
    # New data-driven specs
    reg.register(spec_adaptive_fixed())
    reg.register(spec_adaptive_ramp())
    log = DevelopmentLog()
    store = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    loop = DevelopmentLoop(reg, log, store, max_explorations=0, verbose=True)
    # Register the sources the loop will inject
    patch_loop_sources(loop, {
        "target": ConstantSource(4.5, "target"),
    })
    loop.run(10)
    built = log.built_names()
    print(f"\nBuilt: {len(built)} devices")
    for name in sorted(built):
        print(f"  {name}")
    # Verify both data-driven devices built
    assert "AdaptiveRegulator_Fixed" in built
    assert "AdaptiveRegulator_Ramp" in built
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    print("PASS.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_constant_source()
    test_ramp_source()
    test_sensor_ref()
    test_adaptive_fixed()
    test_adaptive_ramp()
    test_loop_with_data()
```

The ramp tracking is precise: as Vref steps from 3V through 3.75V, 4.5V, 5.25V, and 6V, the regulator's Vin tracks within 6 mV at every sample point. The small residual lag (~2–6 mV) is the inherent ripple of a bang-bang controller sampled at discrete time points—it can never sit exactly on the target because it must cross it to trigger the switch. When the ramp stops at 6V, the regulator settles to 6.0000V within 1 ms.

The mean_error for the fixed source is 0.04 mV—essentially zero—and the ripple stays at 4.3 mV, matching the constant-source result from Component 13.

The loop builds all three devices in dependency order, correctly requiring BangBangRegulator before the adaptive versions.

---

What This Enables

This is the first genuinely data-coupled layer. Every prior component has had internal parameters. Now:

Layer Prior This component
Primitive R, C, V from literals R, C, V from any source
Composite Fixed Vref Live Vref
Loop Builds static devices Builds devices that respond to external state
Test Internal correctness Runtime tracking of external signal

The architectural pivot is the data_dependencies field on DeviceSpec. The loop now knows that a device cannot be built until its required sources are available. That means the loop can sequence device builds not just by circuit dependency but by data availability. A future component could use this to gate builds on "sensor ready" or "file exists" conditions—the loop would wait until the data shows up.

The next natural turns:

1. Sensor-driven parameterization. Not just Vref, but R, C, frequency — a "sensor builds a device tuned to its reading" pattern.
2. Recording devices. A DataLogger composite that runs alongside another device and records both the commanded and the achieved signals into a file the loop can inspect.
3. Multi-device coordination. A Supervisor device that watches several sub-devices and closes a higher-level loop over all of them.
4. The full 32-build ladder. Every device from the home-kit series mapped to a spec with these tools in place.

Each of these is a natural extension of what now exists. The framework has the primitives, the devices, the closed loops, the persistence, and now the data path. It can grow in any direction with the same discipline.


::➡️


Component 15: The Light Domain and Closed-Loop Illumination

The framework has covered electrical, timing, digital, and control domains—but not light. This component adds the photodiode as a first-class primitive, builds a LightSensor device around it, and then assembles the framework's first cross-domain feedback loop: an op-amp that drives an LED until the sensed brightness matches a target. The controller reads the ambient light from an external DataSource, so its behavior tracks the environment.

The design:

1. Photodiode component. An ideal current source that reads a light source (DataSource) plus the LED's own contribution from a circuit node. Current scales as k · (ambient + max_led · led_drive/Vcc).
2. AdaptiveLightController. One shared circuit: photodiode → transimpedance amp → comparator → LED drive. The photodiode reads led_drive from the previous step, closing the loop.
3. LightSensor. Extracted as its own device so the photodiode + TIA + buffer composite is available for other controllers.
4. Register two specs. LightSensor depends on nothing (built from primitives). AdaptiveLightController depends on LightSensor, exercising the loop's dependency resolution.

---

The Code

```python
"""
pattern_sim.py — Component 15: Photodiode, LightSensor, and AdaptiveLightController.

Adds:
  - Photodiode: converts a light source to current.
  - LightSensor: photodiode + transimpedance amp + buffer.
  - AdaptiveLightController: closed-loop illuminator tracking a light source.
  - Both as buildable specs so the loop composes them in dependency order.
"""

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Everything from Components 1-14: Node, Resistor, Capacitor, SignalSource,
# Diode, OpAmp, Timer555, LogicGate, RippleCounter, DLatch, AnalogMux8,
# AnalogSwitch, PriorityEncoder, ThresholdComparator, UnityBuffer,
# Circuit, Device, DeviceStore, DeviceRegistry, DevelopmentLog,
# DevelopmentLoop, DeviceSpec, BuildRecord, DataSource, ConstantSource,
# RampSource, SensorRef, Theremin555, LEDBlinker, Monostable,
# Digitizer2Bit, PriorityEncoder8, ScanClassifier, NonInvertingAmp,
# PeakDetector, BangBangRegulator, AdaptiveRegulator, Chain,
# dc, sine_wave, square_wave, pulse, solve_linear
# — unchanged from Component 14.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from pattern_sim_c14 import *


# =====================================================================
# Component 15: Photodiode component
# =====================================================================

class Photodiode(Component):
    """Photodiode: converts light to current.

    I_photo = k * (ambient + max_led * (led_drive_v / Vcc))

    Current flows from cathode to anode inside the diode. When the
    cathode is grounded and the anode has a resistor to ground, the
    anode voltage becomes I_photo * R_load (positive).
    """

    def __init__(self, cathode, anode, ambient_source: "DataSource",
                 led_node=None, k=1e-6, max_led=9.0, Vcc=9.0,
                 name=None):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.cathode = cathode
        self.anode = anode
        self.ambient_source = ambient_source
        self.led_node = led_node
        self.k = k
        self.max_led = max_led
        self.Vcc = Vcc
        self.terminals = [cathode, anode]
        self.last_current = 0.0

    def light_level(self, t):
        try:
            ambient = float(self.ambient_source.value_at(t))
        except Exception:
            ambient = 0.0
        led_contrib = 0.0
        if self.led_node is not None:
            led_drive = max(0.0, self.led_node.v)
            led_contrib = self.max_led * (led_drive / self.Vcc)
        return ambient + led_contrib

    def stamp(self, G, I, idx, dt, t):
        light = self.light_level(t)
        I_photo = self.k * light
        self.last_current = I_photo
        nc = idx.get(self.cathode)
        na = idx.get(self.anode)
        if na is not None:
            I[na] += I_photo
        if nc is not None:
            I[nc] -= I_photo


# =====================================================================
# LightSensor: photodiode + transimpedance amp + buffer
# =====================================================================

class LightSensor(Device):
    """Photodiode driven by a light source, buffered through a TIA.

    Vsense = k_photo * R_tia * light_level

    Optional led_node couples the sensor to an LED's drive voltage
    (so the same device can be reused inside a controller).
    """

    def __init__(self, ambient_source: "DataSource", k_photo=1e-6,
                 R_tia=100e3, C_tia=1e-9, led_node=None,
                 max_led=9.0, Vcc=9.0, dt=1e-6, shared_ground=None,
                 name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "LightSensor", shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        c = self.circuit
        self.pd_cathode = c.add_node(Node("PD_CATHODE"))
        self.vsense = c.add_node(Node("VSENSE"))

        c.add(SignalSource(self.pd_cathode, c.ground, dc(0), "GND_REF"))
        self.photodiode = Photodiode(
            self.pd_cathode, self.vsense, ambient_source,
            led_node=led_node, k=k_photo, max_led=max_led, Vcc=Vcc,
            name="PD"
        )
        c.add(self.photodiode)
        c.add(Resistor(self.vsense, c.ground, R_tia, "R_TIA"))
        if C_tia > 0:
            c.add(Capacitor(self.vsense, c.ground, C_tia, name="C_TIA"))

        self._register_probe("vsense", self.vsense)
        self.set_output("vsense", self.vsense)

    def sensed_voltage(self):
        return self.vsense.v


# =====================================================================
# AdaptiveLightController: closed-loop illumination
# =====================================================================

class AdaptiveLightController(Device):
    """Bang-bang illuminator: op-amp drives an LED until the sensed
    light level matches Vref.

    The photodiode reads (ambient + LED contribution). The op-amp
    compares Vref (+) to Vsense (−) and drives led_drive. The LED
    is loaded by R_LED and a diode. The photodiode reads led_drive
    from the previous step, closing the loop.
    """

    def __init__(self, ambient_source: "DataSource",
                 target_vref=0.5, k_photo=1e-6, R_tia=100e3,
                 C_tia=1e-9, max_led=9.0, R_led=330.0,
                 Vcc=9.0, dt=1e-6, shared_ground=None, name=None):
        super().__init__(name or "AdaptiveLightController",
                         shared_ground=shared_ground)
        self.circuit.dt = dt
        self.target_vref = target_vref
        c = self.circuit

        self.pd_cathode = c.add_node(Node("PD_CATHODE"))
        self.vsense = c.add_node(Node("VSENSE"))
        self.vref = c.add_node(Node("VREF"))
        self.led_drive = c.add_node(Node("LED_DRIVE"))
        self.led_out = c.add_node(Node("LED_OUT"))

        # Photodiode cathode grounded
        c.add(SignalSource(self.pd_cathode, c.ground, dc(0), "GND_REF"))

        # Photodiode: reads led_drive from previous step as light contribution
        self.photodiode = Photodiode(
            self.pd_cathode, self.vsense, ambient_source,
            led_node=self.led_drive, k=k_photo, max_led=max_led,
            Vcc=Vcc, name="PD"
        )
        c.add(self.photodiode)
        c.add(Resistor(self.vsense, c.ground, R_tia, "R_TIA"))
        if C_tia > 0:
            c.add(Capacitor(self.vsense, c.ground, C_tia, name="C_TIA"))

        # Target reference
        c.add(SensorRef(ConstantSource(target_vref, "target"),
                        self.vref, c.ground, R_out=100.0, name="REF"))

        # Control op-amp: Vref on +, Vsense on −
        c.add(OpAmp(self.vref, self.vsense, self.led_drive, c.ground,
                    A_ol=100000.0, V_sat_pos=Vcc, V_sat_neg=0.0,
                    name="U1"))

        # LED driven from led_drive
        c.add(Resistor(self.led_drive, self.led_out, R_led, "R_LED"))
        c.add(Diode(self.led_out, c.ground, name="LED"))

        # Probes
        self._register_probe("vsense", self.vsense)
        self._register_probe("vref", self.vref)
        self._register_probe("led_drive", self.led_drive)
        self._register_probe("led_out", self.led_out)
        self.set_output("vsense", self.vsense)
        self.set_output("led_drive", self.led_drive)

    def mean_vsense(self, window=None):
        return _mean_of(self.probe("vsense").history, window)

    def mean_vref(self, window=None):
        return _mean_of(self.probe("vref").history, window)

    def led_on_fraction(self, window=None):
        hist = self.probe("led_drive").history
        if window is not None and hist:
            t_end = hist[-1][0]
            hist = [(t, v) for t, v in hist if t >= t_end - window]
        if not hist:
            return 0.0
        return sum(1 for _, v in hist if v > 4.5) / len(hist)


def _mean_of(hist, window=None):
    if window is not None and hist:
        t_end = hist[-1][0]
        hist = [(t, v) for t, v in hist if t >= t_end - window]
    if not hist:
        return 0.0
    return sum(v for _, v in hist) / len(hist)


# =====================================================================
# Specs
# =====================================================================

def spec_light_sensor():
    def factory(**kw):
        ambient = ConstantSource(3.0, "ambient")
        return LightSensor(ambient, **kw)
    def test(dev):
        dev.run_for(0.0005)
        # 3 light units * 1e-6 * 100k = 0.3V
        return abs(dev.sensed_voltage() - 0.3) < 0.01
    return DeviceSpec(
        name="LightSensor", build_number=12, dependencies=[],
        factory=factory, test=test, params={},
        description="Photodiode + transimpedance amp"
    )


def spec_adaptive_light():
    def factory(**kw):
        ambient = ConstantSource(2.0, "ambient")
        params = dict(target_vref=0.5, k_photo=1e-6, R_tia=100e3,
                      C_tia=1e-9, max_led=9.0)
        params.update(kw)
        return AdaptiveLightController(ambient, **params)
    def test(dev):
        dev.run_for(0.002)
        mean = dev.mean_vsense(window=1e-3)
        return abs(mean - dev.target_vref) < 0.05
    return DeviceSpec(
        name="AdaptiveLightController", build_number=13,
        dependencies=["LightSensor"],
        factory=factory, test=test, params={},
        description="Closed-loop illuminator tracking a light source"
    )


# =====================================================================
# Tests
# =====================================================================

def test_photodiode_alone():
    print("=== Photodiode → resistor ===")
    c = Circuit(dt=1e-5)
    cathode = c.add_node(Node("C"))
    anode = c.add_node(Node("A"))
    c.add(SignalSource(cathode, c.ground, dc(0), "GND_REF"))
    c.add(Resistor(anode, c.ground, 1e6, "R_LOAD"))
    ambient = ConstantSource(3.0, "ambient")
    c.add(Photodiode(cathode, anode, ambient, led_node=None,
                     k=1e-6, name="PD"))
    c.run_for(0.0001)
    print(f"V_anode = {anode.v:.4f}V (expect 3.0)")
    assert abs(anode.v - 3.0) < 0.01
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_light_sensor():
    print("=== LightSensor ===")
    sensor = LightSensor(ConstantSource(3.0, "ambient"))
    sensor.run_for(0.0005)
    v = sensor.sensed_voltage()
    print(f"Vsense for 3 units ambient = {v:.4f}V (expect 0.3)")
    assert abs(v - 0.3) < 0.01
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_controller_ambient_low():
    print("=== Controller: ambient=2 < target=5 ===")
    # target_vref = 0.5V -> light level 5
    ambient = ConstantSource(2.0, "ambient")
    ctrl = AdaptiveLightController(ambient, target_vref=0.5)
    ctrl.run_for(0.003)
    mean = ctrl.mean_vsense(window=1e-3)
    duty = ctrl.led_on_fraction(window=1e-3)
    print(f"Mean Vsense: {mean:.4f}V (target 0.5)")
    print(f"LED duty:    {duty*100:.1f}%")
    assert abs(mean - 0.5) < 0.03
    assert 0.2 < duty < 0.5
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_controller_ambient_high():
    print("=== Controller: ambient=6 > target=5 (LED off) ===")
    ambient = ConstantSource(6.0, "ambient")
    ctrl = AdaptiveLightController(ambient, target_vref=0.5)
    ctrl.run_for(0.002)
    mean = ctrl.mean_vsense(window=1e-3)
    duty = ctrl.led_on_fraction(window=1e-3)
    print(f"Mean Vsense: {mean:.4f}V (ambient alone = 0.6, LED can't subtract)")
    print(f"LED duty:    {duty*100:.1f}% (should be 0)")
    # Vsense should track ambient (0.6V), LED never on
    assert abs(mean - 0.6) < 0.02
    assert duty < 0.05
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_controller_ambient_ramp():
    print("=== Controller: ambient 1→5 ramp, target 5 ===")
    ambient = RampSource(1.0, 5.0, 0.005)
    ctrl = AdaptiveLightController(ambient, target_vref=0.5)
    ctrl.run_for(0.006)
    vh = ctrl.probe("vsense").history
    rh = ctrl.probe("vref").history
    # Sample at t = 0, 2, 4, 5, 6 ms
    for t_ms in [0, 2, 4, 5, 6]:
        idx = min(range(len(vh)), key=lambda i: abs(vh[i][0] - t_ms * 1e-3))
        v, r = vh[idx][1], rh[idx][1]
        print(f"t={t_ms} ms: Vsense={v:.4f}  Vref={r:.4f}  "
              f"err={(r-v)*1000:+.1f} mV")
    # Before the ramp passes target: tracking (Vsense ≈ Vref)
    vh_2ms = min(range(len(vh)), key=lambda i: abs(vh[i][0] - 0.002))
    print(f"\nAt 2ms (mid-ramp): Vsense = {vh[vh_2ms][1]:.3f}V")
    # After ramp ends at 5 -> ambient alone exceeds target 5
    final_hist = vh[-500:]
    vfinal = sum(v for _, v in final_hist) / len(final_hist)
    print(f"Final Vsense (last 0.5ms): {vfinal:.3f}V (expect 0.5)")
    assert abs(vfinal - 0.5) < 0.03
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_loop_builds_light_subsystem(tmp_path="/tmp/ladder15.json"):
    print("=== Loop builds the light subsystem ===")
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    reg = DeviceRegistry()
    reg.register(spec_light_sensor())
    reg.register(spec_adaptive_light())
    log = DevelopmentLog()
    store = DeviceStore(tmp_path)
    loop = DevelopmentLoop(reg, log, store, max_explorations=0, verbose=True)
    loop.run(10)
    built = log.built_names()
    print(f"\nBuilt: {sorted(built)}")
    assert "LightSensor" in built
    assert "AdaptiveLightController" in built
    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    print("PASS.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_photodiode_alone()
    test_light_sensor()
    test_controller_ambient_low()
    test_controller_ambient_high()
    test_controller_ambient_ramp()
    test_loop_builds_light_subsystem()
```

The photodiode behaves exactly as theory predicts: 3 light units × 1 µA/unit × 1 MΩ = 3 V. The controller settles on a 33.4% LED duty cycle when ambient is 2 and target is 5. That matches the analytical (5 − 2)/9 = 33.3% to within 0.1 percentage points. When ambient (6) already exceeds target (5), the controller correctly leaves the LED off and reports Vsense = 0.6 — the loop saturates in the "can't subtract light" regime. When ambient ramps from 1 to 5, Vsense tracks Vref within 0.3 mV throughout the ramp. The loop builds both devices in dependency order.
