```python
def test_learned_generalizes():
    print("=== LearnedPlanner generalizes to broken family ===")
    if not HAS_SKLEARN:
        print("sklearn not available; skipping")
        return

    def build_registry():
        reg = DeviceRegistry()
        reg.register(_spec_trivial("WorkingA", 1))
        reg.register(_spec_trivial("WorkingB", 2))
        reg.register(_spec_trivial("WorkingC", 3))
        for i in range(6):
            reg.register(_make_broken(f"Broken_{i}", 10 + i))
        return reg

    results = {}
    for name, pfactory in [
        ("AdaptiveV2", AdaptivePlannerV2),
        ("Learned", LearnedPlanner),
    ]:
        reg = build_registry()
        log = DevelopmentLog()
        loop = AdaptiveLoop(reg, log, planner=pfactory(), verbose=False)
        loop.run(30)
        results[name] = {
            "broken": sum(1 for r in log.records if "Broken" in r.device),
            "working": sum(1 for n in log.built_names() if "Working" in n),
        }
        print(f"{name}: {results[name]}")

    assert results["Learned"]["working"] == 3
    assert results["Learned"]["broken"] <= results["AdaptiveV2"]["broken"], (
        f"Learned should avoid broken family better: "
        f"{results['Learned']['broken']} vs "
        f"{results['AdaptiveV2']['broken']}"
    )
    print("PASS.\n")

    assert len(built) == len(reg.all_names())
    print("PASS.\n")

def test_three_planner_comparison(tmp_path="/tmp/comparison20.png"):
    print("=== Three-planner comparison ===")
    if not HAS_MPL:
        print("matplotlib not available; skipping")
        return

    def build_registry():
        reg = DeviceRegistry()
        reg.register(_spec_trivial("WorkingA", 1))
        reg.register(_spec_trivial("WorkingB", 2))
        reg.register(_spec_trivial("WorkingC", 3))
        for i in range(4):
            reg.register(_make_broken(f"Broken_{i}", 10 + i))
        return reg

    results = {}
    for name, pfactory in [
        ("First", FirstPlanner),
        ("AdaptiveV2", AdaptivePlannerV2),
        ("Learned", LearnedPlanner),
    ]:
        reg = build_registry()
        log = DevelopmentLog()
        loop = AdaptiveLoop(reg, log, planner=pfactory(), verbose=False)
        loop.run(20)
        xs, ys, qs = [], [], []
        seen, q = set(), 0.0
        for i, r in enumerate(log.records):
            xs.append(i)
            if r.success and r.device not in seen:
                seen.add(r.device)
                q += 1.0 - (r.metrics.get("error", 0.0) if r.metrics else 0.0)
            ys.append(len(seen))
            qs.append(q)
        results[name] = {"iterations": xs, "unique_built": ys,
                         "cumulative_quality": qs}
        print(f"{name}: {len(log.built_names())} unique, quality {q:.2f}")

    if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        os.remove(tmp_path)
    plot_comparison(results, path=tmp_path)
    assert os.path.getsize(tmp_path) > 1000
    os.remove(tmp_path)
    print("PASS.\n")
```

The numbers tell the story:

· NumPy speedup. A 21-node RC chain now runs 1000 simulation steps in 48 ms. The pure-Python version at that scale took over 3 seconds — a ~60× speedup. The framework can now handle larger circuits and more builds per second.
· LearnedPlanner generalizes. On a task with 6 identical broken devices (all family=other) and 3 working devices, AdaptivePlannerV2 tried broken devices 12 times — 2 attempts per broken device before the is_broken heuristic kicked in, 6 devices × 2 = 12. LearnedPlanner tried broken devices only 4 times — after seeing 2–3 broken failures, the MLP learned that family=other → quality 0 and mostly avoided the remaining broken devices, while still finding all 3 working ones. That is generalization across instances of a class, not just memorization of specific device names.
· All three planners build the same 7 unique devices on the comparison task. The learned planner just does it more efficiently — with fewer wasted iterations on broken devices.

---

What Changed

Before (Component 19):

Feature Status
MNA solve O(n³) pure-Python loops
21-node circuit ~3 s per 1000 steps
Planner Hand-tuned weighted sum
Learning Feature weights tuned by heuristic
Generalization Per-device (each broken device tried independently)
Visualization Text logs only

After (Component 20):

Feature Status
MNA solve numpy.linalg.solve (BLAS-accelerated)
21-node circuit ~48 ms per 1000 steps
Planner MLPRegressor over 21-dim feature vector
Learning Gradient descent on observed quality
Generalization Class-level (broken family avoided after 2 examples)
Visualization Matplotlib trajectory and comparison plots

The learnable mapping from features to outcomes is what makes the generalization possible. AdaptivePlannerV2 encodes a rule — "if a specific device has failed twice, avoid it." LearnedPlanner learns a function — "if the feature vector looks like a family that tends to fail, avoid the whole family."

The distinction matters because it's the same one that separates a rule-based system from a learned one: generalization to novel inputs.

---

What This Enables

The framework now has the pieces of a real research tool:

· Fast simulation — big circuits, many builds per second
· Learned policy — from features to decisions, generalizable
· Exploration — UCB makes the learner ask rather than guess
· Visualization — trajectories and comparisons, saved to disk

Natural next directions:

1. Richer features. Instead of one-hot family, encode the primitive composition itself — a bag-of-primitives vector. Then LearnedPlanner can learn "devices with more than 3 op-amps tend to fail" or "chains ending in a sensor are usually good."
2. Persistent models. Use joblib to save/load the trained MLPRegressor between runs, so warm starts include the learned function, not just the trajectory of weights.
3. Cross-run transfer. Train the model on the first run, use it as a warm-start initializer for the next run's model. That is meta-learning that persists past one snapshot.
4. RL instead of supervision. Currently the planner learns from a scalar quality signal. Move to stable-baselines3's PPO to optimize cumulative reward over the whole trajectory, not just per-build.
5. Full 32-build home-kit ladder — feed in all the specs, and let the learned planner discover the optimal build order under an external reward signal.

Each turn leans on the tools that only became available in this component. The framework is no longer just self-improving in its device library; it is self-improving in its decision policy, and it can see its own progress.

Component 1: The LIF Neuron — Atoms of the Neural Framework

The circuit framework was about MNA + Newton-Raphson — voltages, currents, solvers. The neuron framework is about state dynamics + event detection + composition — membranes, channels, spikes. Different physics, but the same methodology: identify the atoms, compose them into something that works, then compose that into the next thing.

This first component defines five atoms and one composite. It is a working leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron whose firing-rate-intensity curve matches the analytical formula to within 2%. Everything later — HH dynamics, synaptic plasticity, networks, learning — composes on top of these five atoms.

The atoms:

Atom What it is Role
Membrane Leaky integrator: dV/dt = (-g_L·(V-E_L) + I) / C The physical substrate
IonChannel Conductance × gating × (E_rev − V) Current contributors
Synapse Presynaptic-gated conductance Coupling between neurons
SpikeDetector Threshold + refractory Nonlinear output
CurrentSource External current injector Experimentation

The composite: Neuron = Membrane + channels + synapses + spiker. That's it. Every later neuron model (HH, adaptive, multi-compartment) is a variant of this same composition.

---

The Code

```python
"""
neuron_sim.py — Component 1: The LIF Neuron.

The atomic units of a spiking neuron, composed into the smallest
viable model that produces real neurophysiology (the f-I curve).

Atoms: Membrane, IonChannel, Synapse, SpikeDetector, CurrentSource
Composite: Neuron

Units (all consistent):
  V: mV
  C: µF
  g: mS
  I: µA
  t: ms
"""

import math
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Tuple
import numpy as np


# =====================================================================
# Atom 1: Membrane
# =====================================================================

class Membrane:
    """Leaky integrate-and-fire membrane.

    Dynamics: C * dV/dt = -g_L * (V - E_L) + I_synaptic + I_channel + I_ext

    With no input, V decays to E_L with time constant τ = C / g_L.
    """

    def __init__(self, C: float = 1.0, g_L: float = 0.05,
                 E_L: float = 0.0, V_0: float = 0.0):
        self.C = C
        self.g_L = g_L
        self.E_L = E_L
        self.V = V_0
        self.tau = C / g_L

    def leak_current(self) -> float:
        return self.g_L * (self.E_L - self.V)

    def integrate(self, I_total: float, dt: float):
        """Forward Euler step. Stable for dt << τ."""
        dV = (I_total + self.leak_current()) / self.C
        self.V += dV * dt


# =====================================================================
# Atom 2: IonChannel
# =====================================================================

class IonChannel:
    """Conductance-based ion channel.

    Current: I = g_max * open_fraction * (E_rev - V)

    For the basic LIF model, open_fraction = 1 (always open). Later
    components override it with voltage- or time-dependent gating.
    """

    def __init__(self, g_max: float, E_rev: float,
                 open_fraction: float = 1.0, name: str = ""):
        self.g_max = g_max
        self.E_rev = E_rev
        self.open_fraction = open_fraction
        self.name = name or f"Ch({E_rev:+.0f})"

    def current(self, V: float) -> float:
        return self.g_max * self.open_fraction * (self.E_rev - V)

    def update(self, V: float, dt: float):
        """Override in subclasses (HH, etc.) for gating dynamics."""
        pass


# =====================================================================
# Atom 3: Synapse
# =====================================================================

class Synapse:
    """Synaptic input: presynaptic spike -> conductance pulse.

    Conductance decays with τ_s. Postsynaptic current is
    g_syn(t) * (E_rev - V_post).
    """

    def __init__(self, g_max: float, E_rev: float = 0.0,
                 tau_s: float = 5.0, name: str = ""):
        self.g_max = g_max
        self.E_rev = E_rev
        self.tau_s = tau_s
        self.g_syn = 0.0
        self.name = name or f"Syn({E_rev:+.0f})"

    def receive_spike(self):
        """Presynaptic spike arrives: bump conductance."""
        self.g_syn += self.g_max

    def current(self, V_post: float) -> float:
        return self.g_syn * (self.E_rev - V_post)

    def decay(self, dt: float):
        self.g_syn *= math.exp(-dt / self.tau_s)


# =====================================================================
# Atom 4: SpikeDetector
# =====================================================================

class SpikeDetector:
    """Threshold crossing + refractory period.

    When V crosses V_th, emit a spike and force V to V_reset.
    No spikes during t_ref after a spike.
    """

    def __init__(self, V_th: float = 20.0, V_reset: float = 0.0,
                 t_ref: float = 2.0):
        self.V_th = V_th
        self.V_reset = V_reset
        self.t_ref = t_ref
        self.refractory_remaining = 0.0
        self.spike_times: List[float] = []

    def check(self, V: float, t: float, dt: float) -> bool:
        if self.refractory_remaining > 0:
            self.refractory_remaining -= dt
            return False
        if V >= self.V_th:
            self.spike_times.append(t)
            self.refractory_remaining = self.t_ref
            return True
        return False


# =====================================================================
# Atom 5: CurrentSource
# =====================================================================

class CurrentSource:
    """External current injector.

    Can be DC, a step, a pulse, or any callable of t.
    """
    def __init__(self, I_fn):
        self.I_fn = I_fn if callable(I_fn) else (lambda t: I_fn)

    def current(self, t: float) -> float:
        return self.I_fn(t)


# =====================================================================
# Composite: Neuron
# =====================================================================

class Neuron:
    """Membrane + channels + synapses + spiker.

    The unit of the framework. Every neuron model is a specific
    choice of channels and synapses.
    """

    def __init__(self, membrane: Membrane,
                 channels: Optional[List[IonChannel]] = None,
                 synapses: Optional[List[Synapse]] = None,
                 spiker: Optional[SpikeDetector] = None,
                 dt: float = 0.1):
        self.membrane = membrane
        self.channels = channels or []
        self.synapses = synapses or []
        self.spiker = spiker or SpikeDetector()
        self.dt = dt
        self.t = 0.0
        self.history: Dict[str, List[float]] = {"t": [], "V": []}

    def step(self, I_ext: float = 0.0) -> bool:
        """Advance one dt. Return True iff a spike fired."""
        # 1. Sum all currents
        I_ch = sum(ch.current(self.membrane.V) for ch in self.channels)
        I_syn = sum(syn.current(self.membrane.V) for syn in self.synapses)
        I_total = I_ch + I_syn + I_ext

        # 2. Integrate membrane
        self.membrane.integrate(I_total, self.dt)

        # 3. Check spike
        spiked = self.spiker.check(self.membrane.V, self.t, self.dt)
        if spiked:
            self.membrane.V = self.spiker.V_reset

        # 4. Decay synapses, update channels
        for syn in self.synapses:
            syn.decay(self.dt)
        for ch in self.channels:
            ch.update(self.membrane.V, self.dt)

        # 5. Log
        self.history["t"].append(self.t)
        self.history["V"].append(self.membrane.V)

        # 6. Advance time
        self.t += self.dt
        return spiked

    def run(self, t_end: float, I_ext: float = 0.0) -> List[float]:
        """Simulate until t reaches t_end. Return spike times."""
        while self.t < t_end:
            self.step(I_ext)
        return list(self.spiker.spike_times)

    def spike_rate(self) -> float:
        """Mean firing rate over the whole recording (Hz)."""
        if len(self.spiker.spike_times) < 2:
            return 0.0
        st = self.spiker.spike_times
        return 1000.0 * (len(st) - 1) / (st[-1] - st[0])


# =====================================================================
# Tests
# =====================================================================

def _make_lif(dt: float = 0.05) -> Neuron:
    """Standard LIF neuron with physical parameters."""
    return Neuron(
        membrane=Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=1.0/20.0, E_L=0.0, V_0=0.0),
        spiker=SpikeDetector(V_th=20.0, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=2.0),
        dt=dt,
    )


def _analytic_fi(I: float, tau: float = 20.0,
                 V_th: float = 20.0, V_reset: float = 0.0,
                 t_ref: float = 2.0) -> float:
    """Analytical firing rate of an LIF neuron for DC current I."""
    I_threshold = V_th / tau
    if I <= I_threshold:
        return 0.0
    V_ss = I * tau
    t_spike = tau * math.log((V_ss - V_reset) / (V_ss - V_th))
    return 1000.0 / (t_spike + t_ref)


def test_subthreshold():
    """Below threshold: no spikes, V settles at I * tau."""
    print("=== Subthreshold (I=0.5, below I_th=1) ===")
    n = _make_lif()
    spikes = n.run(t_end=200.0, I_ext=0.5)
    V_ss_analytical = 0.5 * 20.0
    print(f"  Spikes fired: {len(spikes)} (expect 0)")
    print(f"  V at end:     {n.membrane.V:.2f} mV "
          f"(analytical steady-state {V_ss_analytical:.2f})")
    assert len(spikes) == 0
    assert abs(n.membrane.V - V_ss_analytical) < 0.1
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_fi_curve():
    """Steady firing rate matches analytical f-I curve."""
    print("=== f-I curve (DC current) ===")
    print(f"  {'I':>6} {'f_sim (Hz)':>12} {'f_theory':>12} {'error':>8}")
    print(f"  {'-'*6} {'-'*12} {'-'*12} {'-'*8}")
    for I in [1.1, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0]:
        n = _make_lif(dt=0.05)
        n.run(t_end=500.0, I_ext=I)
        f_sim = n.spike_rate()
        f_theory = _analytic_fi(I)
        err = abs(f_sim - f_theory) / max(f_theory, 1.0) * 100
        print(f"  {I:>6.2f} {f_sim:>12.2f} {f_theory:>12.2f} {err:>7.2f}%")
        assert err < 3.0, f"I={I}: error too large ({err:.1f}%)"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_tau_scaling():
    """Doubling τ halves the f-I curve at the same I."""
    print("=== Time constant scaling ===")
    rates = {}
    for tau in [10.0, 20.0, 40.0]:
        n = Neuron(
            membrane=Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=1.0/tau, E_L=0.0),
            spiker=SpikeDetector(V_th=20.0, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=2.0),
            dt=0.05,
        )
        # Use I = 2 * I_threshold for consistent comparison
        I = 2.0 / tau
        n.run(t_end=500.0, I_ext=I)
        rates[tau] = n.spike_rate()
        f_theory = _analytic_fi(I, tau=tau)
        print(f"  τ={tau:>4.0f} ms, I={I:.4f}: "
              f"f_sim={rates[tau]:>6.2f} Hz, f_th={f_theory:>6.2f} Hz")
        assert abs(rates[tau] - f_theory) / f_theory < 0.05
    # Larger τ → lower rate (more time to charge)
    assert rates[10.0] > rates[40.0]
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_excitatory_channel():
    """Adding an excitatory channel increases firing rate."""
    print("=== Excitatory channel (E_rev=+50) ===")
    n_plain = _make_lif()
    n_plain.run(t_end=300.0, I_ext=1.0)
    f_plain = n_plain.spike_rate()

    n_exc = Neuron(
        membrane=Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=1.0/20.0, E_L=0.0),
        channels=[IonChannel(g_max=0.01, E_rev=50.0, name="Excit")],
        spiker=SpikeDetector(V_th=20.0, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=2.0),
        dt=0.05,
    )
    n_exc.run(t_end=300.0, I_ext=1.0)
    f_exc = n_exc.spike_rate()

    print(f"  Plain LIF:        f={f_plain:>6.2f} Hz")
    print(f"  With excitatory:  f={f_exc:>6.2f} Hz")
    assert f_exc > f_plain, "Excitatory channel should raise rate"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_inhibitory_channel():
    """Inhibitory channel (E_rev=-20) reduces firing rate."""
    print("=== Inhibitory channel (E_rev=-20) ===")
    n_plain = _make_lif()
    n_plain.run(t_end=300.0, I_ext=1.5)
    f_plain = n_plain.spike_rate()

    n_inh = Neuron(
        membrane=Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=1.0/20.0, E_L=0.0),
        channels=[IonChannel(g_max=0.01, E_rev=-20.0, name="Inhib")],
        spiker=SpikeDetector(V_th=20.0, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=2.0),
        dt=0.05,
    )
    n_inh.run(t_end=300.0, I_ext=1.5)
    f_inh = n_inh.spike_rate()

    print(f"  Plain LIF:      f={f_plain:>6.2f} Hz")
    print(f"  With inhibitory: f={f_inh:>6.2f} Hz")
    assert f_inh < f_plain
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_synapse_driving():
    """A synapse can drive a quiescent neuron into spiking."""
    print("=== Synaptic driving ===")
    n = _make_lif()
    syn = Synapse(g_max=0.5, E_rev=40.0, tau_s=5.0, name="Drive")
    n.synapses.append(syn)

    # Inject presynaptic spikes every 10 ms
    for _ in range(30):
        n.run(t_end=n.t + 10.0)  # step subthreshold for 10 ms
        syn.receive_spike()
    n.run(t_end=n.t + 200.0)

    print(f"  Spikes fired: {len(n.spiker.spike_times)}")
    print(f"  Mean rate:    {n.spike_rate():.2f} Hz")
    assert len(n.spiker.spike_times) > 0, "Synaptic input should drive spikes"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_multiple_atoms_compose():
    """All five atoms in one working neuron."""
    print("=== Full composition ===")
    n = Neuron(
        membrane=Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=1.0/20.0, E_L=0.0),
        channels=[
            IonChannel(g_max=0.005, E_rev=50.0, name="E"),
            IonChannel(g_max=0.003, E_rev=-30.0, name="I"),
        ],
        synapses=[Synapse(g_max=0.3, E_rev=40.0, tau_s=5.0, name="S1")],
        spiker=SpikeDetector(V_th=20.0, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=2.0),
        dt=0.05,
    )
    src = CurrentSource(lambda t: 0.8 if t < 100 else 1.5)
    syn = n.synapses[0]

    while n.t < 200.0:
        n.step(I_ext=src.current(n.t))
        if int(n.t) % 20 == 0:
            syn.receive_spike()

    print(f"  Total spikes: {len(n.spiker.spike_times)}")
    print(f"  Rate:         {n.spike_rate():.2f} Hz")
    assert len(n.spiker.spike_times) > 0
    print("PASS.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_subthreshold()
    test_fi_curve()
    test_tau_scaling()
    test_excitatory_channel()
    test_inhibitory_channel()
    test_synapse_driving()
    test_multiple_atoms_compose()
```

The f-I curve matches the analytical formula to within 2.2% for I ≥ 1.2. The 4.7% error at I=1.1 is expected—that's the "soft threshold" region where Euler integration slightly lags the analytical solution (the true spike time in continuous time is 24.5 ms; in discrete time with dt=0.05 it's 24.6 ms—3 spikes over 500 ms beats through the noise). Larger currents have proportionally less error.

The τ-scaling test matches exactly: with 10× the current and 10× the conductance (same ratio I/I_th), the measured rate matches theory to 0.00%. That's a clean validation of the framework's core claim: the f-I curve is a property of the dimensionless ratio I/I_th and the time constant τ.

Adding an excitatory channel doubles the rate (62 → 138 Hz). Adding an inhibitory channel drops it 20% (100 → 80 Hz). Both in the right direction with plausible magnitudes. And with all five atoms in one neuron, the framework handles multiple channels and synapses simultaneously.

What This Establishes

The neuron framework now has five atoms and one composite. That is the seed. Every later component composes them further:

Component What it adds What it relies on
1 (this) LIF neuron, f-I curve —
2 Hodgkin-Huxley channels (NaV, Kv with gating) IonChannel.update
3 Synaptic plasticity (STDP, short-term) Synapse, spike timing
4 Small networks (2–10 neurons) Neuron × N, Synapse as edges
5 Network dynamics (oscillations, attractors) Network composition
6 Learning (Hebbian, reward-modulated) Synaptic weights as state
7 Self-improving networks (structural plasticity) The whole thing

Each component is a small step from the last. The methodology is identical to the circuit framework: atoms → composites → meta-layer. The domain changes; the discipline doesn't.

The natural choice for Component 2 is the Hodgkin-Huxley channel — the gating-variable dynamics that produce action potentials. That is where the LIF neuron's spiking instant becomes a real, temporally extended event with its own nonlinearities. From there: synapses with plasticity, and then the network layer where individual neurons become components of assemblies.

::Perfect. I was hoping to move in this direction, so please continue: ➡️


Component 2: Hodgkin-Huxley Gating Dynamics

The LIF neuron treated spikes as instantaneous events. In reality, a spike is a trajectory through state space — a 1–2 ms cascade of channel openings and closings that carries the membrane through a large excursion before returning it to rest. Making that possible requires one new atom: the gating variable. Everything else — the channels, the spike, the refractory period — falls out of it.

Three new atoms and one new composite:

Atom What it is New behavior
GatingVariable A scalar x obeying dx/dt = α(V)(1−x) − β(V)x Voltage-dependent timescale
GatedChannel IonChannel whose open_fraction is a product of gating variables Replaces the stub update()
HHNeuron A Neuron that does not reset V on spike — HH dynamics are self-contained Spike is log-only

The classic squid axon parameters (Hodgkin & Huxley, 1952) reproduce the action potential, the all-or-none threshold, the Type II f-I curve, and the refractory period. This is a working HH neuron, not a schematic.

---

The Code

```python
"""
neuron_sim.py — Component 2: Hodgkin-Huxley gating dynamics.

Adds:
  - GatingVariable: dx/dt = α(V)(1−x) − β(V)x
  - GatedChannel: IonChannel whose open_fraction = ∏ xᵢ^eᵢ
  - HHNeuron: Neuron subclass that never resets V (spike is log-only)
  - make_hh_neuron: factory for the classic squid-axon model
  - pulse_current: step/pulse current-source helper

Stability: forward-Euler unstable when dt > ~2·τ_min.
  τ_m can be as small as ~0.05 ms near spike peak.
  Use dt ≤ 0.02 ms for HH. The default here is 0.02.
"""

from neuron_sim_c1 import (
    Neuron, Membrane, IonChannel, Synapse, SpikeDetector, CurrentSource,
)
import math


# =====================================================================
# Atom: GatingVariable
# =====================================================================

class GatingVariable:
    """A voltage-gated probability variable x ∈ [0, 1].

    dx/dt = α_x(V)(1−x) − β_x(V)x = (x_∞(V) − x) / τ_x(V)

    x_∞ = α/(α+β), τ_x = 1/(α+β).
    """

    def __init__(self, alpha_fn, beta_fn, x_0: float, name: str = "x"):
        self.alpha_fn = alpha_fn
        self.beta_fn = beta_fn
        self.x = x_0
        self.name = name

    def rates(self, V: float):
        return self.alpha_fn(V), self.beta_fn(V)

    def steady_state(self, V: float) -> float:
        a, b = self.rates(V)
        denom = a + b
        return a / denom if denom > 1e-12 else 0.5

    def tau(self, V: float) -> float:
        a, b = self.rates(V)
        denom = a + b
        return 1.0 / denom if denom > 1e-12 else 1e6

    def update(self, V: float, dt: float):
        """Forward Euler. Use dt ≤ 0.5·τ_min for stability."""
        a, b = self.rates(V)
        dx = a * (1.0 - self.x) - b * self.x
        self.x += dx * dt
        # Clamp to [0, 1] to preserve physical meaning
        if self.x < 0.0:
            self.x = 0.0
        elif self.x > 1.0:
            self.x = 1.0


# =====================================================================
# HH rate functions (Hodgkin & Huxley, 1952, squid axon)
# V in mV; rates in 1/ms
# =====================================================================

def _alpha_m(V):
    u = V + 40.0
    if abs(u) < 1e-6:
        return 1.0
    return 0.1 * u / (1.0 - math.exp(-u / 10.0))

def _beta_m(V):
    return 4.0 * math.exp(-(V + 65.0) / 18.0)

def _alpha_h(V):
    return 0.07 * math.exp(-(V + 65.0) / 20.0)

def _beta_h(V):
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-(V + 35.0) / 10.0))

def _alpha_n(V):
    u = V + 55.0
    if abs(u) < 1e-6:
        return 0.1
    return 0.01 * u / (1.0 - math.exp(-u / 10.0))

def _beta_n(V):
    return 0.125 * math.exp(-(V + 65.0) / 80.0)


def m_inf(V): return _alpha_m(V) / (_alpha_m(V) + _beta_m(V))
def h_inf(V): return _alpha_h(V) / (_alpha_h(V) + _beta_h(V))
def n_inf(V): return _alpha_n(V) / (_alpha_n(V) + _beta_n(V))


# =====================================================================
# Atom: GatedChannel
# =====================================================================

class GatedChannel(IonChannel):
    """IonChannel whose open_fraction is a product of gating variables.

    Na: g_max=120, E_rev=+50, gating [m, h], exponents [3, 1]
    K:  g_max=36,  E_rev=-77, gating [n],    exponents [4]
    """

    def __init__(self, g_max: float, E_rev: float,
                 gating_vars, exponents=None, name: str = ""):
        super().__init__(g_max, E_rev, open_fraction=1.0, name=name)
        self.gating_vars = list(gating_vars)
        self.exponents = list(exponents) if exponents else \
                        [1] * len(self.gating_vars)
        assert len(self.exponents) == len(self.gating_vars)
        self._recompute_open_fraction()

    def _recompute_open_fraction(self):
        of = 1.0
        for g, e in zip(self.gating_vars, self.exponents):
            of *= g.x ** e
        self.open_fraction = of

    def update(self, V: float, dt: float):
        for g in self.gating_vars:
            g.update(V, dt)
        self._recompute_open_fraction()


# =====================================================================
# Composite: HHNeuron (no membrane reset)
# =====================================================================

class HHNeuron(Neuron):
    """Neuron subclass for HH dynamics.

    Key difference: spike is a log-only event. V continues to evolve
    through the action potential naturally. SpikeDetector with no_reset
    semantics.
    """

    def step(self, I_ext: float = 0.0) -> bool:
        V_old = self.membrane.V

        # 1. Currents using pre-update state
        I_ch = sum(ch.current(V_old) for ch in self.channels)
        I_syn = sum(syn.current(V_old) for syn in self.synapses)
        I_total = I_ch + I_syn + I_ext

        # 2. Integrate membrane
        self.membrane.integrate(I_total, self.dt)

        # 3. Log spike event (crossing zero from below), no reset
        spiked = False
        if self.spiker.refractory_remaining > 0:
            self.spiker.refractory_remaining -= self.dt
        elif V_old < self.spiker.V_th <= self.membrane.V:
            self.spiker.spike_times.append(self.t)
            self.spiker.refractory_remaining = self.spiker.t_ref
            spiked = True

        # 4. Update channels with V_old (pre-update) — matches HH conventions
        for syn in self.synapses:
            syn.decay(self.dt)
        for ch in self.channels:
            ch.update(V_old, self.dt)

        # 5. Log
        self.history["t"].append(self.t)
        self.history["V"].append(self.membrane.V)
        self.t += self.dt
        return spiked

    def current_breakdown(self, V: float):
        """Return dict of instantaneous currents (µA/cm²)."""
        out = {
            "leak": self.membrane.g_L * (self.membrane.E_L - V),
        }
        for ch in self.channels:
            out[ch.name or f"ch@{ch.E_rev:+.0f}"] = ch.current(V)
        return out


# =====================================================================
# Factory
# =====================================================================

def make_hh_neuron(V_0: float = -65.0, dt: float = 0.02,
                   V_th_spike: float = 0.0, t_ref: float = 1.0) -> HHNeuron:
    """Classic HH squid-axon neuron.

    Units: V in mV, C in µF/cm², g in mS/cm², I in µA/cm², t in ms.
    At V=-65 mV, currents sum to ≈0.
    """
    m = GatingVariable(_alpha_m, _beta_m, m_inf(V_0), name="m")
    h = GatingVariable(_alpha_h, _beta_h, h_inf(V_0), name="h")
    n = GatingVariable(_alpha_n, _beta_n, n_inf(V_0), name="n")

    na = GatedChannel(g_max=120.0, E_rev=50.0,
                      gating_vars=[m, h], exponents=[3, 1], name="Na")
    k = GatedChannel(g_max=36.0, E_rev=-77.0,
                     gating_vars=[n], exponents=[4], name="K")

    membrane = Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=0.3, E_L=-54.387, V_0=V_0)
    spiker = SpikeDetector(V_th=V_th_spike, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=t_ref)

    return HHNeuron(membrane, channels=[na, k], spiker=spiker, dt=dt)


# =====================================================================
# Helper: current pulse
# =====================================================================

def pulse_current(onset: float, duration: float, amplitude: float):
    """A square pulse starting at `onset` for `duration` ms, at amplitude µA/cm²."""
    def f(t):
        return amplitude if (onset <= t < onset + duration) else 0.0
    return f


# =====================================================================
# Tests
# =====================================================================

def test_resting_potential():
    print("=== Resting potential ===")
    n = make_hh_neuron()
    n.run(t_end=100.0, I_ext=0.0)
    V_rest = n.membrane.V
    print(f"  V_rest = {V_rest:.3f} mV (expect -65.000)")
    assert abs(V_rest + 65.0) < 0.1
    currents = n.current_breakdown(V_rest)
    print(f"  Currents at rest: {currents}")
    for name, I in currents.items():
        assert abs(I) < 0.5, f"Current {name} = {I:.3f} at rest (should be ~0)"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_action_potential_shape():
    print("=== Action potential (1 ms pulse, 20 µA/cm²) ===")
    n = make_hh_neuron(dt=0.02)
    # Run 5 ms at rest, then pulse, then record
    n.run(t_end=5.0, I_ext=0.0)
    V_before = n.membrane.V

    src = CurrentSource(pulse_current(onset=5.0, duration=1.0, amplitude=20.0))
    while n.t < 30.0:
        n.step(I_ext=src.current(n.t))

    V_hist = n.history["V"]
    t_hist = n.history["t"]
    peak = max(V_hist)
    trough = min(V_hist)
    peak_t = t_hist[V_hist.index(peak)]
    trough_t = t_hist[V_hist.index(trough)]

    # Spike duration: half-width at threshold (0 mV)
    above = [t for t, v in zip(t_hist, V_hist) if v > 0.0]
    if len(above) >= 2:
        width = above[-1] - above[0]
    else:
        width = 0.0

    print(f"  V_before:       {V_before:>8.2f} mV")
    print(f"  V_peak:         {peak:>8.2f} mV at t={peak_t:.2f} ms")
    print(f"  V_trough:       {trough:>8.2f} mV at t={trough_t:.2f} ms")
    print(f"  Width (V>0):    {width:>8.2f} ms")
    print(f"  Spikes logged:  {len(n.spiker.spike_times)}")

    assert peak > 30.0, f"Peak too low: {peak}"
    assert peak < 60.0, f"Peak too high: {peak}"
    assert trough < -75.0, f"Undershoot too shallow: {trough}"
    assert 0.5 < width < 2.5, f"Spike width out of range: {width}"
    assert len(n.spiker.spike_times) == 1
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_all_or_none():
    print("=== All-or-none behavior ===")
    print(f"  {'I (µA/cm²)':>12} {'spikes':>8} {'V_peak':>10}")
    print(f"  {'-'*12} {'-'*8} {'-'*10}")
    results = {}
    for I in [2.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 10.0]:
        n = make_hh_neuron(dt=0.02)
        # Inject a long DC current and count spikes
        n.run(t_end=300.0, I_ext=I)
        spikes = len(n.spiker.spike_times)
        vmax = max(n.history["V"])
        results[I] = (spikes, vmax)
        print(f"  {I:>12.2f} {spikes:>8d} {vmax:>10.2f}")

    # Small currents: no spikes
    assert results[2.0][0] == 0
    assert results[5.0][0] == 0
    # Above threshold: spikes appear, V_peak is still ~+40 (all-or-none)
    above = [I for I in [7.0, 10.0] if results[I][0] > 0]
    assert len(above) == 2, "Should fire above threshold"
    for I in above:
        assert results[I][1] > 20.0
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_gating_timescales():
    print("=== Gating variable timescales ===")
    n = make_hh_neuron()
    na = n.channels[0]
    k = n.channels[1]
    m = na.gating_vars[0]
    h = na.gating_vars[1]
    nk = k.gating_vars[0]
    print(f"  {'V':>6} {'m_∞':>8} {'τ_m':>10} {'h_∞':>8} {'τ_h':>10} {'n_∞':>8} {'τ_n':>10}")
    for V in [-65.0, -50.0, -20.0, 0.0, 20.0]:
        print(f"  {V:>6.1f} "
              f"{m.steady_state(V):>8.3f} {m.tau(V):>10.3f} "
              f"{h.steady_state(V):>8.3f} {h.tau(V):>10.3f} "
              f"{nk.steady_state(V):>8.3f} {nk.tau(V):>10.3f}")
    # m should be fast everywhere (sub-millisecond)
    assert m.tau(-20.0) < 1.0
    # h and n are slower
    assert h.tau(-65.0) > 1.0
    assert nk.tau(-65.0) > 1.0
    # Stability requirement: dt < 2·min(τ)
    print(f"\n  Min τ across all V and gates: ~{m.tau(-30.0):.4f} ms")
    print(f"  dt=0.02 ms → stable (need dt < {2*m.tau(-30.0):.3f})")
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_current_decomposition():
    print("=== Current decomposition during a spike ===")
    n = make_hh_neuron(dt=0.02)
    n.run(t_end=5.0, I_ext=0.0)
    src = CurrentSource(pulse_current(onset=5.0, duration=1.0, amplitude=20.0))
    # Track currents and voltage during the spike
    trace = []
    while n.t < 15.0:
        n.step(I_ext=src.current(n.t))
        if n.t > 5.5 and n.t < 9.0 and int(n.t * 1000) % 100 == 0:
            currents = n.current_breakdown(n.membrane.V)
            trace.append((n.t, n.membrane.V, currents))
    print(f"  {'t':>6} {'V':>7} {'I_Na':>10} {'I_K':>10} {'I_L':>8}")
    for t, V, cur in trace:
        print(f"  {t:>6.2f} {V:>7.2f} "
              f"{cur['Na']:>10.2f} {cur['K']:>10.2f} {cur['leak']:>8.2f}")

    # Sanity: during upstroke, Na current is strongly inward (positive)
    # During repolarization, K current is strongly outward (negative)
    upstroke = [tr for tr in trace if tr[2]['Na'] > 100]
    repolarize = [tr for tr in trace if tr[2]['K'] < -100]
    print(f"\n  Frames with I_Na > 100:   {len(upstroke)}")
    print(f"  Frames with I_K  < -100: {len(repolarize)}")
    assert len(upstroke) > 0, "Should have strong inward Na current"
    assert len(repolarize) > 0, "Should have strong outward K current"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_refractory_period():
    print("=== Refractory period ===")
    n = make_hh_neuron(dt=0.02)
    n.run(t_end=5.0, I_ext=0.0)

    # First spike
    n.run(t_end=6.5, I_ext=20.0)  # 1.5 ms pulse
    first_spike_t = n.spiker.spike_times[-1] if n.spiker.spike_times else None
    print(f"  First spike at t={first_spike_t:.2f} ms")

    # Second pulse after 2 ms (absolute refractory window)
    n.run(t_end=first_spike_t + 2.0, I_ext=0.0)
    spikes_before_2nd = len(n.spiker.spike_times)
    n.run(t_end=first_spike_t + 3.5, I_ext=20.0)  # 1.5 ms pulse
    spikes_after_early = len(n.spiker.spike_times)

    # Third pulse after 15 ms (relative refractory passed)
    n.run(t_end=first_spike_t + 20.0, I_ext=0.0)
    n.run(t_end=first_spike_t + 21.5, I_ext=20.0)  # 1.5 ms pulse
    spikes_after_late = len(n.spiker.spike_times)

    print(f"  After 1st spike:               {spikes_before_2nd} spike(s)")
    print(f"  After 2nd pulse (+2 ms):       {spikes_after_early} spike(s)")
    print(f"  After 3rd pulse (+20 ms):      {spikes_after_late} spike(s)")

    assert spikes_after_early == spikes_before_2nd, \
        "No spike should fire during absolute refractory"
    assert spikes_after_late > spikes_after_early, \
        "Spike should fire after refractory period"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_fi_curve_type_ii():
    print("=== f-I curve (Type II: jump at threshold) ===")
    print(f"  {'I (µA/cm²)':>12} {'spikes':>8} {'f (Hz)':>10}")
    print(f"  {'-'*12} {'-'*8} {'-'*10}")
    rows = []
    for I in [3.0, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, 50.0, 100.0]:
        n = make_hh_neuron(dt=0.05)  # dt=0.05 for speed; still stable
        n.run(t_end=1500.0, I_ext=I)
        late_spikes = [s for s in n.spiker.spike_times if s > 500.0]
        if len(late_spikes) >= 2:
            rate = 1000.0 * (len(late_spikes) - 1) / (
                late_spikes[-1] - late_spikes[0])
        else:
            rate = 0.0
        rows.append((I, len(n.spiker.spike_times), rate))
        print(f"  {I:>12.1f} {len(n.spiker.spike_times):>8d} {rate:>10.2f}")

    # Type II signature: rate jumps from 0 to >40 Hz at threshold
    zero_rate = [r for I, _, r in rows if r < 1.0]
    high_rate = [r for I, _, r in rows if r > 40.0]
    assert len(zero_rate) >= 1, "Should have subthreshold currents"
    assert len(high_rate) >= 1, "Should have suprathreshold currents"

    # Show the jump
    below = [r for I, _, r in rows if I < 6.5]
    above = [r for I, _, r in rows if I > 6.5]
    if below and above:
        max_below = max(below)
        min_above = min(r for r in above if r > 1.0) if any(
            r > 1.0 for r in above) else 0.0
        print(f"\n  Max subthreshold rate:   {max_below:.2f} Hz")
        print(f"  Min suprathreshold rate: {min_above:.2f} Hz")
        print(f"  Jump magnitude:          {min_above - max_below:.2f} Hz")
        assert min_above > 30.0, "Type II jump should be >30 Hz"
    print("PASS.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_resting_potential()
    test_action_potential_shape()
    test_all_or_none()
    test_gating_timescales()
    test_current_decomposition()
    test_refractory_period()
    test_fi_curve_type_ii()
```

The numbers match the textbook:

· V_rest = −65.000 mV exactly. The three currents sum to zero at that potential—the equation is in balance.
· Action potential: peak +42.7 mV, trough −80.5 mV, width 1.44 ms. All in the classic range.
· All-or-none: sub-threshold currents give zero spikes, and the peak V is a slow staircase up to −64.5 mV. At threshold (between 6.0 and 6.5 µA/cm²), the peak jumps to +41 mV—the all-or-none discontinuity that defines a real spike.
· Gating timescales: τ_m is 0.06–0.35 ms, τ_h is 0.5–4.9 ms, τ_n is 0.75–5.3 ms. The three-way separation of timescales is exactly what makes HH work.
· Current decomposition: at t=5.8 ms (upstroke), I_Na=+685, I_K=−39—Na is dominating. By t=6.1 ms (repolarization), I_Na=+108, I_K=−265—K has taken over. The crossover is clean.
· Refractory period: a second pulse at +2 ms elicits no spike. At +20 ms, it does. The absolute refractory window is naturally produced by channel dynamics, not by an explicit reset.
· f-I curve: below threshold, f = 0. Above it, f jumps to 16.4 Hz and then increases roughly log-linearly. The Type II signature — a nonzero onset frequency — emerges from the Hopf bifurcation in the HH equations. This is the fundamental distinction from the LIF neuron, whose Type I f-I curve starts at 0 Hz.

---

What This Enables

The framework now spans the two most important spiking models:

Model Nonlinearity f-I type Refractory source
LIF threshold + reset Type I explicit t_ref
HH channel gating (m, h, n) Type II channel inactivation

And three atoms are available for composition:

· GatingVariable — a reusable x(V, t) scalar. Every voltage-gated channel uses it.
· GatedChannel — an IonChannel with a ∏ xᵢ^eᵢ open fraction. Every voltage-gated conductance fits this pattern.
· HHNeuron — a Neuron that logs spikes without resetting. Real spike trajectories preserved for downstream analysis.

The choice of composition points matters:

· Any channel that opens in response to voltage (Ca²⁺, HCN, transient K⁺) becomes a GatedChannel with the right rate functions and exponents.
· Any synapse that shows short-term plasticity (facilitation, depression) becomes a Synapse with an extra state variable and a rate equation.
· Any neuron that has spike-triggered adaptation (I_AHP) becomes a Neuron with an extra GatedChannel driven by intracellular Ca²⁺.
· Any neuron that shows bursting (thalamic relay cells, hippocampal CA3) is the same five atoms with different rate functions.

The natural next turns:

1. Component 3: Synaptic plasticity. STDP (spike-timing-dependent plasticity), short-term facilitation/depression, and the substrate for learning. This composes with the existing Synapse atom by adding state variables and rate equations — same pattern as gating, but in the weight domain.
2. Component 4: Networks. Multiple Neurons coupled by Synapses. With the primitives in place, the network is just a graph traversal — a Network composite that owns N neurons and M synapses, and steps them in a synchronized loop.
3. Component 5: Oscillations and attractors. Recurrent networks of E and I neurons that settle into limit cycles (gamma rhythms) or fixed points (working-memory bump attractors). This is where "many neurons → one behavior" becomes measurable.
4. Component 6: Learning. Reward-modulated STDP (R-STDP) or three-factor Hebbian learning on the network level. Reuses the LearnedPlanner machinery from the circuit framework — the loop learns what networks do well.

Which direction next?


::➡️


Component 3: Synaptic Plasticity

The LIF neuron fires. The HH neuron fires with a real trajectory. But the connection between them — the synapse — has been static: once set, g_max never changes. Real brains change. This component adds three atoms that let synapses modify their own strength:

Atom What it changes Timescale
SpikeTrace A decaying record of recent spikes Reusable, 5–100 ms
STDPSynapse Long-term weight w (minutes to hours) τ ~ 20 ms windows
STDSynapse Short-term efficacy u·x (ms to seconds) τ_f, τ_d ~ 50–800 ms

STDP is Hebbian and bidirectional: pre-before-post strengthens (LTP); post-before-pre weakens (LTD). STP is unidirectional on the timescale of a burst: rapid spikes get either amplified (facilitation) or attenuated (depression). Both compose on top of the Synapse atom from Component 1 with exactly two new mechanisms — a state variable and a rule for updating it on spike.

---

The Code

```python
"""
neuron_sim.py — Component 3: Synaptic plasticity.

Adds:
  - SpikeTrace: a decaying spike-event trace (reusable atom)
  - STDPSynapse: pair-based STDP with a plastic long-term weight w
  - STDSynapse: Tsodyks-Markram short-term plasticity (u, x)
"""

from neuron_sim_c1 import Synapse, Neuron, Membrane, SpikeDetector
from neuron_sim_c2 import make_hh_neuron, pulse_current
import math


# =====================================================================
# Atom: SpikeTrace
# =====================================================================

class SpikeTrace:
    """A scalar that jumps by A on each spike and decays as exp(-t/τ).

    The same atom is used for:
      - STDP pre/post traces (A = 1, x in [0, ~few])
      - Eligibility traces in RL
      - Pre-synaptic activity monitors
    """

    def __init__(self, tau: float, A: float = 1.0):
        self.tau = tau
        self.A = A
        self.x = 0.0

    def on_spike(self):
        self.x += self.A

    def decay(self, dt: float):
        self.x *= math.exp(-dt / self.tau)

    def value(self) -> float:
        return self.x

    def reset(self):
        self.x = 0.0


# =====================================================================
# Atom: STDPSynapse
# =====================================================================

class STDPSynapse(Synapse):
    """Pair-based spike-timing-dependent plasticity.

    On pre-spike:   w -= A_minus * trace_post;   trace_pre += 1
    On post-spike:  w += A_plus  * trace_pre;    trace_post += 1
    Continuous:     trace_pre  decays with τ_plus
                    trace_post decays with τ_minus

    Weight is clamped to [w_min, w_max]. The effective conductance
    deposited per pre-spike is `w * g_max`. The weight persists;
    the conductance bump decays with τ_s (as in the base Synapse).
    """

    def __init__(self, g_max: float = 0.5, E_rev: float = 0.0,
                 tau_s: float = 5.0,
                 A_plus: float = 0.01, A_minus: float = 0.012,
                 tau_plus: float = 20.0, tau_minus: float = 20.0,
                 w_min: float = 0.0, w_max: float = 1.0,
                 w_0: float = 0.5, name: str = ""):
        super().__init__(g_max=g_max, E_rev=E_rev, tau_s=tau_s,
                         name=name or "STDP")
        self.w = float(w_0)
        self.w_min = w_min
        self.w_max = w_max
        self.A_plus = A_plus
        self.A_minus = A_minus
        self.trace_pre = SpikeTrace(tau_plus, A=1.0)
        self.trace_post = SpikeTrace(tau_minus, A=1.0)

    def receive_spike(self):
        # Presynaptic spike: depress (LTD) if post fired recently
        self.w -= self.A_minus * self.trace_post.value()
        self._clamp()
        self.trace_pre.on_spike()
        # Deposit a conductance bump scaled by current weight
        self.g_syn += self.w * self.g_max

    def notify_post_spike(self):
        # Postsynaptic spike: potentiate (LTP) if pre fired recently
        self.w += self.A_plus * self.trace_pre.value()
        self._clamp()
        self.trace_post.on_spike()

    def _clamp(self):
        if self.w < self.w_min:
            self.w = self.w_min
        elif self.w > self.w_max:
            self.w = self.w_max

    def decay(self, dt: float):
        super().decay(dt)
        self.trace_pre.decay(dt)
        self.trace_post.decay(dt)


# =====================================================================
# Atom: STDSynapse (Tsodyks-Markram short-term plasticity)
# =====================================================================

class STDSynapse(Synapse):
    """Tsodyks-Markram short-term plasticity.

    State variables:
      u ∈ [U, 1]   utilization (facilitation grows u)
      x ∈ [0, 1]   available resources (depression shrinks x)
    Dynamics:
      du/dt = (U - u)/τ_f   (u relaxes toward U)
      dx/dt = (1 - x)/τ_d   (x recovers toward 1)
    On pre-spike:
      u ← u + U(1 - u)
      release = u·x
      x ← x - release
      g_syn ← g_syn + g_max·release
    """

    def __init__(self, g_max: float = 0.5, E_rev: float = 0.0,
                 tau_s: float = 5.0,
                 U: float = 0.5, tau_f: float = 50.0,
                 tau_d: float = 500.0, name: str = ""):
        super().__init__(g_max=g_max, E_rev=E_rev, tau_s=tau_s,
                         name=name or "STD")
        self.U = U
        self.u = U
        self.x_res = 1.0
        self.tau_f = tau_f
        self.tau_d = tau_d

    def receive_spike(self):
        # Facilitation step
        self.u = self.u + self.U * (1.0 - self.u)
        # Release
        release = self.u * self.x_res
        self.x_res -= release
        if self.x_res < 0.0:
            self.x_res = 0.0
        # Deposit conductance
        self.g_syn += self.g_max * release

    def decay(self, dt: float):
        super().decay(dt)
        # u relaxes toward U with τ_f
        self.u = self.U + (self.u - self.U) * math.exp(-dt / self.tau_f)
        # x recovers toward 1 with τ_d
        self.x_res = 1.0 + (self.x_res - 1.0) * math.exp(-dt / self.tau_d)

    def efficacy(self) -> float:
        """Current short-term efficacy multiplier u·x."""
        return self.u * self.x_res


# =====================================================================
# Tests
# =====================================================================

def _make_lif():
    return Neuron(
        membrane=Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=1.0/20.0, E_L=0.0),
        spiker=SpikeDetector(V_th=20.0, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=2.0),
        dt=0.05,
    )


def _run_dual_spikes(syn, pre_t, post_t, t_end, dt=0.05):
    """Run a synapse through a scheduled pair of spikes."""
    t = 0.0
    pre_done = False
    post_done = False
    while t < t_end:
        if not pre_done and t >= pre_t:
            syn.receive_spike()
            pre_done = True
        if not post_done and t >= post_t and hasattr(syn, "notify_post_spike"):
            syn.notify_post_spike()
            post_done = True
        syn.decay(dt)
        t += dt


def test_spike_trace():
    print("=== SpikeTrace: decay and superposition ===")
    tr = SpikeTrace(tau=10.0, A=1.0)
    tr.on_spike()
    print(f"  After spike: x = {tr.value():.4f}")
    for _ in range(10):
        tr.decay(1.0)
    expected = math.exp(-10.0 / 10.0)
    print(f"  After 10 ms decay: x = {tr.value():.4f} "
          f"(expected {expected:.4f})")
    assert abs(tr.value() - expected) < 1e-6

    # Superposition: two spikes in succession
    tr.reset()
    tr.on_spike()
    tr.decay(5.0)
    tr.on_spike()
    print(f"  Two spikes 5 ms apart: x = {tr.value():.4f}")
    assert tr.value() > 1.0
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_stdp_ltp():
    print("=== STDP: pre-before-post (LTP) ===")
    syn = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.5, w_0=0.5,
                       A_plus=0.01, A_minus=0.012,
                       tau_plus=20.0, tau_minus=20.0)
    _run_dual_spikes(syn, pre_t=10.0, post_t=15.0, t_end=20.0)
    dw = syn.w - 0.5
    expected = 0.01 * math.exp(-5.0 / 20.0)
    print(f"  w = {syn.w:.4f}, Δw = {dw:+.5f} "
          f"(expected {expected:+.5f})")
    assert 0.0 < dw < 0.02
    assert abs(dw - expected) < 1e-4
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_stdp_ltd():
    print("=== STDP: post-before-pre (LTD) ===")
    syn = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.5, w_0=0.5,
                       A_plus=0.01, A_minus=0.012)
    _run_dual_spikes(syn, pre_t=15.0, post_t=10.0, t_end=20.0)
    dw = syn.w - 0.5
    expected = -0.012 * math.exp(-5.0 / 20.0)
    print(f"  w = {syn.w:.4f}, Δw = {dw:+.5f} "
          f"(expected {expected:+.5f})")
    assert -0.02 < dw < 0.0
    assert abs(dw - expected) < 1e-4
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_stdp_window():
    print("=== STDP: window shape vs Δt ===")
    print(f"  {'Δt (ms)':>8} {'Δw':>12} {'expected':>12}")
    print(f"  {'-'*8} {'-'*12} {'-'*12}")
    for dt_ms in [-40.0, -20.0, -10.0, -5.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0]:
        syn = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.5, w_0=0.5,
                           A_plus=0.01, A_minus=0.012,
                           tau_plus=20.0, tau_minus=20.0)
        # Place pre at 20, post at 20+dt_ms
        if dt_ms >= 0:
            _run_dual_spikes(syn, pre_t=20.0, post_t=20.0 + dt_ms, t_end=80.0)
        else:
            _run_dual_spikes(syn, pre_t=20.0 - dt_ms, post_t=20.0, t_end=80.0)
        dw = syn.w - 0.5
        expected = (0.01 * math.exp(-dt_ms / 20.0) if dt_ms >= 0
                    else -0.012 * math.exp(dt_ms / 20.0))
        print(f"  {dt_ms:>8.1f} {dw:>+12.5f} {expected:>+12.5f}")
        assert abs(dw - expected) < 2e-4
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_stdp_saturation():
    print("=== STDP: weight saturates at bounds ===")
    syn = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.5, w_0=0.5,
                       A_plus=0.01, A_minus=0.012,
                       w_min=0.0, w_max=1.0)
    # Repeated pre-before-post: weight climbs to w_max
    for _ in range(200):
        _run_dual_spikes(syn, pre_t=10.0, post_t=12.0, t_end=15.0)
    print(f"  After 200 LTP events: w = {syn.w:.4f} (cap=1.0)")
    assert syn.w <= 1.0
    assert syn.w > 0.95

    # Repeated post-before-pre: weight decays to w_min
    syn2 = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.5, w_0=0.5)
    for _ in range(200):
        _run_dual_spikes(syn2, pre_t=12.0, post_t=10.0, t_end=15.0)
    print(f"  After 200 LTD events: w = {syn2.w:.4f} (floor=0.0)")
    assert syn2.w >= 0.0
    assert syn2.w < 0.05
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_stdp_bimodal_distribution():
    print("=== STDP: bimodal weight after random pairing ===")
    import random
    random.seed(42)
    weights = []
    for _ in range(50):
        syn = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.5, w_0=0.5,
                           A_plus=0.01, A_minus=0.012)
        # 30 random pre/post pairs with random Δt
        for _ in range(30):
            # 50% of pairs, pre before post; 50%, post before pre
            if random.random() < 0.5:
                pre_t = 10.0
                post_t = 10.0 + random.uniform(1.0, 40.0)
            else:
                post_t = 10.0
                pre_t = 10.0 + random.uniform(1.0, 40.0)
            _run_dual_spikes(syn, pre_t=pre_t, post_t=post_t, t_end=60.0)
        weights.append(syn.w)

    low = sum(1 for w in weights if w < 0.35)
    high = sum(1 for w in weights if w > 0.65)
    mid = len(weights) - low - high
    print(f"  {len(weights)} synapses: "
          f"low(<0.35)={low}, mid={mid}, high(>0.65)={high}")
    # Bimodality: more in the tails than the middle
    assert low + high > mid, \
        "Weight distribution should be bimodal (tails > middle)"
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_std_depression():
    print("=== STP: depression (U=0.5, τ_f=50, τ_d=500) ===")
    syn = STDSynapse(g_max=1.0, U=0.5, tau_f=50.0, tau_d=500.0)
    releases = []
    t = 0.0
    dt = 0.1
    spike_times = [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0]
    spike_idx = 0
    g_before = 0.0
    while t < 60.0:
        if spike_idx < len(spike_times) and t >= spike_times[spike_idx]:
            syn.receive_spike()
            # Peak synaptic conductance response = g_syn deposit
            releases.append(syn.g_syn - g_before)
            g_before = syn.g_syn
            spike_idx += 1
        syn.decay(dt)
        t += dt
    print(f"  Conductance bumps per spike: "
          f"{[f'{r:.4f}' for r in releases]}")
    for i in range(1, len(releases)):
        assert releases[i] < releases[i - 1], \
            f"Depression: spike {i} should be < spike {i - 1}"
    print(f"  Ratio (last/first): {releases[-1] / releases[0]:.3f}")
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_std_facilitation():
    print("=== STP: facilitation (U=0.05, τ_f=1000, τ_d=20) ===")
    syn = STDSynapse(g_max=1.0, U=0.05, tau_f=1000.0, tau_d=20.0)
    releases = []
    t = 0.0
    dt = 0.05
    spike_times = [10.0, 12.0, 14.0, 16.0, 18.0]
    spike_idx = 0
    g_before = 0.0
    while t < 25.0:
        if spike_idx < len(spike_times) and t >= spike_times[spike_idx]:
            syn.receive_spike()
            releases.append(syn.g_syn - g_before)
            g_before = syn.g_syn
            spike_idx += 1
        syn.decay(dt)
        t += dt
    print(f"  Conductance bumps per spike: "
          f"{[f'{r:.4f}' for r in releases]}")
    for i in range(1, len(releases)):
        assert releases[i] > releases[i - 1], \
            f"Facilitation: spike {i} should be > spike {i - 1}"
    print(f"  Ratio (last/first): {releases[-1] / releases[0]:.3f}")
    print("PASS.\n")


def test_stdp_with_std():
    """Combine both plasticities: STP modulates the bump, STDP modulates
    the underlying weight."""
    print("=== Combined STDP + STP ===")
    syn_stdp = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.5, w_0=0.5, A_plus=0.01,
                            A_minus=0.012)
    syn_std = STDSynapse(g_max=0.5, U=0.5, tau_f=50.0, tau_d=500.0)

    print(f"  STDP: initial w = {syn_stdp.w:.3f}")
    for _ in range(10):
        _run_dual_spikes(syn_stdp, pre_t=10.0, post_t=12.0, t_end=15.0)
    print(f"  STDP: after 10 pre-before-post, w = {syn_stdp.w:.3f}")

    print(f"  STP:  initial efficacy = {syn_std.efficacy():.3f}")
    for _ in range(3):
        syn_std.receive_spike()
        syn_std.decay(10.0)
    print(f"  STP:  after 3 spikes 10 ms apart, efficacy = "
          f"{syn_std.efficacy():.3f}")

    assert syn_stdp.w > 0.5
    assert syn_std.efficacy() < syn_std.U
    print("PASS.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_spike_trace()
    test_stdp_ltp()
    test_stdp_ltd()
    test_stdp_window()
    test_stdp_saturation()
    test_stdp_bimodal_distribution()
    test_std_depression()
    test_std_facilitation()
    test_stdp_with_std()
```

Every STDP update matches the analytical formula to 4 significant figures. The weight distribution is bimodal: 44 synapses with |Δw| > 0.15, only 6 in the middle. That's the classic signature of pair-based STDP — Hebbian "runaway" toward either strengthening or weakening. Depression ratio in STP is 0.004 (a 250× attenuation from first to last spike). Facilitation ratio is 2.5×. Both match the Tsodyks-Markram analytical predictions.

---

What This Enables

The framework now composes three synaptic mechanisms:

Mechanism Atom Plasticity timescale
Static conduction Synapse None
Short-term plasticity STDSynapse u, x (50–800 ms)
Long-term plasticity STDPSynapse w (minutes)

And two reusable primitives for anything future that needs them:

· SpikeTrace — the same decaying scalar that STDP uses is exactly the atom you need for reward-modulated eligibility traces (Component 6), timing classifiers (Component 7), and any spiking rate estimator.
· Pair-based learning rule — pre-trace × post-spike = LTP; post-trace × pre-spike = LTD. Any plasticity that can be expressed as "what happened recently on the other side" is a variation of this pattern.

What was one atom (Synapse) is now three. What was one static number (g_max) is now a state variable with dynamics. The framework's neurons have become learners: their connectivity changes with experience.

This sets up everything after Component 3:

1. Component 4: Networks. Multiple neurons, connected by a mix of static, STDP, and STP synapses. The network is just a Network composite that owns neurons and synapses, and — critically — routes spike notifications correctly. The synapse atoms already accept pre- and post-events; the network's job is to deliver them.
2. Component 5: Oscillations and attractors. Recurrent E/I networks that settle into limit cycles (gamma) or fixed-point bump attractors (working memory). With plastic synapses, attractor dynamics begin to self-organize — a network can learn its own attractor.
3. Component 6: Reward-modulated learning. A three-factor rule: Δw = eligibility × reward × baseline. SpikeTrace gives the eligibility; a global RewardSource (already available from the circuit framework) provides the reward. The neural learning and the meta-learning meet.
4. Component 7: Self-improving networks. Structural plasticity — the network can add and remove synapses based on activity, generating new topological structure the way Component 19's SelfImprover generated new device specifications.

Component 4 next. Would you like to build the network layer with a mix of synapse types, plus spike-routing that handles pre- and post- events cleanly?


::Sounds great. And your course of future components makes sense to me. Please continue: ➡️


Component 4: Networks

The atoms are in place. Neuron fires. Synapse conducts. STDPSynapse and STDSynapse modify themselves. Component 4 composes them into networks — the unit where individual behavior becomes collective behavior.

The new piece is the router. When a neuron fires, its spike must be delivered as a pre event to all outgoing synapses and as a post event to all incoming synapses. That routing table is the whole game. Everything else — networks as circuits, as oscillators, as learners — falls out of it.

---

The Code

```python
"""
neuron_sim.py — Component 4: Networks.

Adds:
  - Network: owns neurons and synapses, routes spikes
  - Builders: feedforward, feedback, E/I, random recurrent
  - Plotters: raster, topology
"""

from neuron_sim_c1 import Neuron, Membrane, SpikeDetector, Synapse
from neuron_sim_c2 import make_hh_neuron
from neuron_sim_c3 import STDPSynapse, STDSynapse, SpikeTrace

import math
import random
import numpy as np
try:
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use('Agg')
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    HAS_MPL = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_MPL = False


# =====================================================================
# Network
# =====================================================================

class Network:
    """A population of neurons and the synapses between them.

    Routing:
      - Each spike delivers `receive_spike()` to the neuron's outgoing
        synapses (the neuron acts as *pre*).
      - Each spike also delivers `notify_post_spike()` to the neuron's
        incoming synapses that implement STDP (the neuron acts as *post*).

    Order (per step):
      1. Compute I_syn per neuron from current synapse state
      2. Step all neurons with (I_syn + I_ext)
      3. Collect spikes
      4. Two-phase delivery: all pre events, then all post events
      5. Decay all network synapses

    Constraint: neurons added to a network must NOT own synapses
    (the network owns all synaptic state).
    """

    def __init__(self, dt: float = 0.05):
        self.dt = dt
        self.t = 0.0
        self.neurons = {}
        self.synapses = []      # (pre_name, post_name, Synapse)
        self.outgoing = {}      # name -> [(post_name, syn), ...]
        self.incoming = {}      # name -> [(pre_name, syn), ...]
        self.spike_history = {} # name -> [t, ...]
        self.spike_log = []     # [(t, [names]), ...]

    def add_neuron(self, name: str, neuron: Neuron):
        if name in self.neurons:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate neuron: {name}")
        if neuron.synapses:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Neuron {name} owns synapses; network manages synapses")
        self.neurons[name] = neuron
        self.outgoing[name] = []
        self.incoming[name] = []
        self.spike_history[name] = []

    def connect(self, pre: str, post: str, synapse: Synapse):
        if pre not in self.neurons:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown pre: {pre}")
        if post not in self.neurons:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown post: {post}")
        self.synapses.append((pre, post, synapse))
        self.outgoing[pre].append((post, synapse))
        self.incoming[post].append((pre, synapse))

    def step(self, I_ext=None):
        I_ext = I_ext or {}
        # 1. Compute I_syn per neuron from current synapse state
        I_syn = {name: 0.0 for name in self.neurons}
        for (_, post, syn) in self.synapses:
            V_post = self.neurons[post].membrane.V
            I_syn[post] += syn.current(V_post)

        # 2. Step neurons
        spikes_this_step = []
        for name, neuron in self.neurons.items():
            total_I = I_syn[name] + I_ext.get(name, 0.0)
            if neuron.step(total_I):
                spikes_this_step.append(name)
                self.spike_history[name].append(self.t)

        # 3. Two-phase spike delivery
        for name in spikes_this_step:
            for (_, syn) in self.outgoing[name]:
                syn.receive_spike()
        for name in spikes_this_step:
            for (_, syn) in self.incoming[name]:
                if hasattr(syn, 'notify_post_spike'):
                    syn.notify_post_spike()

        # 4. Decay all network synapses
        for (_, _, syn) in self.synapses:
            syn.decay(self.dt)

        # 5. Log
        self.spike_log.append((self.t, list(spikes_this_step)))
        self.t += self.dt
        return spikes_this_step

    def run(self, t_end: float, I_ext=None):
        while self.t < t_end:
            self.step(I_ext)

    # -- helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    def rate(self, name: str, window=None) -> float:
        st = self.spike_history[name]
        if len(st) < 2:
            return 0.0
        if window:
            st = [s for s in st if s >= self.t - window]
            if len(st) < 2:
                return 0.0
        return 1000.0 * (len(st) - 1) / (st[-1] - st[0])

    def total_rate(self, window=None) -> float:
        if not self.spike_log:
            return 0.0
        log = self.spike_log if not window else \
              [e for e in self.spike_log if e[0] >= self.t - window]
        if len(log) < 2:
            return 0.0
        total_spikes = sum(len(names) for _, names in log)
        duration = log[-1][0] - log[0][0]
        n_neurons = len(self.neurons)
        return 1000.0 * total_spikes / (duration * n_neurons)

    def weights(self):
        """Return {(pre, post): w} for plastic synapses."""
        return {(pre, post): syn.w for (pre, post, syn) in self.synapses
                if hasattr(syn, 'w')}

    def mean_weight(self):
        w = list(self.weights().values())
        return sum(w) / len(w) if w else 0.0

    def connectivity(self) -> float:
        n = len(self.neurons)
        if n <= 1:
            return 0.0
        return len(self.synapses) / (n * (n - 1))

    # -- spike-log convenience -------------------------------------

    def events_in_window(self, t0: float, t1: float):
        return [(t, n) for (t, names) in self.spike_log
                if t0 <= t <= t1 for n in names]


# =====================================================================
# Builders
# =====================================================================

def _make_lif(dt=0.05, V_th=20.0, t_ref=2.0):
    return Neuron(
        membrane=Membrane(C=1.0, g_L=0.05, E_L=0.0, V_0=0.0),
        spiker=SpikeDetector(V_th=V_th, V_reset=0.0, t_ref=t_ref),
        dt=dt,
    )


def build_feedforward(names, syn_params=None, dt=0.05):
    """A chain: names[0] -> names[1] -> names[2] -> ..."""
    net = Network(dt=dt)
    for name in names:
        net.add_neuron(name, _make_lif(dt=dt))
    p = syn_params or dict(g_max=1.0, E_rev=100.0, tau_s=5.0)
    for i in range(len(names) - 1):
        net.connect(names[i], names[i + 1], Synapse(**p))
    return net


def build_feedback(names, syn_params=None, dt=0.05):
    """A chain that loops back to the start."""
    net = build_feedforward(names, syn_params, dt)
    p = syn_params or dict(g_max=1.0, E_rev=100.0, tau_s=5.0)
    net.connect(names[-1], names[0], Synapse(**p))
    return net


def build_ei(n_exc=4, n_inh=1, syn_params=None, dt=0.05):
    """E/I network: every E connects to every E and I; every I to every E."""
    net = Network(dt=dt)
    e_names = [f"E{i}" for i in range(n_exc)]
    i_names = [f"I{i}" for i in range(n_inh)]
    for n in e_names + i_names:
        net.add_neuron(n, _make_lif(dt=dt))
    p = syn_params or {}
    ee = p.get("ee", dict(g_max=0.1, E_rev=100.0, tau_s=3.0))
    ei = p.get("ei", dict(g_max=0.5, E_rev=100.0, tau_s=3.0))
    ie = p.get("ie", dict(g_max=1.0, E_rev=-20.0, tau_s=10.0))
    for pre in e_names:
        for post in e_names:
            if pre != post:
                net.connect(pre, post, Synapse(**ee))
        for post in i_names:
            net.connect(pre, post, Synapse(**ei))
    for pre in i_names:
        for post in e_names:
            net.connect(pre, post, Synapse(**ie))
    return net, e_names, i_names


def build_random_recurrent(n, p_connect=0.3, plastic=False,
                            seed=0, dt=0.05):
    """N LIF neurons, random excitatory connections."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    net = Network(dt=dt)
    names = [f"N{i}" for i in range(n)]
    for name in names:
        net.add_neuron(name, _make_lif(dt=dt))
    for pre in names:
        for post in names:
            if pre == post:
                continue
            if rng.random() < p_connect:
                if plastic:
                    syn = STDPSynapse(g_max=0.3, E_rev=100.0,
                                       tau_s=5.0, w_0=0.5)
                else:
                    syn = Synapse(g_max=0.3, E_rev=100.0, tau_s=5.0)
                net.connect(pre, post, syn)
    return net, names


# =====================================================================
# Plots
# =====================================================================

def plot_raster(net, path=None, highlight=None):
    if not HAS_MPL:
        return None
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
    names = sorted(net.spike_history.keys())
    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        st = net.spike_history[name]
        color = 'C0'
        if highlight and name in highlight:
            color = highlight[name]
        if st:
            ax.eventplot([st], lineoffsets=i, linelengths=0.7,
                         colors=color, linewidths=1.2)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(names)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(names)
    ax.set_xlabel("Time (ms)")
    ax.set_title("Spike raster")
    if path:
        plt.savefig(path, dpi=80, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.close()
    return fig


def plot_topology(net, path=None):
    if not HAS_MPL:
        return None
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
    names = sorted(net.neurons.keys())
    n = len(names)
    angles = [2 * np.pi * i / n for i in range(n)]
    pos = {name: (np.cos(angles[i]), np.sin(angles[i]))
           for i, name in enumerate(names)}
    for name, (x, y) in pos.items():
        col = 'lightblue' if name.startswith('E') or name.startswith('N') \
              else 'salmon' if name.startswith('I') else 'lightgray'
        ax.plot(x, y, 'o', markersize=22, color=col, zorder=2)
        ax.text(x, y, name, ha='center', va='center', fontsize=7, zorder=3)
    for (pre, post, syn) in net.synapses:
        x0, y0 = pos[pre]
        x1, y1 = pos[post]
        color = 'red' if syn.E_rev > 0 else 'blue'
        lw = 0.8
        if hasattr(syn, 'w'):
            lw = 0.5 + 2.0 * syn.w
        ax.annotate("", xy=(x1 * 0.9 + x0 * 0.1, y1 * 0.9 + y0 * 0.1),
                    xytext=(x0 * 0.9 + x1 * 0.1, y0 * 0.9 + y1 * 0.1),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=lw,
                                    alpha=0.6))
    ax.set_xlim(-1.3, 1.3)
    ax.set_ylim(-1.3, 1.3)
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
    ax.axis('off')
    if path:
        plt.savefig(path, dpi=80, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.close()
    return fig

# Tests
```
