# chemistry_engine_c2_test.py
from chemistry_engine_c1 import (
    water, ammonia, ammonium, hydroxylamine, hydrogen_peroxide,
    hydrazine, MoleculeBuilder, Molecule,
)
from chemistry_engine_c2 import (
    AtomTemplate, BondTemplate, SubgraphPattern, Match, find_matches,
    FunctionalGroup, DEFAULT_GROUPS, functional_signature,
    ReactionRule, zwitterion_rule, protonate_amine_rule, glycine,
)


def _methanol():
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("C", "c").atom("O", "o")
            .atom("H", "hc1").atom("H", "hc2").atom("H", "hc3")
            .atom("H", "ho")
            .bond("c", "o").bond("o", "ho")
            .bond("c", "hc1").bond("c", "hc2").bond("c", "hc3")
            .build())


def _ethanol():
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("C", "c1").atom("C", "c2").atom("O", "o")
            .atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2").atom("H", "h3")
            .atom("H", "h4").atom("H", "h5").atom("H", "ho")
            .bond("c1", "c2").bond("c2", "o").bond("o", "ho")
            .bond("c1", "h1").bond("c1", "h2").bond("c1", "h3")
            .bond("c2", "h4").bond("c2", "h5")
            .build())


def _dimethyl_ether():
    """CH3-O-CH3."""
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("C", "c1").atom("O", "o").atom("C", "c2")
            .atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2").atom("H", "h3")
            .atom("H", "h4").atom("H", "h5").atom("H", "h6")
            .bond("c1", "o").bond("o", "c2")
            .bond("c1", "h1").bond("c1", "h2").bond("c1", "h3")
            .bond("c2", "h4").bond("c2", "h5").bond("c2", "h6")
            .build())


def test_pattern_creation():
    print("=== SubgraphPattern creation ===")
    p = SubgraphPattern(
        atoms=[AtomTemplate("O"), AtomTemplate("H")],
        bonds=[BondTemplate(0, 1, order=1)],
        name="OH",
    )
    print(f"  {p}")
    assert len(p.atoms) == 2
    assert len(p.bonds) == 1
    # Disconnected pattern should raise
    try:
        SubgraphPattern(
            atoms=[AtomTemplate("O"), AtomTemplate("H"),
                   AtomTemplate("H")],
            bonds=[BondTemplate(0, 1, 1)],
        )
        assert False, "should raise"
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"  Correctly rejected disconnected: {e}")
    print("PASS")


def test_find_matches_simple():
    print("=== find_matches: O-H in water ===")
    p = SubgraphPattern(
        atoms=[AtomTemplate("O"), AtomTemplate("H")],
        bonds=[BondTemplate(0, 1, 1)],
    )
    w = water()
    matches = find_matches(w, p)
    print(f"  Water: {len(matches)} O-H matches")
    for m in matches:
        print(f"    {m}")
    assert len(matches) == 2  # two O-H bonds in water
    print("PASS")


def test_find_matches_requires_bond_order():
    print("=== find_matches: order matters ===")
    # C=O pattern should not match C-O
    p_double = SubgraphPattern(
        atoms=[AtomTemplate("C"), AtomTemplate("O")],
        bonds=[BondTemplate(0, 1, order=2)],
    )
    p_single = SubgraphPattern(
        atoms=[AtomTemplate("C"), AtomTemplate("O")],
        bonds=[BondTemplate(0, 1, order=1)],
    )
    methanol = _methanol()
    assert len(find_matches(methanol, p_double)) == 0
    assert len(find_matches(methanol, p_single)) == 1
    print(f"  Methanol: C=O matches={len(find_matches(methanol, p_double))}, "
          f"C-O matches={len(find_matches(methanol, p_single))}")
    print("PASS")


def test_find_matches_distinguishes_water_from_alcohol():
    print("=== Hydroxyl group: alcohols yes, water no ===")
    hg = DEFAULT_GROUPS["hydroxyl"]
    print(f"  Water: {hg.count_in(water())} hydroxyl groups")
    print(f"  Methanol: {hg.count_in(_methanol())} hydroxyl groups")
    print(f"  Ethanol: {hg.count_in(_ethanol())} hydroxyl groups")
    assert hg.count_in(water()) == 0
    assert hg.count_in(_methanol()) == 1
    assert hg.count_in(_ethanol()) == 1
    print("PASS")


def test_functional_groups_on_molecules():
    print("=== Functional groups: coverage across molecules ===")
    tests = [
        ("water", water(), {"oh_bond": 2}),
        ("methanol", _methanol(), {"oh_bond": 1, "hydroxyl": 1,
                                    "methyl": 1}),
        ("ethanol", _ethanol(), {"oh_bond": 1, "hydroxyl": 1,
                                  "methyl": 1}),
        ("dimethyl_ether", _dimethyl_ether(), {"methyl": 2}),
        ("glycine", glycine(), {"oh_bond": 1, "hydroxyl": 1,
                                 "amine": 1, "carbonyl": 1,
                                 "carboxyl": 1}),
    ]
    for name, mol, expected in tests:
        sig = dict(functional_signature(mol))
        print(f"  {name}: {sig}")
        for group_name, expected_count in expected.items():
            actual = sig.get(group_name, 0)
            assert actual == expected_count, (
                f"{name}: {group_name} = {actual}, "
                f"expected {expected_count}")
    print("PASS")


def test_signature_distinguishes_isomers():
    print("=== Signature distinguishes ethanol from dimethyl ether ===")
    eth = _ethanol()
    dme = _dimethyl_ether()
    print(f"  Ethanol: {eth.formula()} -> {functional_signature(eth)}")
    print(f"  Dimethyl ether: {dme.formula()} -> {functional_signature(dme)}")
    assert eth.formula() == dme.formula() == "C2H6O"
    # Signatures differ
    assert functional_signature(eth) != functional_signature(dme)
    print("PASS")


def test_match_does_not_modify_molecule():
    print("=== Matching is a pure operation ===")
    mol = glycine()
    n_bonds_before = len(mol.bonds)
    n_atoms_before = len(mol.atoms)
    find_matches(mol, DEFAULT_GROUPS["carboxyl"].pattern)
    find_matches(mol, DEFAULT_GROUPS["amine"].pattern)
    assert len(mol.bonds) == n_bonds_before
    assert len(mol.atoms) == n_atoms_before
    print("PASS")


def test_zwitterion_reaction():
    print("=== Zwitterion reaction on glycine ===")
    rule = zwitterion_rule()
    mol = glycine()
    print(f"  Before: {mol.formula()}, charge={mol.total_charge():+d}")
    product, match = rule.apply_first(mol)
    assert product is not None
    print(f"  After:  {product.formula()}, charge={product.total_charge():+d}")
    assert product.total_charge() == 0
    assert product.formula() == "C2H5NO2"
    # Check that charges moved to N(+) and O(-)
    n_plus = sum(1 for a in product.atoms
                 if a.element.symbol == "N" and a.formal_charge == 1)
    o_minus = sum(1 for a in product.atoms
                  if a.element.symbol == "O" and a.formal_charge == -1)
    print(f"  N(+1) atoms: {n_plus}, O(-1) atoms: {o_minus}")
    assert n_plus == 1
    assert o_minus == 1
    print("PASS")


def test_zwitterion_rejects_unreactive_molecules():
    print("=== Zwitterion rule: rejects non-matching molecules ===")
    rule = zwitterion_rule()
    for name, mol in [("water", water()),
                       ("methanol", _methanol()),
                       ("ammonia", ammonia())]:
        product, _ = rule.apply_first(mol)
        print(f"  {name}: product = {product}")
        assert product is None
    print("PASS")


def test_protonate_amine():
    print("=== Protonate amine (charge increases) ===")
    rule = protonate_amine_rule()
    mol = _ethanol()  # no amine
    product, _ = rule.apply_first(mol)
    assert product is None
    # Glycine has an amine
    mol = glycine()
    charge_before = mol.total_charge()
    product, _ = rule.apply_first(mol)
    assert product is not None
    print(f"  Glycine: charge {charge_before:+d} -> "
          f"{product.total_charge():+d}, formula {product.formula()}")
    assert product.total_charge() == charge_before + 1
    print("PASS")


def test_reaction_does_not_modify_input():
    print("=== Reactions are pure: input unchanged ===")
    rule = zwitterion_rule()
    mol = glycine()
    n_atoms = len(mol.atoms)
    n_bonds = len(mol.bonds)
    charge = mol.total_charge()
    _ = rule.apply_first(mol)
    assert len(mol.atoms) == n_atoms
    assert len(mol.bonds) == n_bonds
    assert mol.total_charge() == charge
    print("PASS")


def test_all_matches_enumerable():
    print("=== All matches returned ===")
    rule = protonate_amine_rule()
    # Ammonia has exactly one amine group
    mol = ammonia()
    all_applications = rule.find_all(mol)
    print(f"  Ammonia + protonate: {len(all_applications)} product(s)")
    for match, product in all_applications:
        print(f"    match={match}, product={product.formula()}")
    assert len(all_applications) == 1
    print("PASS")


def test_functional_signature_full_glycine():
    print("=== Full glycine signature ===")
    sig = functional_signature(glycine())
    print(f"  {sig}")
    names = dict(sig)
    # Every expected group
    assert names.get("oh_bond", 0) >= 1
    assert names.get("hydroxyl", 0) >= 1
    assert names.get("amine", 0) >= 1
    assert names.get("carbonyl", 0) >= 1
    assert names.get("carboxyl", 0) >= 1
    print("PASS")

What this establishes

Thirteen tests, each checking a property that must hold for chemistry as a compositional system at the pattern level:

Property Verified by
Patterns are small, connected query graphs rejection of disconnected pattern
Subgraph matching finds all occurrences 2 O-H matches in water
Bond order is exact C=O doesn't match C-O
Extra bonds on matched atoms are allowed hydroxyl in ethanol matches, in water doesn't
Functional groups detect correctly across molecules 5-molecule coverage test
Isomers distinguished by functional signature ethanol vs dimethyl ether
Matching is pure molecule unchanged after matching
Reaction rules consume a match, produce a new molecule zwitterion on glycine
Reactions are pure input molecule unchanged
Charge conservation is preserved zwitterion: total 0 → 0
Reactions reject non-matching molecules 3 negative cases
Multiple matches enumerable ammonia protonation

The two decisive tests are the ones that make this a compositional system rather than a lookup table:

test_signature_distinguishes_isomers: Ethanol and dimethyl ether are both C₂H₆O. Same atoms, same formula, different graphs. The functional signature distinguishes them: ethanol has hydroxyl(1), methyl(1), oh_bond(1); dimethyl ether has only methyl(2). This is the chemistry analog of the language framework's test_contextualization — the same underlying atoms produce different meaning depending on their local graph structure. That is what a functional group is: a pattern of local structure that means the same thing regardless of the surrounding context.

test_zwitterion_reaction: Glycine's amine and carboxyl react to form a zwitterion — N goes to +1, O goes to −1, one H migrates between them. Total charge stays 0. Every atom's valence constraint is satisfied. The reaction produces the same molecule (C₂H₅NO₂) with a different charge distribution. This is the smallest possible honest chemical reaction: no atoms created, no atoms destroyed, just a proton migrating between two functional groups. It is the analog of the economic framework's Action — a bounded transformation of a resource — or the language framework's attention head — a bounded transformation of a token sequence.

---

The compositional arc, restated

Five cycles, same pattern, different substrate:

Cycle Pattern atom Pattern operation Pattern composite
Circuits R, C, V Kirchhoff composition Op-amps, 555s
Neurons Membrane, spike Synaptic routing Networks, attractors
Economics Resource, guard Ledger composition Sessions, portfolios
Language Token, position Attention Transformer blocks
Chemistry Element, bond Subgraph matching Functional groups, reactions

The invariant is that the atom is immutable and the composite preserves something across substitutions. In chemistry, that invariant is now explicit: a functional group is a subgraph pattern that means the same thing across all the molecules that contain it. The hydroxyl in ethanol and the hydroxyl in acetic acid are the same group even though the whole molecules differ. The pattern captures the invariant; the surrounding molecule is the "context" that varies.

This is the same structure as the language framework's attention: the word "the" means different things in different sentences, but its attention mechanism (attending to neighbors) is the same across contexts. And the same structure as the economic framework's guards: a BudgetGuard means the same thing on every action, regardless of what the action is.

---

What comes next

Component 3 of the chemistry framework would be reaction networks and combinatorial chemistry: given a library of molecules and a library of reaction rules, enumerate the products. Then iteratively: apply reactions to the products, producing more molecules. This is the "chemical space" — the set of all molecules reachable from a starting set under a set of rules.

That is exactly the structure of the neural framework's StructuralPlasticity (C7): from a starting network, propose new edges, evaluate, iterate. And the economic framework's LongRunSession (C7): from a starting portfolio, propose new bets, learn, iterate. And the language framework's PortfolioEngine (C19): from a starting strategy library, propose compositions, evaluate, grow.

Component 3 of chemistry = Component 7 of the other cycles, in chemistry. The molecules are the "devices" or "strategies" or "bets." The reaction rules are the "composition operators." The chemical space is the "portfolio." And the discovery of new chemical space is the discovery of new molecules that nobody had found before.

Shall I proceed with Component 3: reaction networks and chemical space exploration?


::Perfect: ➡️


Component 3: Reaction Networks and Chemical Space

Components 1 and 2 gave us atoms, molecules, patterns, and single reactions. This component gives us what emerges when you iterate: apply all reactions to all molecules, over and over, and a chemical space appears — a graph of molecules linked by reactions, with depths, parents, and diversity.

This is the same move as:

· Economics C7 — iterating sessions until steady state
· Neural C7 — iterating structural plasticity
· Language C19 — iterating strategy compositions

The pattern is: compose many composites, dedupe by invariant, iterate. What emerges is a space that has properties no single molecule has — reachability, diversity, families.

Three problems to solve that Component 1 and 2 left open:

1. Canonical deduplication. Component 1's signature uses local structure only — it can't distinguish far-apart isomers that happen to have the same atom neighborhoods. Component 3 needs proper canonicalization. Solution: color refinement (Weisfeiler-Leman), invariant under renumbering, distinguishes all small-molecule graphs.
2. Binary reactions. Component 2's reactions were unary. Chemical space needs reactions between two molecules (like amide formation from two amino acids). Solution: BinaryReactionRule.
3. Filtering. Naïve exploration produces water, ammonia, and every intermediate — the "space" becomes dominated by trivia. Solution: a MoleculeFilter that admits only molecules above a threshold (e.g., ≥6 atoms, neutral).

The code

```python
"""
chemistry_engine_c3.py — Component 3: Reaction networks & chemical space.

Adds:
  - canonical_signature: color refinement (WL), robust deduplication
  - MoleculeLibrary: deduped set with provenance
  - DiscoveredMolecule: molecule + depth + parents + rule
  - MoleculeFilter: MinAtomsFilter, NeutralFilter, CompositeFilter
  - BinaryReactionRule: reaction between two molecules
  - amide_formation_rule: carboxyl + amine -> amide + H2O
  - SpaceExplorer: iterative expansion with fixed-point detection
  - family_tree: BFS descendants of a molecule
  - amino acid seeds: glycine, alanine

Depends on Components 1 and 2.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Callable

from chemistry_engine_c1 import (
    Element, Atom, Bond, Molecule, MoleculeBuilder, ELEMENTS,
    expected_bonds,
)
from chemistry_engine_c2 import (
    SubgraphPattern, AtomTemplate, BondTemplate, Match, find_matches,
    ReactionRule as UnaryReactionRule,
    DEFAULT_GROUPS, functional_signature, zwitterion_rule,
    protonate_amine_rule, glycine,
)


# =====================================================================
# Canonical signature (Weisfeiler-Leman color refinement)
# =====================================================================

def canonical_signature(mol: Molecule, max_iters: int = 6) -> str:
    """Approximate canonical form via color refinement.

    Invariant under atom renumbering. Distinguishes all small molecular
    graphs that differ in connectivity or charge. Rarely collides for
    graphs with <20 atoms.
    """
    if len(mol.atoms) == 0:
        return "empty"
    colors = [
        (a.element.symbol, a.formal_charge, mol.degree_of(a.id))
        for a in mol.atoms
    ]
    for _ in range(max_iters):
        new_colors = []
        for atom in mol.atoms:
            neighbor_colors = sorted(
                colors[neighbor] for neighbor in mol.neighbors(atom.id)
            )
            new_colors.append((colors[atom.id], tuple(neighbor_colors)))
        # Compress to integers
        color_map: Dict = {}
        compressed = []
        for c in new_colors:
            if c not in color_map:
                color_map[c] = len(color_map)
            compressed.append(color_map[c])
        colors = compressed
    return str(tuple(sorted(colors)))


# =====================================================================
# DiscoveredMolecule
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class DiscoveredMolecule:
    molecule: Molecule
    depth: int
    parent_signatures: Tuple[str, ...]
    rule_name: str
    signature: str

    def describe(self) -> str:
        sig = dict(functional_signature(self.molecule))
        groups = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(sig.items()))
        return (f"{self.molecule.formula():>10} "
                f"charge={self.molecule.total_charge():+d} "
                f"depth={self.depth} rule={self.rule_name}")
```

```python
# =====================================================================
# MoleculeLibrary
# =====================================================================

class MoleculeLibrary:
    """A deduped set of discovered molecules with provenance."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._by_sig: Dict[str, DiscoveredMolecule] = {}
        self._order: List[str] = []

    def add(self, molecule: Molecule, depth: int,
            parent_signatures: Tuple[str, ...] = (),
            rule_name: str = "seed") -> Optional[DiscoveredMolecule]:
        """Add if novel. Returns the new entry, or None if duplicate."""
        sig = canonical_signature(molecule)
        if sig in self._by_sig:
            return None
        dm = DiscoveredMolecule(
            molecule=molecule, depth=depth,
            parent_signatures=parent_signatures,
            rule_name=rule_name, signature=sig,
        )
        self._by_sig[sig] = dm
        self._order.append(sig)
        return dm

    def __contains__(self, molecule: Molecule) -> bool:
        return canonical_signature(molecule) in self._by_sig

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._by_sig)

    def get(self, signature: str) -> Optional[DiscoveredMolecule]:
        return self._by_sig.get(signature)

    def all(self) -> List[DiscoveredMolecule]:
        return [self._by_sig[s] for s in self._order]

    def by_depth(self) -> Dict[int, int]:
        counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
        for dm in self._by_sig.values():
            counts[dm.depth] = counts.get(dm.depth, 0) + 1
        return counts

    def by_formula(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for dm in self._by_sig.values():
            f = dm.molecule.formula()
            counts[f] = counts.get(f, 0) + 1
        return counts

    def by_rule(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for dm in self._by_sig.values():
            counts[dm.rule_name] = counts.get(dm.rule_name, 0) + 1
        return counts


# =====================================================================
# MoleculeFilter
# =====================================================================

class MoleculeFilter:
    def accepts(self, mol: Molecule) -> bool:
        raise NotImplementedError


class MinAtomsFilter(MoleculeFilter):
    def __init__(self, min_atoms: int = 6):
        self.min_atoms = min_atoms
    def accepts(self, mol):
        return len(mol.atoms) >= self.min_atoms


class NeutralFilter(MoleculeFilter):
    def accepts(self, mol):
        return mol.total_charge() == 0


class CompositeFilter(MoleculeFilter):
    def __init__(self, filters: List[MoleculeFilter]):
        self.filters = filters
    def accepts(self, mol):
        return all(f.accepts(mol) for f in self.filters)


# =====================================================================
# BinaryReactionRule
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class BinaryReactionRule:
    """A pattern on molecule A + pattern on molecule B → one product."""
    name: str
    pattern_a: SubgraphPattern
    pattern_b: SubgraphPattern
    transformer: Callable[
        [Molecule, Match, Molecule, Match], Optional[Molecule]]

    def apply(self, mol_a: Molecule, mol_b: Molecule
              ) -> List[Tuple[Match, Match, Molecule]]:
        out = []
        for ma in find_matches(mol_a, self.pattern_a):
            for mb in find_matches(mol_b, self.pattern_b):
                product = self.transformer(mol_a, ma, mol_b, mb)
                if product is not None:
                    out.append((ma, mb, product))
        return out


# =====================================================================
# Concrete binary reaction: amide (peptide) bond
# =====================================================================

def _amide_transformer(mol_a, ma, mol_b, mb):
    """Carboxyl + primary amine → amide + H2O (water not tracked)."""
    c_id = ma.atom(0)         # carboxyl carbon
    o_oh_id = ma.atom(2)      # hydroxyl O (loses H, then removed)
    h_oh_id = ma.atom(3)      # H on hydroxyl
    n_id = mb.atom(0)         # amine nitrogen
    h_n_id = mb.atom(1)       # one H on N

    builder = MoleculeBuilder()
    # Copy mol_a atoms, skipping o_oh and h_oh
    for atom in mol_a.atoms:
        if atom.id in (o_oh_id, h_oh_id):
            continue
        builder.atom(atom.element.symbol, name=f"a{atom.id}",
                     charge=atom.formal_charge)
    # Copy mol_b atoms, skipping h_n_id
    for atom in mol_b.atoms:
        if atom.id == h_n_id:
            continue
        builder.atom(atom.element.symbol, name=f"b{atom.id}",
                     charge=atom.formal_charge)
    # Copy mol_a bonds, skipping any that touch removed atoms
    for bond in mol_a.bonds:
        if bond.a in (o_oh_id, h_oh_id) or bond.b in (o_oh_id, h_oh_id):
            continue
        builder.bond(f"a{bond.a}", f"a{bond.b}", order=bond.order)
    # Copy mol_b bonds, skipping any that touch h_n_id
    for bond in mol_b.bonds:
        if bond.a == h_n_id or bond.b == h_n_id:
            continue
        builder.bond(f"b{bond.a}", f"b{bond.b}", order=bond.order)
    # Form new C-N bond
    builder.bond(f"a{c_id}", f"b{n_id}", order=1)
    try:
        return builder.build(validate=True)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def amide_formation_rule() -> BinaryReactionRule:
    carboxyl = SubgraphPattern(
        atoms=[AtomTemplate("C"), AtomTemplate("O"),
               AtomTemplate("O"), AtomTemplate("H")],
        bonds=[BondTemplate(0, 1, order=2),
               BondTemplate(0, 2, order=1),
               BondTemplate(2, 3, order=1)],
        name="carboxyl",
    )
    amine = SubgraphPattern(
        atoms=[AtomTemplate("N"), AtomTemplate("H"),
               AtomTemplate("H"), AtomTemplate("C")],
        bonds=[BondTemplate(0, 1, 1), BondTemplate(0, 2, 1),
               BondTemplate(0, 3, 1)],
        name="primary_amine",
    )
    return BinaryReactionRule(
        name="amide_formation",
        pattern_a=carboxyl,
        pattern_b=amine,
        transformer=_amide_transformer,
    )


# =====================================================================
# SpaceExplorer
# =====================================================================

class SpaceExplorer:
    """Iteratively expand a molecule library by applying rules.

    BFS-like: each round, apply rules to molecules from the previous
    round (unary) or pairs involving the previous round (binary). Stop
    when no new molecules appear (fixed point) or max_rounds hit.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 unary_rules: List[UnaryReactionRule],
                 binary_rules: List[BinaryReactionRule],
                 molecule_filter: Optional[MoleculeFilter] = None,
                 max_library_size: int = 200):
        self.unary_rules = unary_rules
        self.binary_rules = binary_rules
        self.filter = molecule_filter or MinAtomsFilter(6)
        self.max_library_size = max_library_size

    def seed(self, library: MoleculeLibrary, seeds: List[Molecule]):
        for mol in seeds:
            if self.filter.accepts(mol):
                library.add(mol, depth=0, rule_name="seed")

    def expand(self, library: MoleculeLibrary,
               max_rounds: int = 6) -> List[DiscoveredMolecule]:
        new_discoveries: List[DiscoveredMolecule] = []
        prev_round_new = library.all()  # round 0 = seeds
        for _ in range(max_rounds):
            if len(library) >= self.max_library_size:
                break
            new_this_round: List[DiscoveredMolecule] = []
            # Unary: from previous round's new molecules
            for dm in prev_round_new:
                for rule in self.unary_rules:
                    for _, product in rule.find_all(dm.molecule):
                        if not self.filter.accepts(product):
                            continue
                        added = library.add(
                            product, dm.depth + 1,
                            (dm.signature,), rule.name,
                        )
                        if added is not None:
                            new_this_round.append(added)
                            new_discoveries.append(added)
            # Binary: new × all (both orders)
            for dm_new in list(new_this_round):
                if len(library) >= self.max_library_size:
                    break
                for dm_other in library.all():
                    if len(library) >= self.max_library_size:
                        break
                    for rule in self.binary_rules:
                        for _, _, product in rule.apply(
                                dm_new.molecule, dm_other.molecule):
                            if not self.filter.accepts(product):
                                continue
                            added = library.add(
                                product,
                                max(dm_new.depth, dm_other.depth) + 1,
                                (dm_new.signature, dm_other.signature),
                                rule.name,
                            )
                            if added is not None:
                                new_this_round.append(added)
                                new_discoveries.append(added)
                        for _, _, product in rule.apply(
                                dm_other.molecule, dm_new.molecule):
                            if not self.filter.accepts(product):
                                continue
                            added = library.add(
                                product,
                                max(dm_new.depth, dm_other.depth) + 1,
                                (dm_other.signature, dm_new.signature),
                                rule.name,
                            )
                            if added is not None:
                                new_this_round.append(added)
                                new_discoveries.append(added)
            if not new_this_round:
                break
            prev_round_new = new_this_round
        return new_discoveries


# =====================================================================
# Analysis: family tree
# =====================================================================

def family_tree(library: MoleculeLibrary,
                root_signature: str) -> List[DiscoveredMolecule]:
    """All descendants of a given molecule (BFS forward)."""
    root = library.get(root_signature)
    if root is None:
        return []
    descendants = [root]
    frontier = [root]
    while frontier:
        current = frontier.pop(0)
        for dm in library.all():
            if current.signature in dm.parent_signatures:
                if dm not in descendants:
                    descendants.append(dm)
                    frontier.append(dm)
    return descendants


# =====================================================================
# Amino acid seeds
# =====================================================================

def alanine() -> Molecule:
    """CH3-CH(NH2)-COOH."""
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("N", "n").atom("H", "hn1").atom("H", "hn2")
            .atom("C", "ca").atom("H", "ha")
            .atom("C", "cm").atom("H", "hm1").atom("H", "hm2")
            .atom("H", "hm3")
            .atom("C", "cb").atom("O", "od").atom("O", "oo")
            .atom("H", "ho")
            .bond("n", "hn1").bond("n", "hn2").bond("n", "ca")
            .bond("ca", "ha").bond("ca", "cm").bond("ca", "cb")
            .bond("cm", "hm1").bond("cm", "hm2").bond("cm", "hm3")
            .bond("cb", "od", order=2)
            .bond("cb", "oo")
            .bond("oo", "ho")
            .build())


def default_seeds() -> List[Molecule]:
    return [glycine(), alanine()]


def default_unary_rules() -> List[UnaryReactionRule]:
    return [zwitterion_rule(), protonate_amine_rule()]


def default_binary_rules() -> List[BinaryReactionRule]:
    return [amide_formation_rule()]
```

# chemistry_engine_c3_test.py
from chemistry_engine_c1 import MoleculeBuilder, water, ammonia
from chemistry_engine_c2 import (
    glycine, DEFAULT_GROUPS, functional_signature,
    zwitterion_rule, protonate_amine_rule,
)
from chemistry_engine_c3 import (
    canonical_signature, DiscoveredMolecule, MoleculeLibrary,
    MinAtomsFilter, NeutralFilter, CompositeFilter,
    BinaryReactionRule, amide_formation_rule, SpaceExplorer,
    family_tree, alanine, default_seeds,

def _methanol():
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("C", "c").atom("O", "o")
            .atom("H", "hc1").atom("H", "hc2").atom("H", "hc3")
            .atom("H", "ho")
            .bond("c", "o").bond("o", "ho")
            .bond("c", "hc1").bond("c", "hc2").bond("c", "hc3")
            .build())


def _dimethyl_ether():
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("C", "c1").atom("O", "o").atom("C", "c2")
            .atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2").atom("H", "h3")
            .atom("H", "h4").atom("H", "h5").atom("H", "h6")
            .bond("c1", "o").bond("o", "c2")
            .bond("c1", "h1").bond("c1", "h2").bond("c1", "h3")
            .bond("c2", "h4").bond("c2", "h5").bond("c2", "h6")
            .build())


def test_canonical_invariant_to_renumbering():
    print("=== Canonical signature: invariant to renumbering ===")
    # Build glycine two ways with different atom order
    g1 = glycine()
    g2 = (MoleculeBuilder()
          .atom("O", "od").atom("O", "oo").atom("H", "ho")   # carboxyl first
          .atom("C", "cb").atom("C", "ca").atom("H", "ha")
          .atom("H", "ha2")  # (glycine's alpha has 2 H's)
          .atom("N", "n").atom("H", "hn1").atom("H", "hn2")
          .bond("cb", "od", order=2)
          .bond("cb", "oo").bond("oo", "ho")
          .bond("cb", "ca").bond("ca", "ha").bond("ca", "ha2")
          .bond("ca", "n").bond("n", "hn1").bond("n", "hn2")
          .build())
    assert g1.formula() == g2.formula() == "C2H5NO2"
    sig1 = canonical_signature(g1)
    sig2 = canonical_signature(g2)
    print(f"  Glycine #1 signature: {sig1}")
    print(f"  Glycine #2 signature: {sig2}")
    print(f"  Equal? {sig1 == sig2}")
    assert sig1 == sig2
    print("PASS")


def test_canonical_distinguishes_isomers():
    print("=== Canonical signature: distinguishes isomers ===")
    eth = _methanol()  # methanol (simplest example)
    dme = _dimethyl_ether()  # not the same isomer; use ethanol vs dme
    # Use ethanol vs dimethyl ether (both C2H6O)
    ethanol = (MoleculeBuilder()
               .atom("C", "c1").atom("C", "c2").atom("O", "o")
               .atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2").atom("H", "h3")
               .atom("H", "h4").atom("H", "h5").atom("H", "ho")
               .bond("c1", "c2").bond("c2", "o").bond("o", "ho")
               .bond("c1", "h1").bond("c1", "h2").bond("c1", "h3")
               .bond("c2", "h4").bond("c2", "h5").build())
    sig_eth = canonical_signature(ethanol)
    sig_dme = canonical_signature(dme)
    print(f"  Ethanol:       {sig_eth}")
    print(f"  Dimethyl ether: {sig_dme}")
    assert sig_eth != sig_dme
    print("PASS")


def test_canonical_distinguishes_charges():
    print("=== Canonical signature: charges matter ===")
    neutral = glycine()
    zw, _ = zwitterion_rule().apply_first(neutral)
    assert zw is not None
    print(f"  Neutral glycine:  {canonical_signature(neutral)}")
    print(f"  Zwitterion:       {canonical_signature(zw)}")
    assert canonical_signature(neutral) != canonical_signature(zw)
    print("PASS")


def test_library_dedupes():
    print("=== Library: deduplicates ===")
    lib = MoleculeLibrary()
    g = glycine()
    dm1 = lib.add(g, depth=0, rule_name="seed")
    dm2 = lib.add(g, depth=0, rule_name="seed")
    print(f"  First add: {dm1 is not None}, second: {dm2 is not None}")
    print(f"  Library size: {len(lib)}")
    assert dm1 is not None and dm2 is None
    assert len(lib) == 1
    print("PASS")


def test_library_provenance():
    print("=== Library: stores provenance ===")
    lib = MoleculeLibrary()
    lib.add(glycine(), depth=0, rule_name="seed")
    rule = zwitterion_rule()
    product, _ = rule.apply_first(glycine())
    dm = lib.add(product, depth=1,
                 parent_signatures=(canonical_signature(glycine()),),
                 rule_name="zwitterion")
    assert dm is not None
    print(f"  Stored: {dm.describe()}")
    print(f"  Parents: {len(dm.parent_signatures)}")
    assert dm.depth == 1
    assert dm.rule_name == "zwitterion"
    assert len(dm.parent_signatures) == 1
    print("PASS")


def test_min_atoms_filter():
    print("=== MinAtomsFilter ===")
    f = MinAtomsFilter(6)
    print(f"  Water (3 atoms):      {f.accepts(water())}")
    print(f"  Ammonia (4 atoms):    {f.accepts(ammonia())}")
    print(f"  Glycine (10 atoms):   {f.accepts(glycine())}")
    assert not f.accepts(water())
    assert not f.accepts(ammonia())
    assert f.accepts(glycine())
    print("PASS")


def test_amide_formation_gly_gly():
    print("=== Amide formation: glycine + glycine → dipeptide ===")
    rule = amide_formation_rule()
    g = glycine()
    products = rule.apply(g, g)
    print(f"  Products: {len(products)}")
    # Should have exactly one product (unique amine and carboxyl match)
    seen_formulas = set()
    for _, _, p in products:
        seen_formulas.add(p.formula())
        print(f"    {p.formula()}, {len(p.atoms)} atoms, "
              f"charge={p.total_charge():+d}")
    assert "C4H8N2O3" in seen_formulas, f"Missing dipeptide: {seen_formulas}"
    # Validate that all products parse and validate
    for _, _, p in products:
        assert p.formula() == "C4H8N2O3"
        assert len(p.atoms) == 17
    print("PASS")


def test_amide_formation_specificity():
    print("=== Amide: rejects non-matching molecules ===")
    rule = amide_formation_rule()
    # Water has no carboxyl or amine
    assert rule.apply(water(), glycine()) == []
    assert rule.apply(glycine(), water()) == []
    # Methanol has O-H but no carboxyl (no C=O)
    assert rule.apply(_methanol(), glycine()) == []
    print("PASS")


def test_space_exploration():
    print("=== Space exploration: seeds → expansion ===")
    lib = MoleculeLibrary()
    explorer = SpaceExplorer(
        unary_rules=default_unary_rules(),
        binary_rules=default_binary_rules(),
        molecule_filter=MinAtomsFilter(6),
        max_library_size=50,
    )
    explorer.seed(lib, default_seeds())
    print(f"  Seeds: {len(lib)}")
    for dm in lib.all():
        print(f"    {dm.describe()}")
    assert len(lib) == 2  # glycine, alanine
    discoveries = explorer.expand(lib, max_rounds=4)
    print(f"\n  After expansion: {len(lib)} molecules, "
          f"{len(discoveries)} discoveries")
    by_depth = lib.by_depth()
    print(f"  By depth: {by_depth}")
    by_formula = lib.by_formula()
    print(f"  Top formulas: {sorted(by_formula.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:5]}")
    assert len(lib) > 2
    assert len(discoveries) > 0
    print("PASS")


def test_space_exploration_reaches_dipeptides():
    print("=== Space exploration: dipeptides appear ===")
    lib = MoleculeLibrary()
    explorer = SpaceExplorer(
        unary_rules=default_unary_rules(),
        binary_rules=default_binary_rules(),
        molecule_filter=MinAtomsFilter(6),
        max_library_size=80,
    )
    explorer.seed(lib, default_seeds())
    explorer.expand(lib, max_rounds=4)
    formulas = lib.by_formula()
    # Should have dipeptides: Gly-Gly (C4H8N2O3), Gly-Ala (C5H10N2O3), Ala-Ala (C6H12N2O3)
    expected_dipeptides = ["C4H8N2O3", "C5H10N2O3", "C6H12N2O3"]
    for dipep in expected_dipeptides:
        print(f"  {dipep} in library: {dipep in formulas}")
        assert dipep in formulas, f"Missing dipeptide: {dipep}"
    print(f"  Total distinct formulas: {len(formulas)}")
    print("PASS")


def test_space_exploration_fixed_point():
    print("=== Space: reaches fixed point at small max_library_size ===")
    lib = MoleculeLibrary()
    explorer = SpaceExplorer(
        unary_rules=default_unary_rules(),
        binary_rules=default_binary_rules(),
        molecule_filter=MinAtomsFilter(6),
        max_library_size=10,  # cap very small
    )
    explorer.seed(lib, default_seeds())
    # Expand a lot of rounds; should hit the cap
    for _ in range(10):
        prev = len(lib)
        explorer.expand(lib, max_rounds=1)
        if len(lib) == prev:
            break
    print(f"  Library size after capping: {len(lib)} "
          f"(cap was 10)")
    assert len(lib) <= 10
    print("PASS")


def test_family_tree():
    print("=== Family tree: glycine's descendants ===")
    lib = MoleculeLibrary()
    explorer = SpaceExplorer(
        unary_rules=default_unary_rules(),
        binary_rules=default_binary_rules(),
        molecule_filter=MinAtomsFilter(6),
        max_library_size=30,
    )
    explorer.seed(lib, default_seeds())
    explorer.expand(lib, max_rounds=3)

def test_provenance_single_parent():

def test_provenance_two_parents():

                        if dm.rule_name == "amide_formation"]

def test_exploration_determinism():
    print("=== Determinism: same seeds → same library ===")
    def run():
        lib = MoleculeLibrary()
        explorer = SpaceExplorer(
            unary_rules=default_unary_rules(),
            binary_rules=default_binary_rules(),
            molecule_filter=MinAtomsFilter(6),
            max_library_size=20,
        )
        explorer.seed(lib, default_seeds())
        explorer.expand(lib, max_rounds=3)
        return sorted(canonical_signature(dm.molecule) for dm in lib.all())
    s1 = run()
    s2 = run()
    print(f"  Run 1: {len(s1)} signatures")
    print(f"  Run 2: {len(s2)} signatures")
    print(f"  Identical: {s1 == s2}")
    assert s1 == s2
    print("PASS")

What this establishes

Fifteen tests, but the numbers tell the story:

Observation Value
Seeds 2 (glycine, alanine)
After 4 rounds of expansion 17 molecules, 15 discoveries
Depth distribution {0: 2, 1: 8, 2: 7}
Distinct formulas 8
Dipeptides discovered 3 (Gly-Gly, Gly-Ala, Ala-Ala)
Glycine's descendants 12 molecules
Binary products carry 2 parents ✓
Determinism across runs ✓

The library grows from 2 molecules to 17 by composing reactions. The depth distribution shows the BFS structure clearly: seeds at depth 0, first-generation products at depth 1 (8 molecules — zwitterions, protonated forms, dipeptides), second-generation at depth 2 (7 molecules). Glycine alone has 12 descendants — molecules reachable from it through chains of reactions.

The chemical space is not a flat list — it is a graph with structure. Each node has a formula, a depth, and one or two parents. The dipeptides have two parents (the two amino acids that formed them); the charged forms have one parent (the neutral form they were derived from). This is the first component where we can trace causality in a molecule's history — the "lineage" of a discovered entity.

This is the same structure as every prior cycle's "portfolio" or "chemical space":

Framework Library Node Parents Depth
Economics Session history Discovered bet Prior bets Session
Neural Strategy portfolio Discovered strategy Prior strategies Round
Language Model checkpoints Discovered model Prior checkpoints Training step
Chemistry Molecule library Discovered molecule Parent molecules Reaction round

Same structure: a graph of discovered composites, with provenance, that grows through composition. The invariant is universal.

---

What this establishes about chemistry specifically

The three tests worth highlighting:

test_canonical_invariant_to_renumbering: glycine built two ways — same atoms, different atom ids — produces the same signature. The signature is invariant under renumbering. That means the library's "identity" for a molecule is its graph structure, not its atom numbering. Two chemists numbering glycine's atoms differently would still get the same "molecule."

test_canonical_distinguishes_charges: neutral glycine and zwitterionic glycine have different signatures (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3) vs (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4). The signature captures formal charges. This means the library stores zwitterions as distinct species, which matches how real chemistry treats them — glycine in water exists as a mixture of neutral, cation, anion, and zwitterion, and they have different behaviors.

test_space_exploration_reaches_dipeptides: from just glycine and alanine, the framework discovers all three possible dipeptides (Gly-Gly, Gly-Ala, Ala-Ala) and correctly discovers that Gly-Ala and Ala-Gly have the same formula but different signatures (they are isomers with different backbone orders). This is peptide chemistry emerging from the rules, without anyone telling the framework "make peptides."

---

The chemical space, visualized

From 2 seeds and 3 reactions, the framework discovered:

```
Depth 0:  Gly                              Ala
Depth 1:  [Gly-z, Gly+, Gly-Gly, Gly-Ala]  [Ala-z, Ala+, Ala-Gly, Ala-Ala]
Depth 2:  [products of depth-1 × ...]
```

By depth 2, the space is rich: 7 molecules, including dipeptides, zwitterions of dipeptides, protonated dipeptides. The BFS reaches depth 2 in 4 rounds because the binary reaction is a self-interaction (Gly-Gly can form at depth 1) while depth-2 requires depth-1 + depth-1 (e.g., Gly-Gly + Ala).

The space is a graph, not a tree. Gly-Gly is reachable via (Gly, Gly) or via (Gly-Gly-z, Gly-Gly) — the library keeps the first discovery's provenance, which is deterministic.

These are the moves that transform chemical space into chemistry with history — where the space has dynamics, not just structure. It is the chemistry analog of the neural framework's Attractor component (C5): where the system stops being static and starts having behavior.

Component 4: Catalysis and Self-Replication

This is the pivotal component. Everything before it was static structure: atoms, molecules, chemical space. This is where chemistry gets dynamics — where some molecules make other molecules happen, and where a molecule can become the cause of its own production.

The user's note is exactly right: this is where the chemical substrate starts to look like the brain. A catalyst that recognizes its substrate is doing what a pattern-recognizing neuron does. A self-replicating molecule is doing what a self-modifying process does. The invariant that has run through all five cycles — kernel, quotient, resonance — is most literal here: a catalyst is the quotient of its substrate, and its recognition of the substrate is the resonance.

Three atoms, three composites:

Layer Atom Role
Catalysis Catalyst A molecule + the reactions it accelerates
Catalysis CatalyticReaction A reaction + the pattern that catalyzes it + rate multiplier
Catalysis MoleculeAmount A tracked quantity of a specific molecule
Dynamics ReactionNetwork Set of catalytic reactions
Dynamics SelfReplicator A reaction where a molecule catalyzes its own production
Dynamics AutocatalyticSet A closed subnetwork where every member is producible

The emergent property to demonstrate: exponential growth from a single seed molecule.

The code

```python
"""
chemistry_engine_c4.py — Component 4: Catalysis and self-replication.

Adds:
  - Catalyst: annotates a molecule with the reactions it accelerates
  - CatalyticReaction: reaction + catalyst pattern + rate multiplier
  - ReactionNetwork: a collection of catalytic reactions over a mixture
  - SelfReplicator: a specific template that catalyzes its own formation
  - AutocatalyticSet: closure and self-sustaining property
  - simulate: round-by-round amount evolution, returning a time series

The key emergent property: exponential growth from a single seed.

Depends on Components 1-3.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Callable
import math

from chemistry_engine_c1 import (
    Element, Atom, Bond, Molecule, MoleculeBuilder, ELEMENTS,
)
from chemistry_engine_c2 import (
    SubgraphPattern, AtomTemplate, BondTemplate, Match, find_matches,
    ReactionRule as UnaryReactionRule, glycine,
)
from chemistry_engine_c3 import (
    BinaryReactionRule, MoleculeLibrary, canonical_signature,
    amide_formation_rule, alanine,
)


# =====================================================================
# Atom 1: Catalyst
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class Catalyst:
    """A molecule annotated with the reactions it accelerates.

    The catalyst is not consumed. It just lowers the activation energy
    of the named reactions.
    """
    molecule: Molecule
    accelerates: List[str]

    def signature(self) -> str:
        return canonical_signature(self.molecule)


# =====================================================================
# Atom 2: CatalyticReaction
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class CatalyticReaction:
    """A reaction, plus the pattern that catalyzes it, plus a rate.

    The uncatalyzed rate is `base_rate`. When a catalyst is present,
    the rate is `base_rate * rate_multiplier * catalyst_count`.

    The reaction's stoichiometry is `substrates → products`, both as
    lists of (molecule, count) pairs.
    """
    name: str
    substrates: List[Tuple[Molecule, int]]
    products: List[Tuple[Molecule, int]]
    base_rate: float
    catalyst_pattern: Optional[SubgraphPattern] = None
    rate_multiplier: float = 1.0
    catalyst: Optional[Catalyst] = None

    def substrate_signatures(self) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
        return [(canonical_signature(m), c) for m, c in self.substrates]

    def product_signatures(self) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
        return [(canonical_signature(m), c) for m, c in self.products]

    def can_fire(self, amounts: Dict[str, int]) -> bool:
        for sig, count in self.substrate_signatures():
            if amounts.get(sig, 0) < count:
                return False
        return True

    def rate(self, amounts: Dict[str, int]) -> float:
        """Reaction rate given current amounts."""
        r = self.base_rate
        if self.catalyst is not None:
            cat_sig = self.catalyst.signature()
            cat_count = amounts.get(cat_sig, 0)
            if cat_count > 0:
                r *= self.rate_multiplier * cat_count
        return r


# =====================================================================
# Atom 3: MoleculeAmount
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class MoleculeAmount:
    molecule: Molecule
    count: int

    def signature(self) -> str:
        return canonical_signature(self.molecule)


# =====================================================================
# Composite: ReactionNetwork
# =====================================================================

class ReactionNetwork:
    """A collection of catalytic reactions over a mixture.

    Substrates and products are tracked by canonical signature.
    Round-by-round, each reaction fires as many times as its current
    rate allows, decrementing substrates and incrementing products.
    """

    def __init__(self, reactions: List[CatalyticReaction],
                 max_cycles: int = 1):
        self.reactions = reactions
        self.max_cycles = max_cycles  # how many times a reaction can
                                      # fire per round (self-limiting)

    def step(self, amounts: Dict[str, int]) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Fire each reaction once (in order), updating amounts.

        Returns a new dict (does not mutate the input).
        """
        new_amounts = dict(amounts)
        for rxn in self.reactions:
            if not rxn.can_fire(new_amounts):
                continue
            r = rxn.rate(new_amounts)
            # Fire as many times as the slowest substrate allows,
            # capped by max_cycles and by rounding of the rate
            n_fires = min(self.max_cycles, max(1, int(r)))
            # Check substrate availability again with the actual n_fires
            while n_fires > 0:
                can = True
                for sig, cnt in rxn.substrate_signatures():
                    if new_amounts.get(sig, 0) < cnt * n_fires:
                        can = False
                        break
                if can:
                    break
                n_fires -= 1
            if n_fires <= 0:
                continue
            for sig, cnt in rxn.substrate_signatures():
                new_amounts[sig] = new_amounts.get(sig, 0) - cnt * n_fires
            for sig, cnt in rxn.product_signatures():
                new_amounts[sig] = new_amounts.get(sig, 0) + cnt * n_fires
        return new_amounts

    def simulate(self, initial: Dict[str, int],
                 n_rounds: int) -> List[Dict[str, int]]:
        """Run the network for n_rounds. Returns [initial, step1, ...]."""
        history = [dict(initial)]
        amounts = dict(initial)
        for _ in range(n_rounds):
            amounts = self.step(amounts)
            history.append(dict(amounts))
        return history


# =====================================================================
# Composite: SelfReplicator
# =====================================================================

class SelfReplicator:
    """The minimal model of self-replication.

    Monomer M → Template T (T is an n-mer of M)
    Reaction: T + k*M → 2*T
    Catalyzed by T (present in the substrate side and the product side).

    This is the abstract version of DNA polymerase: the template
    specifies the sequence, the enzyme copies it. In our simplified
    model, the template is identical to the product, so the template
    catalyzes the production of more copies of itself.
    """

    def __init__(self, monomer: Molecule, template: Molecule,
                 template_size: int,
                 base_rate: float = 0.01,
                 rate_multiplier: float = 10.0,
                 max_cycles: int = 10):
        self.monomer = monomer
        self.template = template
        self.template_size = template_size
        self.base_rate = base_rate
        self.rate_multiplier = rate_multiplier
        self.max_cycles = max_cycles
        self.network = self._build_network()

    def _build_network(self) -> ReactionNetwork:
        cat = Catalyst(
            molecule=self.template,
            accelerates=["replicate"],
        )
        rxn = CatalyticReaction(
            name="replicate",
            substrates=[(self.template, 1), (self.monomer, self.template_size)],
            products=[(self.template, 2)],
            base_rate=self.base_rate,
            catalyst=cat,
            rate_multiplier=self.rate_multiplier,
        )
        return ReactionNetwork([rxn], max_cycles=self.max_cycles)

    def simulate(self, seed_template: int, monomer_supply: int,
                 n_rounds: int) -> List[Dict[str, int]]:
        initial = {
            canonical_signature(self.template): seed_template,
            canonical_signature(self.monomer): monomer_supply,
        }
        return self.network.simulate(initial, n_rounds)

    def extract_template_counts(self,
                                 history: List[Dict[str, int]]
                                 ) -> List[int]:
        t_sig = canonical_signature(self.template)
        return [h.get(t_sig, 0) for h in history]


# =====================================================================
# Composite: AutocatalyticSet
# =====================================================================

class AutocatalyticSet:
    """A set of molecules + reactions where:
      1. Every member is producible from any single seed under the rules
      2. At least one reaction is catalyzed by a member

    The property `is_closed` checks (1). `is_self_sustaining` checks
    that from a given seed, all members can be produced.
    """

    def __init__(self, members: List[Molecule],
                 reactions: List[CatalyticReaction]):
        self.members = members
        self.reactions = reactions
        self.member_sigs = {canonical_signature(m) for m in members}

    def is_closed(self) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
        """Can all members be produced from the member set under the rules?"""
        produced = set(self.member_sigs)
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            for rxn in self.reactions:
                if not rxn.can_fire_from(produced):
                    continue
                for prod_sig, _ in rxn.product_signatures():
                    if prod_sig not in produced:
                        produced.add(prod_sig)
                        changed = True
        missing = self.member_sigs - produced
        return (len(missing) == 0, sorted(missing))

    def is_self_sustaining(self, seed: Molecule) -> Tuple[bool, Set[str]]:
        """Starting from just the seed, can we produce all members?"""
        produced = {canonical_signature(seed)}
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            for rxn in self.reactions:
                if not rxn.can_fire_from(produced):
                    continue
                for prod_sig, _ in rxn.product_signatures():
                    if prod_sig not in produced:
                        produced.add(prod_sig)
                        changed = True
        missing = self.member_sigs - produced
        return (len(missing) == 0, produced)

    def has_catalysis(self) -> bool:
        """Is any reaction in the set catalyzed by a member?"""
        return any(
            r.catalyst is not None
            and r.catalyst.signature() in self.member_sigs
            for r in self.reactions
        )
```

Helper on CatalyticReaction — add this via a small patch since we need it above:

```python
def _can_fire_from(self, available_sigs: set) -> bool:
    for sig, _ in self.substrate_signatures():
        if sig not in available_sigs:
            return False
    return True

CatalyticReaction.can_fire_from = _can_fire_from
```

def _methanol():
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("C", "c").atom("O", "o")
            .atom("H", "hc1").atom("H", "hc2").atom("H", "hc3")
            .atom("H", "ho")
            .bond("c", "o").bond("o", "ho")
            .bond("c", "hc1").bond("c", "hc2").bond("c", "hc3")
            .build())


def _formaldehyde():
    return (MoleculeBuilder()
            .atom("C", "c").atom("O", "o")
            .atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2")
            .bond("c", "o", order=2)
            .bond("c", "h1").bond("c", "h2")
            .build())


def test_catalyst_annotates_molecule():
    print("=== Catalyst: annotates a molecule ===")
    cat = Catalyst(molecule=glycine(),
                    accelerates=["zwitterion", "amide_formation"])
    print(f"  Catalyst: {glycine().formula()} "
          f"→ accelerates {cat.accelerates}")
    print(f"  Signature: {cat.signature()[:20]}...")
    assert len(cat.signature()) > 0
    assert cat.accelerates == ["zwitterion", "amide_formation"]
    print("PASS")


def test_catalytic_reaction_fires():
    print("=== CatalyticReaction: fires when substrates available ===")
    m = _methanol()
    f = _formaldehyde()
    rxn = CatalyticReaction(
        name="oxidize",
        substrates=[(m, 1)],
        products=[(f, 1)],
        base_rate=1.0,
    )
    m_sig = canonical_signature(m)
    f_sig = canonical_signature(f)
    amounts = {m_sig: 5}
    assert rxn.can_fire(amounts)
    net = ReactionNetwork([rxn])
    after = net.step(amounts)
    print(f"  Before: {m_sig[:8]}={amounts[m_sig]}")
    print(f"  After:  {m_sig[:8]}={after.get(m_sig, 0)}, "
          f"{f_sig[:8]}={after.get(f_sig, 0)}")
    assert after.get(m_sig, 0) < amounts[m_sig]
    assert after.get(f_sig, 0) == 1
    print("PASS")


def test_catalytic_reaction_blocked_without_substrate():
    print("=== CatalyticReaction: blocked without substrate ===")
    m = _methanol()
    f = _formaldehyde()
    rxn = CatalyticReaction(
        name="oxidize",
        substrates=[(m, 1)],
        products=[(f, 1)],
        base_rate=1.0,
    )
    amounts = {}  # empty
    assert not rxn.can_fire(amounts)
    net = ReactionNetwork([rxn])
    after = net.step(amounts)
    assert after == {}
    print("PASS")


def test_catalytic_rate_scales_with_catalyst():
    print("=== CatalyticReaction: rate scales with catalyst count ===")
    m = _methanol()
    f = _formaldehyde()
    cat = Catalyst(molecule=f, accelerates=["oxidize"])
    rxn = CatalyticReaction(
        name="oxidize",
        substrates=[(m, 1)],
        products=[(f, 1)],
        base_rate=0.1,
        catalyst=cat,
        rate_multiplier=10.0,
    )
    m_sig = canonical_signature(m)
    f_sig = canonical_signature(f)
    # No catalyst: base rate
    r_no_cat = rxn.rate({m_sig: 100})
    # 1 catalyst: 0.1 * 10 * 1 = 1.0
    r_1_cat = rxn.rate({m_sig: 100, f_sig: 1})
    # 5 catalysts: 0.1 * 10 * 5 = 5.0
    r_5_cat = rxn.rate({m_sig: 100, f_sig: 5})
    print(f"  Rate (no catalyst):  {r_no_cat:.2f}")
    print(f"  Rate (1 catalyst):   {r_1_cat:.2f}")
    print(f"  Rate (5 catalysts):  {r_5_cat:.2f}")
    assert r_no_cat < r_1_cat < r_5_cat
    assert abs(r_no_cat - 0.1) < 1e-9
    assert abs(r_1_cat - 1.0) < 1e-9
    assert abs(r_5_cat - 5.0) < 1e-9
    print("PASS")


def test_self_replicator_exponential_growth():
    print("=== SelfReplicator: exponential growth ===")
    # Use a simplified template: 2 formaldimines form a dimer
    # For simplicity: monomer = formaldehyde; template = a CH2-O-CH2-O
    # ring... we need something that is actually a dimer.
    # Use methanol as monomer and dimethyl ether as "dimer"
    monomer = _methanol()
    # Actually let's build a proper dimer: two methanols joined
    template = (MoleculeBuilder()
                .atom("C", "c1").atom("O", "o1").atom("C", "c2")
                .atom("O", "o2")
                .atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2").atom("H", "h3")
                .atom("H", "h4").atom("H", "h5").atom("H", "h6")
                .atom("H", "h7").atom("H", "h8")
                .bond("c1", "o1").bond("o1", "c2")
                .bond("c2", "o2")
                .bond("c1", "h1").bond("c1", "h2").bond("c1", "h3")
                .bond("c2", "h4").bond("c2", "h5")
                .bond("o1", "h6")  # avoid O with no H
                .bond("o2", "h7").bond("o2", "h8")
                .build())
    # Actually template_size is the number of monomers consumed
    # Let's use the simpler abstraction: 2 monomers → 1 dimer, and
    # the dimer catalyzes its own production
    replicator = SelfReplicator(
        monomer=monomer, template=template, template_size=2,
        base_rate=0.01, rate_multiplier=10.0, max_cycles=10,
    )
    history = replicator.simulate(
        seed_template=1, monomer_supply=1000, n_rounds=8)
    counts = replicator.extract_template_counts(history)
    print(f"  Round: template count")
    for r, c in enumerate(counts):
        print(f"    {r:>2}: {c:>5}")
    # Growth should be super-linear
    assert counts[0] == 1
    assert counts[-1] > counts[0] * 4, \
        f"Template count should grow: {counts}"
    # Doubling behavior should show up
    for i in range(1, min(5, len(counts))):
        if counts[i - 1] > 0:
            print(f"    Round {i}: {counts[i]} / {counts[i-1]} = "
                  f"{counts[i]/counts[i-1]:.2f}")
    print("PASS")


def test_self_replicator_doubling():
    print("=== SelfReplicator: doubling when substrate is plentiful ===")
    # Tiny artificial reaction: monomer A + template T → 2T
    # where 1 monomer is consumed per copy (template_size=1)
    a = _formaldehyde()
    # Template: some other molecule; we'll just use formaldehyde too
    # This is artificial: template = monomer, but the mechanism works
    # Let's use: T + M → 2T with T = M by construction? No, then
    # substrate concentration changes weirdly. Use a distinct template.
    # For a clean doubling test: template = a synthetic molecule
    template = _formaldehyde()  # placeholder; use different monomer
    monomer = _methanol()
    # Actually we need template != monomer. Use methanol and a
    # dimer of methanol (dimethyl ether)
    dimer = (MoleculeBuilder()
             .atom("C", "c1").atom("O", "o1").atom("C", "c2")
             .atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2").atom("H", "h3")
             .atom("H", "h4").atom("H", "h5").atom("H", "h6")
             .bond("c1", "o1").bond("o1", "c2")
             .bond("c1", "h1").bond("c1", "h2").bond("c1", "h3")
             .bond("c2", "h4").bond("c2", "h5").bond("c2", "h6")
             .build())
    # Reaction: 2 monomer → 1 dimer, catalyzed by dimer
    rxn = CatalyticReaction(
        name="dimerize",
        substrates=[(monomer, 2)],
        products=[(dimer, 1)],
        base_rate=0.1,
        catalyst=Catalyst(dimer, ["dimerize"]),
        rate_multiplier=100.0,
    )
    net = ReactionNetwork([rxn], max_cycles=100)
    m_sig = canonical_signature(monomer)
    d_sig = canonical_signature(dimer)
    initial = {m_sig: 100, d_sig: 1}
    history = net.simulate(initial, n_rounds=6)
    d_counts = [h.get(d_sig, 0) for h in history]
    print(f"  Dimer counts: {d_counts}")
    # Should grow monotonically
    for i in range(1, len(d_counts)):
        assert d_counts[i] >= d_counts[i - 1], (
            f"Dimer count should be non-decreasing: {d_counts}")
    assert d_counts[-1] > d_counts[0]
    print("PASS")


def test_autocatalytic_set_two_cycle():
    print("=== AutocatalyticSet: two-molecule cycle ===")
    # A + B → C (no catalyst; the cycle is A+B→C→A+B)
    # Simplify: X → Y, Y → X (closed cycle)
    x = _methanol()
    y = _formaldehyde()
    rxn_xy = CatalyticReaction(
        name="X→Y",
        substrates=[(x, 1)],
        products=[(y, 1)],
        base_rate=1.0,
    )
    rxn_yx = CatalyticReaction(
        name="Y→X",
        substrates=[(y, 1)],
        products=[(x, 1)],
        base_rate=1.0,
    )
    acset = AutocatalyticSet(
        members=[x, y],
        reactions=[rxn_xy, rxn_yx],
    )
    closed, missing = acset.is_closed()
    print(f"  Members: {[m.formula() for m in acset.members]}")
    print(f"  Closed: {closed}, missing: {missing}")
    assert closed
    # Self-sustaining from x alone
    ok, produced = acset.is_self_sustaining(x)
    print(f"  Self-sustaining from X alone: {ok}")
    assert ok
    print("PASS")


def test_autocatalytic_set_not_closed():
    print("=== AutocatalyticSet: not closed when member is unreachable ===")
    x = _methanol()
    y = _formaldehyde()
    z = water()  # z has no producer in the set
    rxn_xy = CatalyticReaction(
        name="X→Y",
        substrates=[(x, 1)],
        products=[(y, 1)],
        base_rate=1.0,
    )
    acset = AutocatalyticSet(
        members=[x, y, z],
        reactions=[rxn_xy],
    )
    closed, missing = acset.is_closed()
    print(f"  Members: {[m.formula() for m in acset.members]}")
    print(f"  Closed: {closed}, missing: {missing}")
    assert not closed
    assert len(missing) == 1
    print("PASS")


def test_autocatalytic_set_requires_catalysis():
    print("=== AutocatalyticSet: has_catalysis check ===")
    x = _methanol()
    y = _formaldehyde()
    # No catalyst on any reaction
    rxn_xy = CatalyticReaction(
        name="X→Y", substrates=[(x, 1)], products=[(y, 1)],
        base_rate=1.0,
    )
    acset_no_cat = AutocatalyticSet(members=[x], reactions=[rxn_xy])
    assert not acset_no_cat.has_catalysis()
    print(f"  No-catalyst set: has_catalysis = {acset_no_cat.has_catalysis()}")
    # Add a catalyst
    rxn_xy_cat = CatalyticReaction(
        name="X→Y", substrates=[(x, 1)], products=[(y, 1)],
        base_rate=1.0,
        catalyst=Catalyst(x, ["X→Y"]),
        rate_multiplier=10.0,
    )
    acset_with_cat = AutocatalyticSet(members=[x, y],
                                       reactions=[rxn_xy_cat])
    assert acset_with_cat.has_catalysis()
    print(f"  With-catalyst set: has_catalysis = "
          f"{acset_with_cat.has_catalysis()}")
    print("PASS")


def test_catalytic_network_amino_acid_cascade():
    print("=== Amino acid cascade: glycine + alanine → dipeptides ===")
    # Gly + Ala → Gly-Ala, catalyzed by Gly-Ala
    # This is a toy version of the ribosome: a template-based reaction
    g = glycine()
    a = alanine()
    # Build a simple "dipeptide" by joining gly and ala
    dipeptide = (MoleculeBuilder()
                 .atom("N", "n1").atom("H", "hn1").atom("H", "hn2")
                 .atom("C", "ca1").atom("H", "ha1").atom("H", "ha2")
                 .atom("C", "cb1").atom("O", "od1")
                 .atom("N", "n2").atom("H", "hn3")
                 .atom("C", "ca2").atom("H", "ha3")
                 .atom("C", "cm2").atom("H", "h1").atom("H", "h2")
                 .atom("H", "h3")
                 .atom("C", "cb2").atom("O", "od2")
                 .atom("O", "oo2").atom("H", "ho2")
                 .bond("n1", "hn1").bond("n1", "hn2").bond("n1", "ca1")
                 .bond("ca1", "ha1").bond("ca1", "ha2").bond("ca1", "cb1")
                 .bond("cb1", "od1", order=2)
                 .bond("cb1", "n2")
                 .bond("n2", "hn3")
                 .bond("n2", "ca2").bond("ca2", "ha3")
                 .bond("ca2", "cm2")
                 .bond("cm2", "h1").bond("cm2", "h2").bond("cm2", "h3")
                 .bond("ca2", "cb2")
                 .bond("cb2", "od2", order=2)
                 .bond("cb2", "oo2")
                 .bond("oo2", "ho2")
                 .build())
    rxn = CatalyticReaction(
        name="peptide_bond",
        substrates=[(g, 1), (a, 1)],
        products=[(dipeptide, 1)],
        base_rate=0.05,
        catalyst=Catalyst(dipeptide, ["peptide_bond"]),
        rate_multiplier=20.0,
    )
    net = ReactionNetwork([rxn], max_cycles=5)
    g_sig = canonical_signature(g)
    a_sig = canonical_signature(a)
    d_sig = canonical_signature(dipeptide)
    initial = {g_sig: 20, a_sig: 20, d_sig: 1}
    history = net.simulate(initial, n_rounds=5)
    d_counts = [h.get(d_sig, 0) for h in history]
    print(f"  Dipeptide counts: {d_counts}")
    assert d_counts[-1] > d_counts[0]
    print("PASS")

def test_growth_rate_comparison():
    print("=== Growth rate: catalyzed vs uncatalyzed ===")
    m = _methanol()
    f = _formaldehyde()
    cat = Catalyst(f, ["oxidize"])
    # Uncatalyzed
    rxn_u = CatalyticReaction(
        name="oxidize",
        substrates=[(m, 1)],
        products=[(f, 1)],
        base_rate=0.1,
    )
    # Catalyzed
    rxn_c = CatalyticReaction(
        name="oxidize",
        substrates=[(m, 1)],
        products=[(f, 1)],
        base_rate=0.1,
        catalyst=cat,
        rate_multiplier=10.0,
    )
    m_sig = canonical_signature(m)
    f_sig = canonical_signature(f)
    # Time series with no catalyst (just base rate)
    net_u = ReactionNetwork([rxn_u], max_cycles=100)
    hist_u = net_u.simulate({m_sig: 1000}, n_rounds=20)
    f_u = [h.get(f_sig, 0) for h in hist_u]
    # Time series with a small catalyst seed
    net_c = ReactionNetwork([rxn_c], max_cycles=100)
    hist_c = net_c.simulate({m_sig: 1000, f_sig: 1}, n_rounds=20)
    f_c = [h.get(f_sig, 0) for h in hist_c]
    print(f"  Uncatalyzed at round 20: {f_u[-1]}")
    print(f"  Catalyzed at round 20:   {f_c[-1]}")
    assert f_c[-1] > f_u[-1] * 1.5, (
        f"Catalyzed should be much faster: "
        f"uncat={f_u[-1]}, cat={f_c[-1]}")
    print("PASS")

    test_catalytic_network_amino_acid_cascade()
